364	thread cannot terminate while it holds stranded buffers, so the `pthread_join`
365	inside `AUDIOIOC_STOP` never returns. A symptom of the stall, not a cause.
366	
367	## b84–b87: WHO arms the mic, and WHEN the first capture happens
368	
369	**b84 removed the Recognize tab's voice arming** — it was a second, spoken
370	feeding path (`voice_apply()` → `velapaw_feeder_dispense()`) that contradicted
371	Model B (scheduled time **AND** recognised pet). Confirmed gone on hardware.
372	Since b84 the **meal dialog is the only thing that ever opens the audio
373	device**, and `voice_apply`, `voice_idle_text`, `g_voice_lbl`,
374	`g_voice_dismissed/hold/shown` are all deleted.
375	
376	That removal exposed two things Recognize had been providing **by accident**:
377	
378	1. **Readiness.** `vsched_tick()` will not prompt until `g_voice_ready`, set in
379	   exactly one place — after a capture **succeeds**. Standing on Recognize had
380	   always supplied that long before the dialog opened. b85 restores it with a
381	   boot warm-up (unarmed captures, result discarded).
382	2. **Unlimited retries.** b85 fed those warm-up failures into the shared
383	   `g_voice_consec`, and `VOICE_MAX_CAPFAIL 3` latches `g_voice_fail` and
384	   `return NULL` — **the worker thread exits and voice is dead for the boot.**
385	   b85 therefore burned the whole budget at boot and was *worse* than b83.
386	   **b86 gives the warm-up its own counter** (`g_voice_warmfail`) that never
387	   touches `g_voice_consec`, retrying forever with backoff (200 ms ×5, 2 s ×10,
388	   then 10 s). Armed/dialog captures keep the old budget.
389	
390	### What b86 proved: retrying within a boot CANNOT recover
391	
392	19 warm-up captures over 217 s, every one `-110`, hardware state **bit-identical
393	each time** and identical to b78/b79/b80:
394	
395	    rec 0/342  play 19/19      342 RX buffers in, none back; TX 19/19 fine
396	    desc 80000ff0              owner 1, length 0
397	    intraw 000000a0            INFIFO_FULL_WM + INFIFO_UDF_L1, RE-RAISED after
398	                               every kick's INT_CLR -> live starvation
399	    intena 00000002            IN_SUC_EOF enabled, never fires
400	    mickick 19 ok 0  resc 19  start 20
401	
402	TX completing 19/19 through the same GDMA proves the clock runs and the block's
403	EOF path works — **it is specifically the RX channel that never fills.**
404	
405	⚠️ **Two of my own readings here were WRONG — don't repeat them.**
406	`velapaw_i2s_rx_kick()` **does** drain `rx.act` (`while (!sq_empty(&rx.act))
407	sq_addfirst(sq_remlast(...), &rx.pend)`) and then `i2s_rxdma_start()` re-arms
408	one immediately — so `act 1 pend 1` after a kick is the kick **working**, not
409	failing. And **nothing in the UI ever closed the session in b83 either**:
410	`velapaw_mic_shutdown()` is called only from `velapaw_main.c`'s
411	`velapaw kws mic` CLI path, never from `ui_lvgl.c`.
412	
413	### The live hypothesis (b87): the FIRST capture decides, and b84 moved it
414	
415	`velapaw_mic_preopen()` opens one session at boot and **nothing ever closes
416	it**, so once that stream wedges every later capture inherits it — the kick
417	resets GDMA + I2S RX but never the ES8311.
418	
419	    b83 and earlier   first capture when the owner tapped Recognize, tens of
420	                      seconds in, board settled            -> 6 good boots
421	    b85 / b86         first capture at ~13.1 s -- mid TFLM model reads, camera
422	                      bring-up, the 5350 ms pre-open       -> 0 good boots
423	
424	**b87 holds unarmed captures until `VOICE_WARMUP_AT_MS` (30 s) after power-on**,
425	tested against `mono_ms()` (monotonic from boot). Armed captures are *not*
426	delayed. Falsifiable: the vlog shows either nothing (warm-up succeeded) or
427	`warmup FAILED -110 (#1)` at ~33 s — and if it fails at 33 s exactly as at 16 s,
428	**timing is not the variable** and the next move is rebuilding the session
429	(close both fds, re-open, which is the only thing that re-runs ES8311
430	configure). b80 removed that path because `mic_session_close()` hung, but that
431	predates b79's fix of the collect hang.
432	
433	Build chain, all esptool hash-verified on-chip:
434	`b83 288649a9` → `b84 a0860dee` → `b85 ec7c1d4d` → `b86 1666c029` →
435	`b87 95a383ed`. Console fix: [[velapaw-console-blocking]].
436	
437	## ✅ SOLVED: the `es8311 -22` boot spam is cosmetic — never chase it
438	
439	    es8311_getcoeff: MCLK = 4096000 and samplerate = 48000 not supported
440	    es8311_setsamplerate: Failed to set sample rate: -22
441	
442	The driver does it to itself. `es8311.c:2153` sets
443	`priv->samprate = ES8311_DEFAULT_SAMPRATE` (48000), then `:2191` calls
444	`es8311_setsamplerate()` during init while MCLK is 4096000 (= 256 × 16000).
445	`getcoeff(4096000, 48000)` has no table entry → `-22`. The real rate is
446	programmed later from `caps->ac_controls.hw[0]`, and `:1039` already calls
447	`es8311_reset()` *before* `:1046`'s `setsamplerate()`. **It appears in working
448	boots too**, so its presence in a failing log means nothing. This misled a
449	third-party analysis into proposing an ES8311 power-up clock race; that was
450	rejected on evidence.
451	
452	## Session shape
453	
454	Open, configure, `AUDIOIOC_START` **once**; each capture only enqueues and
455	collects. Between captures the session is running but idle. Free-running RX is
456	not an option: `mq_maxmsg = nbuffers + 8`, so with no reader the driver's
457	`mq_send` would drop buffer pointers. `mic_flush_mq()` before each re-arm.
458	
459	⚠️ **`apb->nbytes` is read by the driver *during* the enqueue ioctl** — the
460	caller sets it: record side `0`, playback side `nmaxbytes`. Zeroing it in a
461	shared helper silently sends a zero-length TX buffer → no clock → hang. TX
462	must stay primed; RX borrows BCLK/WS from TX (see [[velapaw-audio-bringup]]).
463	
464	⚠️ Do not conflate this with the falsified theory above. A **zero-length first**
465	TX buffer means `I2S_TX_START` is never set, so the clock never starts — real.
466	TX **draining after** a good buffer is harmless, because `TX_START` stays set
467	and `#16` cleared `TX_STOP_EN`.
468	
469	## Measurement, not ears
470	
471	`velapaw_mic_stats()` prints `peak N@index`, `rms`, `dc`, `rail` and an
472	8-segment peak profile. Reference at 30 dB, build 52, de-interleaved:
473	
474	    silence  rms  26  profile    87    82    87    68    55    67    56    60
475	    "yes"    rms 645  profile   447    90   107   100  4085  5019  1426  1724
476	    "no"     rms 791  profile  1949  5402  3534   596    74    66    87    94
477	
478	`MIC_TRACE` (default 0) prints one line per buffer with the `apb` pointer and
479	four samples — the check on both fixes at once: pointers must all be distinct,
480	`s` must alternate live/0. Turn it on for any future capture regression.
481	Do **not** read a full-scale spike at a fixed index as clipping — that is the
482	start-of-stream transient, see [[velapaw-audio-gain]].

---
name: velapaw-stale-libarch-trap
description: "Edits under nuttx/arch/ were silently dropped from every build — staging/libarch.a was never invalidated, so the linker kept using a Sept 3 object. Found 2026-09-22. Any arch-level conclusion from that window is void."
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: project
---

**Found 2026-09-22 while swapping the I2S driver.** `./build.sh` reported a
successful `LD: nuttx` and regenerated `nuttx.bin`, but **never recompiled the
source we had just replaced** — no `CC:` line, and the resulting image was
byte-identical in size to the previous one.

## The trap

Three things line up to hide it:

1. **NuttX builds arch objects FLAT.** The source is
   `arch/xtensa/src/esp32s3/esp32s3_i2s.c` (reached as `chip/esp32s3_i2s.c` via
   a symlink), but the object is `arch/xtensa/src/esp32s3_i2s.o` — one level up,
   *not* beside the `.c`. `Make.dep` and `.depend` live up there too. Deleting
   `*.o`/`Make.dep` in the `esp32s3/` subdir deletes nothing; the command
   succeeds silently.
2. **`staging/libarch.a` is treated as satisfied** regardless of arch sources.
   With the archive present, the top level relinks from it and never descends.
   A `.c` newer than the `.o` is not enough to trigger a rebuild.
3. **The link still succeeds**, because the stale member is in the archive. The
   only outward sign is a missing `CC:` line in a build log nobody reads
   closely, and an image whose size doesn't move.

On this tree `arch/xtensa/src/esp32s3_i2s.o` was dated **Sep 3 20:37** and
`staging/libarch.a` **Sep 3 20:41** — three weeks of builds linking a Sept 3
object. Sept 3 is the *floor* on how long, not necessarily the start.

## The fix — mandatory, not insurance

After ANY edit under `nuttx/arch/`:

```sh
cd ~/openvela/nuttx
rm -f arch/xtensa/src/<file>.o staging/libarch.a
cd ~/openvela && ./build.sh esp32s3-devkit:waveshare_lcd -j4
```

Other arch objects survive, so removing `libarch.a` forces a re-archive, not a
full arch rebuild — cheap. Removing `Make.dep` too costs a slower build while
it regenerates; harmless.

## How to PROVE a build actually took

Size alone is not enough — the Aug 10 swap produced an image of *exactly* the
same 1,561,976 B, padding having absorbed the delta. Two real tests:

- **Count differing bytes** between old and new images on Windows. A genuine
  rebuild differed in **88,921 bytes (5.7 %)**, spanning `0x9ac`–`0x17d4f9`. A
  timestamp-only difference is ~4 bytes (see [[velapaw-golden-baseline]]).
- **Plant a symbol that only the new code defines.** The link failing without
  it, or succeeding with it, is proof the object was recompiled.

## What this invalidates

**Any conclusion drawn from an `arch/` change between ~Sept 3 and Sept 22 was
drawn from an unchanged binary.** That covers I2S driver work in that window.
See [[velapaw-mic-capture]] for the stall verdict, which was re-established
with this trap accounted for.

Related stale-object traps, same family, different subtree:
[[velapaw-b82-camerafix-rebuild]] (`nuttx/boards/**/*.o`) and
[[velapaw-makefile-recipe]] (`.built`/`.depend`/`Make.dep` under apps).

So the "no spare GPIOs left" constraint doesn't bite, and the codec drops out of the capture path entirely. Two caveats, both real work rather than blockers: the ES8311's ADC output has to be properly disabled so it isn't fighting the mic on the shared DIN line, and patch #25's RX TDM slot map was tuned for the codec's two-slot behaviour — a single-channel I²S mic presents differently, so that needs retuning. The product story stays exactly as designed: you talk to the feeder.

**B. A replacement board.** Worth more than it sounds, because it isn't just a repair — it's the one experiment that cleanly splits "this particular board's hardware" from "the design." No software rollback can do that, which is why we burned a night proving only that software was innocent. If a fresh board's mic works, you're done and you also get back a board that hasn't been through three weeks of cable work and flash cycles. If a fresh board fails identically, that's a far more valuable result than anything else on this list: it would mean the fault is systemic and the two rollbacks were misleading us somehow. Given the hours already spent chasing this, a board is cheap.

**C. Move capture off the board and let the LLM do the parsing.** The board already has CDC-NCM networking and a working `ai_agent` with a live LLM and the schedule store wired up. Speak to a phone or the host, send the intent over the network, and `ai_agent` schedules the meal. This trades the "talk to the feeder" claim for something strictly more capable — free-form natural language ("feed Mochi at eight, skip his lunch") instead of a 14-word constrained decode — and it's mostly built already. The honest cost is that voice stops being on-device, which was part of the point.

**What I'd do:** B and the buffer-fed test path together. Order the board, and while it's in transit, build the stored-buffer input so the dialog logic is verifiable without a microphone. When the board arrives you'll know within ten minutes whether this was one bad codec, and you'll have a regression test either way. Keep A in reserve for if the new board also fails — at that point you'd want the codec out of the path regardless.

C I'd treat as an addition rather than a replacement. It's a good feature on its own merits, but swapping to it now would be deciding the on-device voice path is dead while two cheap tests that could revive it are still unrun.

11	 * The audio devices are opened, configured and STARTed once and then left
12	 * that way.  Each capture only enqueues buffers and collects them again.
13	 *

Found something concrete. Walking the config and the driver together:

**Ruled out (verified, not assumed):** MCLK is properly handled — `CONFIG_ESP32S3_I2S0_MCLK=y`, `MCLKPIN=12`, and the driver routes it at esp32s3_i2s.c:1687-1695 under the master-role branch. Pins match the verified schematic: BCLK 13, WS 15, DIN 14, DOUT **16** (so patch #22's same-pad loopback branch is correctly not taken). Role is master, patch #25's RX TDM slot map is present, patch #16 clears `TX_STOP_EN` so BCLK survives between captures.

**The finding — line 857 of config.golden:**

```
CONFIG_ES8311_SRC_MCLK=y
# CONFIG_ES8311_SRC_BCLK is not set
```

The codec's entire clock tree is hung off the MCLK pin, GPIO12. BCLK and WS are generated independently by the ESP32's TX clock module, so if MCLK isn't physically reaching the ES8311, **BCLK and WS keep toggling perfectly while the codec's ADC produces nothing** — the RX FIFO starves, the descriptor stays owner-set with length 0, and the capture times out at `-110`. That is exactly the signature we have, and it's the one failure mode where every clock you'd instinctively probe looks healthy.

Neither rollback could have caught this, because it's identical in all three images. That's the gap in the "software is exonerated" conclusion: both experiments varied the driver, and this is in the codec's clock-source selection.

**It has a one-symbol test that needs no logic analyzer.** Flip the codec to derive its clock from BCLK and GPIO12 drops out of the picture entirely:

```
# CONFIG_ES8311_SRC_MCLK is not set
CONFIG_ES8311_SRC_BCLK=y
```

If capture comes back, the fault is MCLK delivery — a trace, a solder joint, or the pad. Honest caveat on the reverse result: at 16 kHz × 16-bit × 2 slots, BCLK is 512 kHz, i.e. 32× LRCK, which sits at the very bottom of the ES8311's supported ratio table. It may simply not lock, so **a failure here proves nothing** — only a success is decisive. Worth it anyway, because it's one symbol.

Two warnings on doing it: edit the config directly and do **not** run `make olddefconfig` — it fails in this tree and you'd lose the hand-set symbols. And clear the stale objects first, including `staging/libarch.a`, or you'll flash an unchanged binary and misread the result.

**Also read this at boot.** The driver already prints its live pin map at `LOG_ERR`, esp32s3_i2s.c:1640:

```
VP: i2s pins din=14 dout=16 bclk=13 ws=15 mclk=12 role=...
```

That's ungated by the `DEBUG_AUDIO` symbols, so it should be in the boot log. It confirms the map at runtime rather than in the config, and `mclk=-1` there would settle this instantly.

One correction to the LA plan from earlier: probe **MCLK first**, then BCLK/WS, then DIN. I had DIN as the discriminator, but given `SRC_MCLK` the codec dies on MCLK loss while every other line looks correct — and the earlier register-level falsification of the clock theory tested register state, not what's actually on the pad.

2. **Key Technical Concepts**

   - **The `staging/libarch.a` stale-build trap**: NuttX builds arch objects **flat** in `arch/xtensa/src/` (not the `esp32s3/` chip subdir, which is a `chip` symlink). `staging/libarch.a` is never invalidated by a newer `.c`, so the link silently reuses a stale member. The generalization matters: `es8311.c` lives under `drivers/`, so **its** archive is `staging/libdrivers.a`.
   - **Byte-diff as the honest "did the build take" test**: identical file size ≠ identical content (the Aug 10 swap produced an image of exactly the same 1,561,976 B but differing in 88,921 bytes / 5.7%, spanning 0x9ac–0x17d4f9). A timestamp-only diff is ~4 bytes.
   - **ES8311 clock-source selection**: `CONFIG_ES8311_SRC_MCLK` vs `CONFIG_ES8311_SRC_BCLK`. With SRC_MCLK, the codec's whole clock tree depends on the MCLK pin; BCLK/WS are generated independently by the ESP32, so MCLK loss leaves every other line looking healthy while the ADC goes silent.
   - **I2S full-duplex clock sharing**: `I2S_SIG_LOOPBACK` set when `tx_en && rx_en`; VelaPaw patch #16 clears `I2S_TX_STOP_EN` (which defaults to 1 and would gate BCLK/WS off whenever the TX FIFO empties). Consequence: **RX is clocked via the TX path**, and the playback device must be opened, primed and STARTed for capture to work.
   - **GDMA/I2S register decode (verified, do not re-derive)**: `intraw 000000a0` = bits 5 + 7 = **INFIFO_FULL_WM + INFIFO_UDF_L1** = live RX FIFO starvation. `DSCR_EMPTY` is bit 4 and is clear in every dump. Here's what those two runs actually say — and it points somewhere different from where we were headed.

## The open sequence is fine; the DMA is the thing that's stuck

`preopen 0`, `reccfg 1 recstart 5 playstart 5 bufs 18 ret 0` — all 45 stages completed, both devices configured and STARTed, 18 buffers allocated, correct owner pid. `cfgskip 0` confirms the current (patch-#36) driver is the one linked, so the libarch.a swap took. Nothing in the setup path failed.

`rxconf 0008962c` decodes consistently with intent: RX_START set, TDM/Philips mode, mono, and RX in internal-slave mode taking its clock off the TX side — exactly the full-duplex arrangement patches #16/#25 build. `txconf 08089204` with `play 3/3 (tail/head)` balanced means the TX side is cycling normally. `rxeofn 4092` against a `4080 + 16` descriptor chain is the known 4092 quirk, not a new fault.

Now the part that reframes everything:

- **`desc 80000ff0`** — owner bit set, size 4080, **received length 0**. The DMA never wrote into that descriptor.
- **`intraw 000000a0`** = bit 5 + bit 7 = **INFIFO_FULL_WM** + INFIFO_UDF_L1.

INFIFO_FULL_WM can only assert if the I2S RX module pushed bytes into the GDMA input FIFO. So data *reached the FIFO*, and the descriptor length stayed zero. That is a DMA engine that isn't draining — not a silent microphone.

This matters because of what a silent mic would look like instead: if BCLK/WS are running and the codec sends nothing, I2S RX still samples the DIN pad and you get **buffers full of zeros**, delivered normally. We're not getting zero-valued buffers; we're getting *no* buffers. `rec 1/55 (tail/head)` — 55 enqueued, 1 ever returned.

And `eof 1 match 1 miss 0`, `isr 1 noeof 0 last 00000002` (IN_SUC_EOF): exactly **one** completion fired, ever. One is more interesting than zero — it's probably the first warmup buffer (`MIC_WARMUP_BUFS 3`, and warmup bytes don't count toward `got`), which is why `got 0/32000` despite a real EOF. The path worked once and then stopped.

Three weeks unpowered also answers the cold-codec question: a genuine full power cycle, stale ES8311 register state gone, identical failure. **That hypothesis is dead.** So is MCLK-as-prime-suspect, at least as the first thing to chase — a dead MCLK doesn't fill an RX FIFO.

## The read that settles it is already on your console — free, no rebuild

The driver prints five `VP: RXDUMP` lines through ungated `syslog(LOG_ERR, ...)`, once per boot, on the first RX start (HPWORK thread, [esp32s3_i2s.c:1289-1342](D:/openVela/velapaw-snapshots/2026-08-10-b82-camerafix/src/nuttx/arch/esp32s3_i2s.c#L1289-L1342)). They were printing during both of those runs — you just pasted the probe block and not the scrollback around it.

They give exactly what's missing:

- **`perisel=`** — whether this GDMA channel is actually bound to I2S0. The comment at 1317-1323 calls this out: if it isn't bound, the channel waits forever for a request that never comes.
- **`state=`** and **`fifo=`** (`DMA_IN_STATE` / `DMA_INFIFO_STATUS`) — where the engine is parked and how much is sitting in the FIFO.
- **`ch=`** — the channel number I2S got.
- **`i2sraw=`** — bit 0 RX_DONE, bit 2 RX_HUNG: has the I2S RX peripheral itself ever completed a frame.
- **`rxclkm/rxdiv/rxconf1`** — the RX clock tree.

So, same miniterm session, but capture everything:

Enter five or six times, then tap RESET on the board **with miniterm still attached**, let it boot, run `velapaw voice`, and paste the whole thing from the reset banner down. `Ctrl+]` to exit. I want three groups out of it:

1. `VP: i2s pins din= dout= bclk= ws= mclk= role=` (still never captured — `mclk=-1` there would be its own answer)
2. all five `VP: RXDUMP` lines
3. the `velapaw/voice probe:` block

## And one free experiment while you're in there

The camera takes its own GDMA channel through the same allocator — `g_camchan = esp32s3_dma_request(ESP32S3_DMA_PERIPH_LCDCAM, 0, 1, true)`, with `esp32s3_dma_init()` called again right before it at [esp32s3_st7789.c:677-678](D:/openVela/velapaw-snapshots/2026-08-10-b82-camerafix/src/nuttx/boards/esp32s3_st7789.c#L677-L678). Allocation is clean, so there's no hard-coded channel collision — but that re-init touches GDMA global state *after* I2S has configured its channel.

- **Run A:** fresh boot → `velapaw voice` immediately, never open Recognize.
- **Run B:** fresh boot → press Recognize once (camera runs) → `velapaw voice`.

If A captures and B fails, it's the camera/GDMA interaction and we have the bug. If both fail identically, the RXDUMP numbers tell us where the channel is stuck.

The `ES8311_SRC_MCLK` → `SRC_BCLK` flip is still a valid test, but it's now behind these two — it's a rebuild + reflash to test a codec-clock theory that a full FIFO argues against.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Reconnecting serial console + logger for the VelaPaw board.

The board's console is a firmware CDCACM device, so it disappears from the USB
bus on every reset and takes any attached terminal with it.  This reattaches the
instant the port comes back and appends everything to a log file, so a RESET tap
costs you nothing.

    python velapaw_capture.py [COM8] [velapaw_boot.log]

Type at the prompt as usual (lines are sent with CRLF).  Blank line = Enter.
Ctrl-C to stop.
"""

import sys
import threading
import time

import serial

PORT = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else "COM8"
LOGP = sys.argv[2] if len(sys.argv) > 2 else "velapaw_boot.log"

g_ser = None
g_stop = False


def stdin_pump():
    """Forward typed lines to whichever serial handle is currently open."""
    for line in sys.stdin:
        if g_stop:
            return
        ser = g_ser
        if ser is None:
            sys.stdout.write("[not attached -- line dropped]\n")
            continue
        try:
            ser.write(line.rstrip("\r\n").encode("utf-8", "replace") + b"\r\n")
        except Exception:
            sys.stdout.write("[write failed -- port dropped]\n")


def main():
    global g_ser, g_stop

    log = open(LOGP, "ab", buffering=0)
    threading.Thread(target=stdin_pump, daemon=True).start()

    sys.stdout.write("logging %s -> %s\n" % (PORT, LOGP))
    sys.stdout.write("waiting for port; RESET taps are safe (Ctrl-C to stop)\n")

    attached = False
    try:
        while True:
            try:
                ser = serial.Serial(PORT, 115200, timeout=0.2)
            except Exception:
                if attached:
                    sys.stdout.write("\n--- port gone, waiting ---\n")
                    attached = False
                time.sleep(0.05)
                continue

            g_ser = ser
            attached = True
            stamp = time.strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S")
            banner = "\n--- attached %s %s ---\n" % (PORT, stamp)
            log.write(banner.encode())
            sys.stdout.write(banner)
            sys.stdout.flush()

            try:
                while True:
                    data = ser.read(4096)
                    if data:
                        log.write(data)
                        sys.stdout.write(data.decode("utf-8", "replace"))
                        sys.stdout.flush()
            except Exception:
                pass
            finally:
                g_ser = None
                try:
                    ser.close()
                except Exception:
                    pass
    except KeyboardInterrupt:
        g_stop = True
        sys.stdout.write("\nstopped; log is %s\n" % LOGP)
    finally:
        log.close()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

Two corrections to what I told you, both from this log.

## My FIFO reading doesn't hold

Look at the first `velapaw voice` of the second boot — `caps 0`, `mic fail none recorded`, nothing has been attempted yet:

```
i2s eof 0 match 0 miss 0 empty 0  start 1 busy 1
i2s desc 80000ff0 80000010 ...
i2s intraw 000000a0 intena 00000002 inlink 001ab284
```

`intraw 000000a0` and `desc …length 0` are **already there before a single capture runs**. They're the steady state of preopen's arm-and-start sequence, not a trace of audio arriving and going undrained. So the "the FIFO filled and the DMA didn't empty it" inference is out — that was the load-bearing step in last message's reframe, and it doesn't survive this boot.

And `eof 0` here, after a capture that failed the same way, retracts the other half: last session's `eof 1 match 1` was a one-off, not a reliable "the path completed once" signal.

What's left is decode-independent and solid: RX is started, one descriptor armed, **487 worker loops go by at idle and not one EOF fires**, and the descriptor is never written. Nothing arrives, and we still cannot say whether that's no data on DIN or a GDMA channel that was never bound to I2S0.

## Why the dump lines never appeared — I pointed you at the wrong binary

`VP: i2s pins` and `VP: RXDUMP` are from the **Aug 10 snapshot** driver (3,530 lines). What's flashed was built from the restored VM driver, md5 `720e4818…`, **3,857 lines** — a different version. We captured `[bringup] fb_register ret=0` and `[velapaw] autostart pid=5`, which straddle where both lines should have landed, so the likeliest explanation isn't late attachment: those diagnostics probably aren't in this build at all. The capture loop worked fine; I sent it after output that doesn't exist.

So before anything else, three greps against the authoritative tree — paste the output:

```sh
cd ~/openvela
grep -n "VP: i2s pins\|RXDUMP\|vp_dumped" nuttx/arch/xtensa/src/esp32s3/esp32s3_i2s.c
grep -n "intraw\|inlink\|cfgskip\|chst" nuttx/arch/xtensa/src/esp32s3/esp32s3_i2s.c | head -40
grep -rn "intraw\|cfgskip" apps/examples/velapaw/ | head -20
```

The first says whether the dump exists in what you flashed. The other two show me the plumbing that carries `intraw/intena/inlink/cfgskip/chst` from driver to probe output, so I can write you an exact patch that adds `perisel`, `i2sraw`, `state`, `fifo`, `dscr` and `ch` to that same line. Those six are what discriminate "no clock/no data" from "channel not bound", and on the probe path they print on demand — no reset, no lost console.

## Separately: the board crashed at boot, right after dispensing food you didn't ask for

```
[feeder] dispensed 3 pocket(s) ~15g (1023 steps, asked 13g)
xtensa_user_panic: User Exception: EXCCAUSE=001d task: velapaw
```

`EXCCAUSE=0x1d` is 29, **StoreProhibited** — a write through a bad pointer. Note it's a *store*; the double-instance freeze you have on record is `0x1c` (28, LoadProhibited), so this is a different fault, not that one.

It killed pid 5 on the first boot and didn't recur on the second — and the second boot has no `[feeder]` line either. That correlation reads as a once-per-day catch-up: the stepper actually turned 1023 steps and delivered ~15 g, then the post-dispense bookkeeping stored through something invalid. The trigger is almost certainly the clock anchor — the boot seed is a floor pinned to the build date, today is 2026-10-11, so every scheduled meal looks long overdue the moment it boots.

Two things follow, and neither is mic work:

- The feeder is actuating unprompted on power-up. You'd deferred feeder work, so I'm not touching it — but you should know it moves on its own at boot, with food in the hopper, before you next power the board.
- Any boot where the catch-up path fires takes velapaw's PID 5 down with it. That's worth a stack trace; if you want it, I'd capture it before the i2s patch, since a crashing autostart will confound every probe reading that comes after it.

120	**STEP 7 EVIDENCE CAPTURED 2026-09-04** (`velapaw-snapshots\2026-09-04-ai-agent-toolcut\proactive_capture_raw.log`): 28 min of silence, then the 30-min timer fired **unattended** and ran the full chain — `HEARTBEAT.md` (281 B) → `skills/velapaw-feeding-digest.md` (1084 B) → `velapaw/status.md` (476 B) → `velapaw/feed_log.md` (241 B) → a per-pet assessment that flagged **bob at 33% of baseline appetite, below the skill's own 50% threshold**, while passing jay at 68%. 4 iterations, 7 s, request starting at **8,975 B** on a truly empty session. 122	**THE SESSION FILE PERSISTS ACROSS REBOOT AND MAKES FIRINGS HOLLOW.** `session_mgr.c:59` writes `/data/ai_agent/sessions/tg_<chat_id>.jsonl` to littlefs and replays it, so **a reboot does NOT give a clean agent**. 124	**This is a product bug, not just an evidence problem:** a pet fed at 14:00 with the heartbeat firing at 14:30 gets answered from pre-14:00 history and the feeding is missed. 126	**Correction to the growth note below:** it is bounded, not unbounded — `AGENT_SESSION_MAX_MSGS` is 20 (`agent_config.h:201`) and `session_mgr.c:159` truncates at 2×that, so the request plateaus around the observed 18.5 KB rather than climbing forever.

129	
130	**Remaining risk — the request grows with session history and eats the headroom.** First-call body across 8 consecutive firings: 11,960 → 12,260 → 12,573 → 13,511 → 14,412 → 14,830 → 15,162 → 15,444, i.e. **~500 B per firing, monotonic**; within a single firing it also climbs per react-loop iteration (firing 8 hit **18,483 B** by iteration 3, nearly the old 19,391). 132	Details: `[tools] Tools JSON built (36 builtin + 0 providers)` — **9,946 B of every request was tool schemas**, and 20 of the 36 are irrelevant to a pet feeder (wearable sensors, Feishu, music ×8, quickapp). 134	The retry loop itself IS hardware-verified (2026-09-04): `HTTP call failed in 90s (attempt 1/3)` → `retry 1/2 after 2s` → `attempt 2/3` → `retry 2/2 after 4s` → `attempt 3/3`, correct backoff. First hard evidence it runs at all.
135	
136	**`heartbeat_trigger` requires the `vela>` prompt and `ai_agent &` does NOT give you one.** With `&`, nsh keeps the console and every trigger returns `nsh: heartbeat_trigger: command not found` / `spawnp_ret=-38 builtin_index=-2`. **Park nsh in `sleep 900` to hand stdin to the agent's REPL** — that is what the `sleep 600` in the standard repro pattern is actually for; it is load-bearing, not a delay. 137	
138	**Header-only edits do not recompile dependents in this tree** (same trap as [[velapaw-makefile-recipe]]): `agent_config.h`'s interval change built cleanly but `heartbeat.c` kept the old constant, and the board logged `interval: 180s` while the source said 30 min. 142	**Heartbeat firings must not replay session history — fixed 2026-09-04, hardware-verified in steady state.** `session_mgr` persists every chat to `/data/ai_agent/sessions/tg_<chat_id>.jsonl` on littlefs, so **a reboot does NOT give you a clean agent** and `build_messages` replayed the previous firing's answer into the next one. Safe because empty → `cJSON_Parse` returns NULL → the existing `if (!messages) messages = cJSON_CreateArray()` path, the same one a first-ever boot takes.
143	
144	**Before suppressing history replay, check where tool results live.** `session_append` is called only twice (user msg + final answer, once per message) and `build_messages` runs **once per message, before `run_react_loop`** — the react loop grows its own in-memory `messages` array (observed 8975 → 9599 → 11092 → 12405 B across 4 iterations). Nothing round-trips through the session file, so cutting replay cannot blind the loop to its own tool results. 145	
146	**The evidence discipline that caught it:** capture 1 (unprepared, old code) opened at **14,361 B** and did nothing; capture 2 proved the mechanism only because I hand-deleted the session file, which is a *prepared* result and weak evidence; capture 3 (unprepared, fixed) opened at **8,975 B — byte-identical to the cleared run** while `ls -l` in the same log showed `tg_heartbeat.jsonl` present at 843 B. Always log the pre-state you did **not** touch; a passing run with no proof of the starting condition proves nothing.
147	
148	**STEP 7 COMPLETE 2026-09-04 — both halves captured on hardware.** Proactive half: the steady-state unattended firing above. CLI half: `ask which of my pets should I be worried about today and what should I do` → `iters=3 tools=2 llm_ms=6830`, four tool executions (`read_file` skill → `get_current_time` → `read_file` status.md → `read_file` feed_log.md), bodies 8898 → 10643 → 11970, no cache replay, and an answer that independently reached the same verdict as the heartbeat: Jay fine at 68 % of baseline, **Bob flagged at 33 % (10 g vs a 30 g baseline), below the skill's 50 % threshold**, with four concrete actions. 150	**`ask` was silently truncating at seven words — `#define MAX_ARGS 8` in `nsh_commands.c`.** `cmd_ask` rejoins `argv[1..argc-1]`, and `tokenise()` stops at `max_argc`, so a 15-word question reached the model as `which of my pets should I be` and it correctly replied that the message looked garbled. The echo check is what cleared the wire — but the decisive evidence was a **cache hit on the second run** (`llm_ms=0`): `llm_cache` hashes the first 64 chars (`djb2_hash`, `LLM_CACHE_KEY_LEN`), so a hit proves both runs delivered byte-identical content and the loss was a fixed buffer, not the serial link. **A cache hit is a free byte-for-byte equality test between two runs — use it.** The slow-typing code was left in place but addressed a cause that wasn't there.
151	
152	**"Stale console history suppresses tool calls" — I RECORDED THIS AS CONFIRMED OFF ONE OBSERVATION AND IT DID NOT HOLD.** The original claim: same firmware, same question, 20 min apart, stale `tg_console.jsonl` → `iters=1 tools=0` and an answer that missed Bob; cleared → `iters=3 tools=2` and the right answer. **Two later control runs with stale history never reproduced `tools=0`** — both called tools and failed for an entirely different reason (a broken `list_dir`, below). 153	
154	**`list_dir` was broken two ways at once, and the shortcut turned that into a wrong answer delivered to the user — fixed 2026-09-04, hardware-verified.** (1) The prefix was matched against the *absolute* path (`/data/ai_agent/velapaw`) while the model passes a *relative* one (`velapaw`), so every entry was filtered out; worse, the `continue` ran **before** the recursive call, so non-matching directories were never descended into. (2) `list_dir` sat in the local-tool shortcut set in `agent_loop.c`, so its empty result **ended the turn and was handed to the user as the answer** — a user asking which pet to worry about literally received `(no files found)`. Fixes: match the prefix against **either** the relative or the absolute path (`strncmp(full_path,…) || strncmp(rel,…)`), always recurse, and drop `list_dir` from the shortcut set. Also added: no shortcut when tool output starts with `"Error: "` (the `tool_files.c` convention is `Error: …`/`OK: …` at every one of ~20 sites). **My own trap, worth repeating: I first replaced absolute matching with relative matching — fixing the case I had observed and breaking the case I hadn't. I considered accepting both while designing it and then didn't implement it.** Across three hardware runs the model used three different call shapes (`"velapaw"`, `"/data/ai_agent/"`, no prefix at all) — **a tool that only handles the spelling you happened to observe will look fixed and then fail**; the passing run used no prefix, so the both-forms branch is proven by code reading, not by that run.
155	
156	**Forcing a re-read beats trimming history.** Added to `build_messages` in `agent_loop.c`: when history is non-empty, append a mid-array `{"role":"system"}` message before the user turn saying device state may have changed, any earlier figure is stale, and to re-read the relevant files before answering about present state. Mid-array system messages are already used in this file (lines ~813, ~983) and DeepSeek accepts them. Guard is free: heartbeat blanks `history_json` → `cJSON_Parse` NULL → empty array → skipped. Result with stale history still on disk: `iters=3 tools=2`, both `read_file`s on the real files, answer opens *"Now I have the current feeding data"* and flags Bob correctly. **`AGENT_AI_AGENT_MAX_HISTORY` (10, `agent_config.h:108`) was NOT trimmed — it stays the fallback lever if this regresses.**
157	
158	**Cutting a tool leaves callers behind — the NL fast paths in `agent_loop.c` dispatched to five removed tools, fixed + hardware-verified 2026-09-04 (`cd2b4edd3baf27b25edae5db200ffe4a`).** `handle_nl_fast_path` runs *before* the LLM and returns its result as the final answer, so a shortcut pointing at an unregistered tool ends the turn with garbage. 160	2. **A hand-written music block** (~60 lines, `kw_play` → `music_search` → `music_play`). **The guard could not have saved this one** — on failure it `snprintf`s `"找到了 %s - %s，但播放失败: %s"`, i.e. a confident *non-empty* wrong sentence, or `strncpy`s the zeroed `search_result` into a 4096 B buffer. 161	3. **`inject_session_context` still told the model about `feishu_send_mention`/`feishu_chat_members`** in the system prompt of **every** request — dead bytes working against the request-size fix, plus an invitation to call tools that don't exist. Removed along with the `[mentioned_users: …]` paragraph (Feishu-only, and no Feishu channel is built).
162	Verified directly, not by inference: `ask play some music for my cat` → `NL fast path fired: NO`, one LLM round, `END status=ok`, and a real answer ("I don't have the ability to play music directly") that still knew Bob and Jay from session context. 164	**`Ethernet 2` can silently reroute board traffic into the VPN — and "0 % loss" does not mean the board answered.** A run that ended `END status=timeout llm_ms=480920` (exactly `AGENT_LLM_SOCKET_TIMEOUT_SEC`) was not a model problem: the board's USB Ethernet link was down, so `Get-NetIPInterface` showed `ConnectionState: Disconnected`, 192.168.137.1 sat at `AddressState: Tentative` (DAD never completed ⇒ unusable as a source ⇒ **all routes on that interface are skipped**), and Windows fell through to WireGuard's `128.0.0.0/1`. **My own false pass: `ping -n 2` reported `Received = 2, Lost = 0 (0% loss)` while every reply read `Reply from 10.234.0.0: Destination port unreachable` — ICMP errors from the tunnel. And there's the documented false pass, live: `0% loss` with replies from `192.168.137.1` (*host* unreachable) and `10.234.0.0` (the VPN tunnel). ARP for the board is `Incomplete`. That's just the board not having an address yet — `ifconfig eth0` is manual on every boot. Host half is ready; board half isn't up.

## Where the agent actually stands

Steps 5, 6 and 7 of the integration plan are complete and hardware-captured: `ask` returns real DeepSeek replies, the custom feeding-digest skill is live on littlefs and survives reset, the proactive heartbeat fires unattended and re-reads live device state (the enroll-a-pet-mid-run evidence), and the CLI half independently flagged Bob at 33% of baseline. Request size is down to ~9–12 KB after the tool cut, 8/8 clean firings.

So the agent is the part of this product that works.

**The one thing that's unverified:** the last agent-validated firmware is md5 `cd2b4edd3baf27b25edae5db200ffe4a`. What's on the board right now is a *newer* build — the one from the i2s driver restore, rebuilt with `libarch.a` cleared. The agent sources didn't change, but no agent run has ever touched this image. Before building anything new, that needs one confirming pass, or every later result is suspect.

Two confounders to know about going in:

- The boot crash we just saw (`EXCCAUSE=001d`, StoreProhibited) takes velapaw PID 5 down when the catch-up dispense fires. littlefs keeps `status.md` / `feed_log.md` / `history.bin`, so the agent can still read device state — but with velapaw dead there's no touch UI, so no enrolling pets mid-run for the demo script.
- `ask hello` is cache-poisoned from earlier sessions. Probe with something novel.

## Verification pass

Keep `velapaw_capture.py` running — it's as useful here as it was for the mic, since resets no longer cost you the console. At `nsh>`:

```
ifconfig eth0 192.168.137.2 netmask 255.255.255.0 gw 192.168.137.1
ifconfig
ai_agent &
```

Let the banner run out to `Heartbeat started (every N min)` — that line is also the cheapest anti-stale-flash check. Then, once it's quiet:

```
ask which pet has eaten least today and what should i do about it
```

Pass looks like: `[tools] Tools JSON built (16 builtin + 0 providers)` (16, not 36 — the tool cut), no `Cache hit, skipping LLM call`, one `REQ written`/`RESP hdr in` pair per iteration, and `END status=ok` with `iters=3 tools=2`. I'll re-ping from the host to confirm ARP goes `Reachable` once `ifconfig` has run.

## What I'd build on the agent

The feature the dead mic was blocking is **meal scheduling** — the spoken MEAL→HOUR→CONFIRM dialog. The agent can deliver that same feature without a microphone: a `set_meal_schedule` tool, so `ask schedule Jay's meals at 8am and 6pm` does what the voice dialog was going to do, driven from the CLI instead of speech. 11	The board gets internet via **Windows Internet Connection Sharing** on the
12	CDC-NCM link: share `Wi-Fi` (public) with `Ethernet 2` (private, the "VelaPaw
13	Composite" adapter). ICS then forces `192.168.137.1` onto `Ethernet 2` and
14	provides both NAT and a DNS proxy there. Board side:
15	
16	```
17	ifconfig eth0 192.168.137.2 netmask 255.255.255.0 gw 192.168.137.1
18	```
19	
20	**ICS overrides the adapter address.** The golden CDC-NCM config in
21	[[velapaw-cdcncm-networking]] is static `10.0.0.1`/`10.0.0.2`. Those two schemes
22	are mutually exclusive: enabling ICS replaces `10.0.0.1` with `192.168.137.1`,
23	and disabling it snaps the address back to the static `10.0.0.1`. So an
24	`Ethernet 2` sitting at `10.0.0.1` means ICS is **off**, not that something is
25	misconfigured. Use `10.0.0.x` when the board only needs to talk to the host, and
26	ICS/`192.168.137.x` when it needs the internet.
27	
28	**THE TRAP: `NlaSvc` (Network Location Awareness) stopped.** ICS can be flagged
29	enabled on both connections and still be completely dead — `SharedAccess`
30	stopped, nothing on UDP 53, so every board DNS query returns `-11` and mbedtls
31	returns `ret=0x52` (`MBEDTLS_ERR_NET_UNKNOWN_HOST`, no socket ever opened).
32	`NlaSvc` was `Stopped`/`Manual` on this machine, which is abnormal — it is a
33	subscriber to the COM+ network-configuration events ICS depends on. Symptom when
34	you try to (re)bind sharing:
35	
36	```
37	0x80040201  EVENT_E_ALL_SUBSCRIBERS_FAILED
38	```
39	
40	Fix: `Start-Service NlaSvc`, then restart `SharedAccess` so it re-subscribes.
41	Diagnose from the host with `Resolve-DnsName api.deepseek.com -Server 192.168.137.1`
42	— if that answers, ICS is genuinely live; if not, no amount of board-side work
43	will help.
44	
45	**`NlaSvc` is `Manual` by default and stops again on its own**, taking ICS down
46	with it days later — this recurred once already. `Set-Service NlaSvc
47	-StartupType Automatic` (needs elevation) is what makes the fix durable. Note a
48	normal Claude Code PowerShell session is **not elevated**: service and route
49	changes must go through `Start-Process ... -Verb RunAs` and a UAC prompt.
50	
51	**THE DEFINITIVE ICS LIVENESS TEST: does `SharedAccess` own any listeners?**
52	
53	```powershell
54	$svc = Get-CimInstance Win32_Service -Filter "Name='SharedAccess'"
55	Get-NetUDPEndpoint -OwningProcess $svc.ProcessId
56	```
57	
58	Zero listeners = the ICS **engine** never instantiated, even though the service
59	says `Running`, `ScopeAddress` is right, both connections report `shared=True`,
60	and *no error is logged anywhere*. NAT and the DNS proxy both come from that
61	engine, so when it is hollow the board gets no DNS **and** no forwarding. This
62	is a much sharper signal than any flag.
63	
64	**The `HNetCfg.HNetShare` COM API cannot usefully bind sharing here.** With
65	`NlaSvc` stopped, `EnableSharing(1)` on the private side throws `0x80040201`
66	(tried static and DHCP, both fail). With `NlaSvc` running, **both calls return
67	`ok` and still do nothing** — sharing reads back `True`/type 1 on `Ethernet 2`
68	and `True`/type 0 on `Wi-Fi`, `ScopeAddress` is correct, and `SharedAccess`
69	owns no listeners at all. The API sets flags without starting the engine.
70	**Use the GUI**: `ncpa.cpl` → Wi-Fi → Properties → **Sharing** tab → tick the
71	box → Home networking connection = `Ethernet 2` → OK. netshell takes a
72	different code path and actually instantiates it. If sharing is already flagged
73	on but hollow, **untick, OK, then re-tick** — a fresh tick over a phantom
74	binding is a no-op. Note the COM flag is unreliable in both directions
75	(`False` while ICS serves DNS, `True` while it does nothing) — **test function,
76	never state**.
77	
78	**Do NOT try to replace ICS with WinNAT.** `New-NetNat` exists and the `winnat`
79	service starts, but every call fails with `Invalid class` — the `MSFT_NetNat`
80	WMI provider ships with the Hyper-V platform feature, which is not installed.
81	**Enabling Hyper-V on this machine would be actively harmful**: the whole
82	openVela build environment is a VMware Workstation VM, and Hyper-V's hypervisor
83	takes ownership of VT-x and cripples or breaks VMware. Dead end — don't revisit.
84	
85	**Don't "clean up" existing sharing before re-binding.** Calling
86	`DisableSharing()` on connections that are already flagged shared is easy to do
87	as a "start from a known state" step and is a trap: if the re-enable then fails
88	(see above) you have destroyed a binding you cannot restore from the API, and
89	have to go through the GUI anyway.
90	
91	**Coexisting with the HotspotShield VPN — split-tunnel, don't disconnect it.**
92	The user needs the VPN up to reach claude.ai at all, so "turn the VPN off" is
93	not an available fix. Two distinct ways the tunnel breaks the board:
94	
95	- Its WireGuard adapter installs `0.0.0.0/1` + `128.0.0.0/1`, which beat Wi-Fi's
96	  `0.0.0.0/0` on prefix length before metric is consulted. **Raising the tunnel's
97	  interface metric does nothing** — only a more specific route wins.
98	- That adapter has `Forwarding=Disabled` (Wi-Fi and `Ethernet 2` are Enabled),

100	  forward them. The host's own browsing is unaffected because it is locally
101	  originated, not forwarded — which is why the host works while the board dies.
102	- Its MTU is 1420 vs the board's 1500, silently truncating the agent's ~15KB
103	  POST. Small handshake packets survive, so TLS completes and only the big
104	  request fails (`Failed to parse HTTP status from: ` with an empty body).

107	the Wi-Fi gateway, in the `ActiveStore` so a reboot clears them.

111	             -NextHop <wifi-gw> -RouteMetric 1 -PolicyStore ActiveStore

115	and `8.8.4.4` if the board uses them as resolvers. Verify with a DF-set ping —
116	`ping -f -l 1472 3.173.21.63` must reply (through the tunnel it is 100% loss)

118	`scratchpad/split_tunnel.ps1`.

125	host→board `ping 192.168.137.2` succeeds while board→host fails, and the host's

131	
132	Note the board's nsh in this build has **no `ping`** (`nsh: ping: command not
133	found`), so board-side reachability cannot be tested that way — use `net_test`
134	at the `vela>` prompt, which does DNS + TCP + TLS to `www.baidu.com` with no LLM
135	and no cache involvement.
136	
137	Once ICS actually serves DNS, the board's full path works end to end — DNS
138	resolves, `[vela_tls] Handshake OK: TLSv1.2 / TLS-ECDHE-RSA-WITH-AES-128-GCM-SHA256`,
139	and the request reaches DeepSeek. See

141	
142	**2026-09-03 — the working recipe, reproduced cleanly.** Order matters, because
143	*every* host-side network change (route add, `Set-NetConnectionProfile`, address
144	change) restarts `SharedAccess` and it comes back hollow. So:
145	
146	1. Do all host work first — `Ethernet 2` = `192.168.137.1/24` **Manual**,
147	   category **Private**, DHCP **off**, no stray APIPA; add the
148	   `3.173.21.63/32` (api.deepseek.com) route via **Wi-Fi** so the 15.7 KB POST
149	   gets a 1500-MTU path instead of the tunnel's 1420 (`New-NetRoute
150	   -PolicyStore PersistentStore` is rejected here — ActiveStore only, so it
151	   must be re-added after every ICS re-bind).
152	2. **Then** the `ncpa.cpl` untick/re-tick, last.
153	3. **Then** tap RESET and test the board, changing nothing on the host in
154	   between.
155	
156	Verified serving state — this exact listener set is the pass criterion:
157	`SharedAccess` owning `0.0.0.0:53`, `fe80::…%11:53`, `192.168.137.1:67`,
158	`192.168.137.1:68`. Result: `nslookup api.deepseek.com` → `Addr:
159	123.54.208.173`, `net_test` → `SUCCESS! HTTP Status: 200`, and `ask` got a real
160	DeepSeek response. Note the ICS proxy's answer for `api.deepseek.com`
161	(123.54.208.173) differs from the host's own (3.173.21.63) — both work.
162	
163	**A reflash does NOT knock ICS hollow** — worth knowing, because it looks like
164	it should. Flashing makes the board's USB composite device vanish and
165	re-enumerate, and `Ethernet 2` *is* that device; during the gap `Get-NetIPAddress
166	-InterfaceAlias 'Ethernet 2'` returns nothing. But `SharedAccess` keeps the same
167	pid and all four listeners throughout, and the adapter comes back at
168	`192.168.137.1/24 Manual` on its own. Verified 2026-09-03: flash → wait ~6 s →
169	listeners intact, COM8 back, board worked first try. So **check the listeners
170	before asking for another GUI toggle**; the toggle is only for genuinely hollow.
171	
172	**A host→board ping proves NOTHING about ICS — don't use it as the gate.**
173	2026-09-04: `Ethernet 2` was found `Disconnected` (0 bps) with `SharedAccess`
174	owning 0 listeners. Tempting read: the missing listeners are just a *symptom*
175	of the down link, since ICS binds `192.168.137.1:67/68` on the private side.
176	Half right. A RESET tap re-enumerated CDC-NCM and `Ethernet 2` came back
177	**Up** with host→board ping **4/4, 0% loss** — and the listener count stayed
178	**0**, so the ask still died on three rounds of
179	`dns_recv_response: ERROR: recv failed: -11` (90 s burned) then
180	`net_connect api.deepseek.com:443 ret=0x52`. **The link and the engine fail
181	independently**: a reset fixes the link, only the `ncpa.cpl` untick/re-tick
182	fixes the engine. So a bring-up gate must require all three — ping **and**
183	listeners > 0 **and** an actual `Resolve-DnsName api.deepseek.com -Server
184	192.168.137.1` — or it green-lights a run that cannot succeed.
185	
186	**The Wi-Fi gateway here is `10.29.0.1`, which looks alarmingly like a VPN
187	address but is not.** `Get-NetRoute -DestinationPrefix '3.173.21.63/32'` showing
188	`ifIndex 21 / NextHop 10.29.0.1` is the *correct* split-tunnel route — ifIndex
189	21 is the Intel AX211 Wi-Fi adapter at MTU 1500, and the tunnel is ifIndex 45 at
190	1420. Confirm with `Find-NetRoute -RemoteIPAddress 3.173.21.63`: it should
191	report `InterfaceIndex 21` with a `10.29.x.x` *source* address. Don't "fix" this
192	route on sight.
193	
194	**Never route 8.8.8.8/8.8.4.4 outside the HotspotShield tunnel.** On this
195	mainland-China connection Google DNS is reachable *only* inside the tunnel;
196	adding /32 routes for them out Wi-Fi killed the host's own name resolution and

202	
203	**Once `ai_agent` is running, `vela>` owns the console and `nsh>` is
204	unreachable** — `ifconfig` there returns "Unknown command". Any interface or
205	resolver change must be issued *before* `ai_agent &`, which is also the order

/* Anything that changes the window rewrites both the machine copy and the
 * digest, so the agent never reads a stale status.md. */
static void vp_persist(void)
{
  vp_history_save();
  vp_status_write();
}

/****************************************************************************
 * Day stamping
 *
 * The window is an array whose last slot is "today", so something has to
 * move it.  Until now the only thing that did was the EV_NEXTDAY demo
 * button, which means a board left running past midnight kept adding to the
 * same slot for ever.  Over-reporting intake makes the feeder withhold real
 * meals, so this is the dangerous direction to get wrong.
 ****************************************************************************/

static long vp_days_from_civil(int y, unsigned m, unsigned d)
{
  /* Exact day number across month and year boundaries.  tm_yday alone is
   * not enough: 12-31 -> 01-01 has to be a delta of 1, not -364.
   */
  y -= m <= 2;
  long era = (y >= 0 ? y : y - 399) / 400;
  unsigned yoe = (unsigned)(y - era * 400);
  unsigned doy = (153 * (m + (m > 2 ? -3 : 9)) + 2) / 5 + d - 1;
  unsigned doe = yoe * 365 + yoe / 4 - yoe / 100 + doy;
  return era * 146097 + (long)doe - 719468;
}

static long vp_today_num(void)
{
  time_t now = time(NULL);
  struct tm tmv;

  /* Same sanity floor the feed log uses: an unset clock must never be
   * allowed to shift real history.
   */
  if (now < VP_TS_SANE)
    {
      return -1;
    }

  localtime_r(&now, &tmv);
  return vp_days_from_civil(tmv.tm_year + 1900, tmv.tm_mon + 1, tmv.tm_mday);
}

static void vp_shift_days(int n)
{
  if (n <= 0)
    {
      return;
    }

  if (n > DAYS)
    {
      n = DAYS;
    }

  for (int p = 0; p < VELAPAW_MAX_PETS; p++)
    {
      int d = 0;
      for (; d < DAYS - n; d++)
        {
          g_day_g[p][d] = g_day_g[p][d + n];
          g_day_m[p][d] = g_day_m[p][d + n];
        }

      for (; d < DAYS; d++)
        {
          g_day_g[p][d] = 0;
          g_day_m[p][d] = 0;
        }
    }
}

/* Reconcile the window with the wall clock.  Safe on every path that
 * touches the history -- it is a no-op within a single day.
 */
static void vp_sync_day(void)
{
  long today = vp_today_num();

  if (today < 0)
    {
      return;              /* clock unusable -- leave the window alone */
    }

  if (g_hist_day < 0)
    {
      /* First run, or a VP01 file: the data in the window is real, we just
       * never knew which day it belonged to.  Adopt today, do not shift.
       */
      g_hist_day = today;
      vp_history_save();
      return;
    }

  if (today <= g_hist_day)
    {
      /* Same day, or the clock jumped backwards -- which the build-date
       * boot anchor does on every cold start.  Never shift backwards: it
       * would drop real days off the front and zero slots that hold data.
       */
      return;
    }

  vp_shift_days((int)(today - g_hist_day));
  g_hist_day = today;
  vp_history_save();
}

int velapaw_store_init(void)
{
  memset(g_day_g, 0, sizeof(g_day_g));
  memset(g_day_m, 0, sizeof(g_day_m));
  for (int i = 0; i < VELAPAW_MAX_PETS; i++)
    {
      g_bcs[i] = -1;
    }

  vp_history_load();

  /* A board that has been off -- or simply running -- across midnight has
   * to shift before it reports anything.
   */
  vp_sync_day();

  /* Write the digest at startup too.  Without this, status.md does not exist
   * until the next feed, enroll or BCS update, so a freshly booted board
   * gives the agent's skill nothing to read. */
  vp_status_write();
  return 0;
}

int velapaw_store_log_feeding(const struct velapaw_feed_event *ev)
{
  if (ev == NULL || !valid(ev->pet_id))
    {
      return -1;
    }

  /* Bucket the event in the right day even if the board has been up since
   * before midnight.
   */
  vp_sync_day();

  g_day_g[ev->pet_id][TODAY] += ev->grams;
  g_day_m[ev->pet_id][TODAY] += 1;

  printf("    [store] event pet=%d grams=%d score=%.2f model=%s\n",

  vp_feedlog_append(ev);
  vp_persist();
  return 0;
}

{
  return valid(id) ? g_day_g[id][TODAY] : 0;
}

int velapaw_store_today_meals(velapaw_pet_id_t id)
{
  return valid(id) ? g_day_m[id][TODAY] : 0;
}

## The root cause, and it ties three oddities together

The feed log is strictly append-only, so file order *is* the order events were written. But the timestamps don't increase:

```
08:01 → 09:24 → 19:01 → 19:02 → 09:08 → 08:02 → 09:07 → 08:08 → 08:20 → 10:01 → 08:02 → 08:17
```

Time goes *backwards* repeatedly. The only way that happens on an append-only log is the clock resetting between writes — which is exactly what the build-date anchor floor does on every cold boot. The board starts each boot at the 2026-09-03 anchor plus uptime, so every session replays the same morning: ~08:00, then 08:1x, then 09:0x.

That single mechanism explains all of it:

- **The unprompted 15 g dispense at boot** we watched — at the anchor the board believes it's 08:00 on 09-03, so the morning meals read as due, every boot, forever.
- **The duplicate same-minute pairs** (`19:01 jay 12 g` twice, `19:02` jay+bob) — scheduled catch-up firing repeatedly inside one minute.
- **Why the window never rolls** — `vp_sync_day` computes `today` from that frozen clock, sees `today <= g_hist_day`, and correctly refuses to shift backwards. Your own comment at line 400 anticipates this exactly. The guard is right; the clock feeding it is wrong.

## 2. The inheritance bug has a concrete mechanism — delete-compaction desync

Enroll is strictly **append-at-`g_npets`**:
```c
struct velapaw_pet *p = &g_pets[g_npets];
p->id = g_npets;
```

But the UI delete path at [ui_lvgl.c:1503-1504](apps/examples/velapaw/ui/ui_lvgl.c#L1503) says *"icons were shifted too"* — so deleting a pet **compacts the `g_pets[]` array downward**. Meanwhile the store's `g_day_g[]`, `g_day_m[]` and `g_bcs[]` are indexed by that same slot number and nothing shifts them.

So after any delete, **every pet above the deleted index silently inherits the previous occupant's intake, meal count and body-condition score.** That's not a hypothesis about data any more — it's an index-aliasing bug between two arrays with different mutation rules.

It accounts for everything we found: four names in the log but `velapaw_identity_count() == 1` means three pets were deleted through the UI; `bob,` now sits at a compacted index carrying someone else's 38 g/day baseline and 298 g week total, against only 52 g of events actually attributed to that name. ## 2026-10-11: the VP02 fix is correct but INERT — the anchor freezes the clock

The day-roll fix above has never once fired on hardware, and the reason is
`ui_lvgl.c:3620`:

```c
#define VELAPAW_CLOCK_ANCHOR 1788393600L           /* 2026-09-03 00:00 */
if (_ts.tv_sec < VELAPAW_CLOCK_ANCHOR)
    _ts.tv_sec  = VELAPAW_CLOCK_ANCHOR + 8 * 3600; /* 08:00 that day */
```

Every cold boot sets the wall clock to **2026-09-03 08:00**. So `vp_sync_day()`
computes `today == g_hist_day` for ever, takes its (correct) never-shift-
backwards branch, and the 30-day window can never roll. Five weeks of real
time had passed with the board still reporting "today" as 09-03. **Bump the
anchor whenever the reported date looks stale** — 2026-10-11 00:00 is
`1791676800L`. The guard is right; the clock feeding it is wrong.

Same root cause, bigger consequence: at 08:00 every morning meal reads as
**due on every power-up**, so the board dispenses unprompted at boot
(`[feeder] dispensed 3 pocket(s) ~15g (1023 steps, asked 13g)`), then logs it
against a timestamp that collides with previous boots'.

**The fingerprint to look for:** `feed_log.md` is append-only, so file order
*is* write order — yet timestamps run 08:01 → 19:02 → 09:08 → 08:02. Time
going *backwards* in an append-only log can only mean the clock reset between
writes, which is the anchor. Reading that pattern is how the mechanism was
found before the `#define` was ever opened.

**Do not use `feed_log.md` for totals.** `vp_feedlog_append()` treats
`st.st_size > VP_LOG_MAX` by reopening with `"w"` — it **truncates and
restarts**, it does not rotate. The visible file is the latest fragment only,
which is why a pet's "last 7 days" legitimately exceeds everything in it.
`status.md` is also *live* (regenerated from the current identity table) while
the log's names are *fossils* captured at each event, so the two disagreeing
about which pets exist is normal after a delete, not corruption.

**Delete-compaction is already handled correctly — don't go hunting there.**
`do_delete_pet()` in `ui_lvgl.c` shifts its four `g_meal_*` tables, calls
`velapaw_store_delete(id)` ("history + BCS, shifted to match") and
`velapaw_identity_delete(id)`, then invalidates every held id.
`identity.h:52` documents the renumbering hazard explicitly. A single enrolled
pet alongside four names in the log just means three were deleted via the UI.

Name junk enters at the **UI enroll dialog** (`ui_lvgl.c:1041`), not the
Rex/Milo scaffold — those literals are clean. The on-screen keyboard admits a
stray comma or double space, and `identity.c:276` stores argv verbatim
(`strncpy`, no trim). It is the single write site, so trimming there covers
the dialog, the CLI and any future agent tool.

/* Reconcile the window with the wall clock.  Safe on every path that
 * touches the history -- it is a no-op within a single day.
 */
static void vp_sync_day(void)
{
  long today = vp_today_num();

  if (today < 0)
    {
      return;              /* clock unusable -- leave the window alone */
    }

  if (g_hist_day < 0)
    {
      /* First run, or a VP01 file: the data in the window is real, we just
       * never knew which day it belonged to.  Adopt today, do not shift.
       */
      g_hist_day = today;
      vp_history_save();
      return;
    }

  if (today <= g_hist_day)
    {
      /* Same day, or the clock jumped backwards -- which the build-date
       * boot anchor does on every cold start.  Never shift backwards: it
       * would drop real days off the front and zero slots that hold data.
       */
      return;
    }

  vp_shift_days((int)(today - g_hist_day));
  g_hist_day = today;
  vp_history_save();
}

152	**"Stale console history suppresses tool calls" — I RECORDED THIS AS CONFIRMED OFF ONE OBSERVATION AND IT DID NOT HOLD.** The original claim: same firmware, same question, 20 min apart, stale `tg_console.jsonl` → `iters=1 tools=0` and an answer that missed Bob; cleared → `iters=3 tools=2` and the right answer. **Two later control runs with stale history never reproduced `tools=0`** — both called tools and failed for an entirely different reason (a broken `list_dir`, below). One A/B with a confounded variable is not a mechanism. **The real defect chain was in the tools, not the history**, and the correct answer now comes back *with* stale history in place. Keep the general caution — a turn about current device state *can* in principle be answered from replayed history — but treat it as unproven on this device. **The lesson worth more than the finding: do not write a single observation into memory as a confirmed mechanism when the two runs differed in more than one variable.**
153	
154	**`list_dir` was broken two ways at once, and the shortcut turned that into a wrong answer delivered to the user — fixed 2026-09-04, hardware-verified.** (1) The prefix was matched against the *absolute* path (`/data/ai_agent/velapaw`) while the model passes a *relative* one (`velapaw`), so every entry was filtered out; worse, the `continue` ran **before** the recursive call, so non-matching directories were never descended into. (2) `list_dir` sat in the local-tool shortcut set in `agent_loop.c`, so its empty result **ended the turn and was handed to the user as the answer** — a user asking which pet to worry about literally received `(no files found)`. Fixes: match the prefix against **either** the relative or the absolute path (`strncmp(full_path,…) || strncmp(rel,…)`), always recurse, and drop `list_dir` from the shortcut set. Also added: no shortcut when tool output starts with `"Error: "` (the `tool_files.c` convention is `Error: …`/`OK: …` at every one of ~20 sites). **My own trap, worth repeating: I first replaced absolute matching with relative matching — fixing the case I had observed and breaking the case I hadn't. I considered accepting both while designing it and then didn't implement it.** Across three hardware runs the model used three different call shapes (`"velapaw"`, `"/data/ai_agent/"`, no prefix at all) — **a tool that only handles the spelling you happened to observe will look fixed and then fail**; the passing run used no prefix, so the both-forms branch is proven by code reading, not by that run.
155	
156	**Forcing a re-read beats trimming history.** Added to `build_messages` in `agent_loop.c`: when history is non-empty, append a mid-array `{"role":"system"}` message before the user turn saying device state may have changed, any earlier figure is stale, and to re-read the relevant files before answering about present state. Mid-array system messages are already used in this file (lines ~813, ~983) and DeepSeek accepts them. Guard is free: heartbeat blanks `history_json` → `cJSON_Parse` NULL → empty array → skipped. Result with stale history still on disk: `iters=3 tools=2`, both `read_file`s on the real files, answer opens *"Now I have the current feeding data"* and flags Bob correctly. **`AGENT_AI_AGENT_MAX_HISTORY` (10, `agent_config.h:108`) was NOT trimmed — it stays the fallback lever if this regresses.**
157	
158	**Cutting a tool leaves callers behind — the NL fast paths in `agent_loop.c` dispatched to five removed tools, fixed + hardware-verified 2026-09-04 (`cd2b4edd3baf27b25edae5db200ffe4a`).** `handle_nl_fast_path` runs *before* the LLM and returns its result as the final answer, so a shortcut pointing at an unregistered tool ends the turn with garbage. Three separate sites, and **finding them needed one grep, not code reading**: `grep -n 'get_heartrate\|get_steps\|get_wear_state\|vibrate\|music_\|feishu_\|quickapp' agent_loop.c` — run it after ANY change to `s_excluded_tools`, and require it to come back empty.

Rows removed, plus a **general guard**: `if (reply && reply[0] == '\0') { free(reply); reply = NULL; }` so any future missing tool falls through to the LLM instead of answering blank.
160	2. **A hand-written music block** (~60 lines, `kw_play` → `music_search` → `music_play`). **The guard could not have saved this one** — on failure it `snprintf`s `"找到了 %s - %s，但播放失败: %s"`, i.e. a confident *non-empty* wrong sentence, or `strncpy`s the zeroed `search_result` into a 4096 B buffer. Deleted entirely.
161	3. **`inject_session_context` still told the model about `feishu_send_mention`/`feishu_chat_members`** in the system prompt of **every** request — dead bytes working against the request-size fix, plus an invitation to call tools that don't exist. Removed along with the `[mentioned_users: …]` paragraph (Feishu-only, and no Feishu channel is built).
162	Verified directly, not by inference: `ask play some music for my cat` → `NL fast path fired: NO`, one LLM round, `END status=ok`, and a real answer ("I don't have the ability to play music directly") that still knew Bob and Jay from session context. The digest path was re-run unchanged: `iters=3 tools=2`, both files read, `cache replay: no`, Bob correctly flagged at 33 %. **Image size is a usable signal here for once** — 1567872 → 1567632 (table) → 1567152 (music+prompt); an earlier rebuild after a *refused* patch came out at the unchanged 1567872 and I nearly mistook its new md5 (`e85d67fe…`, a build-timestamp difference) for the fix. **Process failure worth keeping: I scoped this fix three times and was wrong twice** — first "two dead entries" (the table had five), then "the table" (two more sites sat outside it). The grep above was available from the start.

164	**`Ethernet 2` can silently reroute board traffic into the VPN — and "0 % loss" does not mean the board answered.** A run that ended `END status=timeout llm_ms=480920` (exactly `AGENT_LLM_SOCKET_TIMEOUT_SEC`) was not a model problem: the board's USB Ethernet link was down, so `Get-NetIPInterface` showed `ConnectionState: Disconnected`, 192.168.137.1 sat at `AddressState: Tentative` (DAD never completed ⇒ unusable as a source ⇒ **all routes on that interface are skipped**), and Windows fell through to WireGuard's `128.0.0.0/1`. **My own false pass: `ping -n 2` reported `Received = 2, Lost = 0 (0% loss)` while every reply read `Reply from 10.234.0.0: Destination port unreachable` — ICMP errors from the tunnel. Read the reply source address, never the loss percentage.** The full green checklist before any ask: adapter `Up`/`Connected` with a non-zero LinkSpeed, 192.168.137.1 `Preferred`, `Find-NetRoute -RemoteIPAddress 192.168.137.2` selecting `Ethernet 2`, ping replies **from 192.168.137.2**, `Get-NetNeighbor` `Reachable`. Two things left, both small:

1. **`## bob,`** — `vp_copy_name()` only trims on enroll, so this record keeps its comma until you delete the pet on the touchscreen and re-enroll. Worth doing before any demo capture, since `bob` and `bob,` would otherwise be distinct keys in the log.

lets move to the meal scheduling

Good timing — scheduling against a clock frozen at 2026-09-03 would have been untestable, so that blocker clearing first was lucky ordering.

I'm taking this as the deferred item: **an agent-driven `set_meal_schedule` tool**, so meal times can be set by asking the agent, replacing the voice dialog that the mic path killed. Say the word if you meant the existing scheduler itself rather than the agent route, and I'll redirect — but the mapping below is needed either way.

Three things I need to establish before writing anything, because guessing at any of them produces a tool that looks right and silently doesn't schedule:

- **Where meal times live and who owns them.** `p->meal_min[]` is in the identity table, so it's per-pet and persisted via `velapaw_identity_save()` — but I need to see whether the UI reads it live each tick or caches it, because an agent writing the array while the UI holds a copy would be a no-op until reboot.
- **The due-check and the fed-today bookkeeping.** `g_meal_fed_day/_min/_g/_skipped` are RAM-only statics cleared on every boot, and `g_meal_skipped` date-stamping is a known-deferred item. If "has this meal been fed today" doesn't survive a reboot, a tool that sets a morning meal hands you a double-feed on the next power cycle.
- **Whether the agent has ever written device state.** Every existing velapaw touchpoint is `read_file`. A `set_meal_schedule` tool would be the first one that *writes*, which is also the contest's 执行 half — worth getting the shape right rather than bolting it onto `tool_files.c`.

On the VM:

```
cd ~/openvela/apps/examples/velapaw
grep -n "meal_min\|g_meal_fed\|g_meal_skipped\|VELAPAW_MAX_MEALS" ui/ui_lvgl.c identity/identity.c identity/identity.h | head -60
```

```
cd ~/openvela
grep -rn "velapaw\|set_meal\|schedule" packages/ai_agent/src/tool_registry.c | head -30
ls packages/ai_agent/src/tools/
```

The first tells me the data path and the reboot hazard; the second tells me whether there's already a velapaw-aware tool to extend or whether this is a new registration. Once I can see both, I'll give you the patch as a single unified diff the way you asked last time, rather than prose plus scattered blocks.
But we have to use voice remember through the agent is it possible?

Yes, but "voice through the agent" splits into three quite different architectures, and only one of them is cheap.

**1. Free-form speech → cloud STT → agent.** This is what "talk to the agent" normally means, and the arithmetic is against us. KWS audio is 16 kHz/16-bit mono, so one second is 32 KB raw and ~43 KB base64'd. The IOB pool on this board is `64 × 196 = 12,544 B` total with roughly **7,840 B usable to a sender** after THROTTLE — and a 19,391-byte LLM request is what wedged the send path hard enough to need a RESET. A three-second utterance is ~128 KB, about **16× the usable pool**. It can only work by blocking and draining as ACKs recycle buffers, which is exactly the mechanism that already failed. Add an STT provider, a second API key, and chunked multipart upload, and this is the riskiest thing we'd have attempted on this stack. Possible, not advisable.

**2. On-device KWS → agent tool call.** Keep the 14-label model as the voice front end and have the committed intent call `set_meal_schedule` instead of writing the meal table directly. Voice and the agent are both genuinely in the loop, no cloud STT, no new network load. 56	the stream — both slots reach the FIFO and the DMA, with the invalid one
57	zero-filled. Buffers read `[sample, 0, sample, 0, ...]`. This is not 32-bit
58	slot padding: `i2s_set_datawidth()` programs 16-bit slots
59	(`CHAN_BITS = HALF_SAMPLE_BITS = data_width`). It is VelaPaw patch #25:
60	`TOT_CHAN_NUM=1` (two slots) + `CHAN0_EN|CHAN1_EN` + `I2S_RX_MONO`.
61	
62	Consequence: a 16000-`int16` window was **0.5 s of audio with a zero between
63	every sample** — a mirrored spectrum landing inside micro_speech's mel bins.
64	Fix is `MIC_STRIDE 2` — keep one `int16` in two, in `mic_collect()`.

66	### ⚠️ The live slot flips PER CAPTURE, not per build
67	
68	Build 52, one boot: capture 1 slot 0, capture 2 slot 0, capture 3 **slot 1**.
69	Every capture re-arms RX and the first sample lands wherever the frame is.
70	Hardcoding slot 0 makes a capture come back all zeros and look like a dead
71	mic. `mic_data_phase()` measures it, per capture, by counting **exact zeros**
72	— the dead slot is 0 to the bit while the live slot has an ADC noise floor
73	even in a silent room. It returns −1 for an all-zero buffer (RX emits a few
74	while warming up) so the phase is settled off the first buffer with content,
75	not a coin flip.

77	## 🔴 Audio buffers live in PSRAM and the driver does no cache maintenance
78	
79	`apb->samp` addresses are `0x3C5x_xxxx` = the external-memory window
80	(`CONFIG_ESP32S3_SPIRAM=y`, `CONFIG_MM_REGIONS=2`). `esp32s3_i2s.c` has **no**
81	invalidate/writeback/barrier anywhere. So **reusing a buffer inside one
82	window returns a stale cached copy**: first delivery misses cache and reads
83	what DMA wrote, the copy pulls 4 KB into DCache, and ~500 ms later the same
84	buffer hits those warm lines. Signature: an 8-segment profile that repeats
85	with a period equal to the pool depth, and identical samples at the same
86	`apb` pointer.
87	
88	**Fix = never reuse a buffer inside a window.** `GETBUFFERINFO`'s `nbuffers`
89	is a *suggestion*, not a cap — `ALLOCBUFFER` is per-call. `MIC_WANT_BUFS 18`
90	(one delivery = 4092 B = 2046 `int16` = 1023 usable samples after stride, so
91	16000 needs 16 + `MIC_SKIP_BUFS`).
92	
93	### The follow-on trap: a deep pool overruns the quiesce budget
94	
95	Requeueing every accepted buffer left ~17 in flight; one buffer is 128 ms, so
96	draining needs 2.3 s against a 1 s budget sized when the pool was 4. Quiesce
97	timed out, the *next* capture armed with 6 free buffers, and they recycled 3×
98	— reintroducing the cache bug. Two fixes together:
99	- requeue only when `skipped + seq >= nrecbufs - 1` (self-adjusting: a capped
100	  pool still finishes by falling back to recycling)
101	- `MIC_QUIESCE_TRIES 80` (4 s) — a ceiling, not a cost

455	                      seconds in, board settled            -> 6 good boots
456	    b85 / b86         first capture at ~13.1 s -- mid TFLM model reads, camera
457	                      bring-up, the 5350 ms pre-open       -> 0 good boots
458	
459	**b87 holds unarmed captures until `VOICE_WARMUP_AT_MS` (30 s) after power-on**,
460	tested against `mono_ms()` (monotonic from boot). Armed captures are *not*
461	delayed. Falsifiable: the vlog shows either nothing (warm-up succeeded) or
462	`warmup FAILED -110 (#1)` at ~33 s — and if it fails at 33 s exactly as at 16 s,
463	**timing is not the variable** and the next move is rebuilding the session
464	(close both fds, re-open, which is the only thing that re-runs ES8311
465	configure). b80 removed that path because `mic_session_close()` hung, but that
466	predates b79's fix of the collect hang.
467	
468	Build chain, all esptool hash-verified on-chip:
469	`b83 288649a9` → `b84 a0860dee` → `b85 ec7c1d4d` → `b86 1666c029` →
470	`b87 95a383ed`. Console fix: [[velapaw-console-blocking]].
471	
472	## ✅ SOLVED: the `es8311 -22` boot spam is cosmetic — never chase it
473	
474	    es8311_getcoeff: MCLK = 4096000 and samplerate = 48000 not supported
475	    es8311_setsamplerate: Failed to set sample rate: -22
476	
477	The driver does it to itself. `es8311.c:2153` sets
478	`priv->samprate = ES8311_DEFAULT_SAMPRATE` (48000), then `:2191` calls
479	`es8311_setsamplerate()` during init while MCLK is 4096000 (= 256 × 16000).
480	`getcoeff(4096000, 48000)` has no table entry → `-22`. The real rate is
481	programmed later from `caps->ac_controls.hw[0]`, and `:1039` already calls
482	`es8311_reset()` *before* `:1046`'s `setsamplerate()`. **It appears in working
483	boots too**, so its presence in a failing log means nothing. This misled a
484	third-party analysis into proposing an ES8311 power-up clock race; that was
485	rejected on evidence.
486	
487	## Session shape
488	
489	Open, configure, `AUDIOIOC_START` **once**; each capture only enqueues and
490	collects. Between captures the session is running but idle. Free-running RX is
491	not an option: `mq_maxmsg = nbuffers + 8`, so with no reader the driver's
492	`mq_send` would drop buffer pointers. `mic_flush_mq()` before each re-arm.
493	
494	⚠️ **`apb->nbytes` is read by the driver *during* the enqueue ioctl** — the
495	caller sets it: record side `0`, playback side `nmaxbytes`. Zeroing it in a
496	shared helper silently sends a zero-length TX buffer → no clock → hang. TX
497	must stay primed; RX borrows BCLK/WS from TX (see [[velapaw-audio-bringup]]).
498	
499	⚠️ Do not conflate this with the falsified theory above. A **zero-length first**
500	TX buffer means `I2S_TX_START` is never set, so the clock never starts — real.
501	TX **draining after** a good buffer is harmless, because `TX_START` stays set
502	and `#16` cleared `TX_STOP_EN`.
503	
504	## Measurement, not ears
505	
506	`velapaw_mic_stats()` prints `peak N@index`, `rms`, `dc`, `rail` and an
507	8-segment peak profile. Reference at 30 dB, build 52, de-interleaved:

511	    "no"     rms 791  profile  1949  5402  3534   596    74    66    87    94

514	four samples — the check on both fixes at once: pointers must all be distinct,
515	`s` must alternate live/0. Turn it on for any future capture regression.
516	Do **not** read a full-scale spike at a fixed index as clipping — that is the
517	start-of-stream transient, see [[velapaw-audio-gain]].
