**Voice is hardware-blocked, and that's the finding — not a decision I'm making to avoid the work.** You said voice is a requirement, so here's the one cheap test that hasn't been recorded as tried.

The codec's I²S bus is **IO12–16** (MCLK 12, BCLK 13, DIN 14, WS 15, DOUT 16). Voice worked 3-of-5 cold boots on b81 on **2026-08-07**, and was dead by **2026-09-22**. What happened physically in that window is stepper bring-up on **GPIO 9/10/11/43** and the camera connector work. GPIO11 sits directly against GPIO12. That's a loading/adjacency suspect nobody has excluded, and excluding it costs no build:

**Unplug the four stepper wires from the ULN2003 header, cold power cycle (not RESET), press Enter 3×, then go straight to My Pets → Edit and say one word.** Nothing else first — no `velapaw kws mic`, which poisons the product path. If the mic answers, the stepper wiring is the fault and voice comes back for the cost of re-routing one pin. If it still `-110`s, the stepper is excluded and the logic analyzer on GPIO14+BCLK+WS is the real next move — that rig is already parked in the board file behind `SPI_CAPTURE_BUILD 0`.

I'd leave the camera ribbon alone for now: `velapaw-camera-connector` records that a reversed J2 cable is **fatal on power-on**, so that's not a casual unplug-and-retry.

In parallel, meal scheduling ships through `ask`, and it needs a write tool built. Where the state lives decides the shape:

```
cd ~/openvela
grep -n "g_meal_min\|g_meal_fed_day\|g_meal_g\|g_meal_skipped" apps/examples/velapaw/ui/ui_lvgl.c | head -40
grep -rn "meal" apps/examples/velapaw/store/ apps/examples/velapaw/*.h | head -20
```

If the second grep is empty, meal times are RAM-only in `ui_lvgl.c` statics — which is also the double-feed hazard, since "fed today" wouldn't survive a power cycle. Then the job is a persisted setter in the store plus one `set_meal_schedule` tool, and the tool has to clear the `s_excluded_tools` cut and the orphaned-NL-fast-path grep from the integration memory.

Confirmed: meal scheduling has **no persistence at all**. The store knows about intake history and nothing about meal times — `g_meal_min` is a plain static at [ui_lvgl.c:190](apps/examples/velapaw/ui/ui_lvgl.c#L190) initialised to `{8:00, 12:30, 18:00}`, with no save or load anywhere.

That surfaces two real defects, and they matter before any tool gets built:

1. **Meal times don't survive a reboot.** The voice dialog's `COMMIT meal 2 = 08:00` writes RAM. Power cycle and it's back to the hardcoded defaults. An agent tool that sets a meal time which silently evaporates is worse than no tool.
2. **`g_meal_fed_day` doesn't survive either** — [:3601](apps/examples/velapaw/ui/ui_lvgl.c#L3601) resets it to `-1`, "no scheduled meal eaten yet", on every init. So a pet that already ate breakfast gets fed again on the next boot when it's recognised. Same dangerous direction as the day-stamp bug: the feeder acting on state it has lost.

So this isn't "add a tool", it's "give meal scheduling a persistent home, then expose it." The store is the obvious home — it already owns littlefs, the VP02 format and `status.md`.

One thing to settle first, because it decides the tool's signature. `g_meal_min` is `[VELAPAW_MAX_MEALS]` — **global across pets** — but [:1343](apps/examples/velapaw/ui/ui_lvgl.c#L1343) reads `(g_edit_pet >= 0) ? g_edit_meal : g_meal_min`, which looks per-pet, and [:1043](apps/examples/velapaw/ui/ui_lvgl.c#L1043) hands `g_meal_min` to the enroll dialog as "3 meal times". Those can't all be true at once:

```
cd ~/openvela
grep -rn "meal" apps/examples/velapaw/identity/ | grep -v "\.o:" | head -20
sed -n '1335,1350p' apps/examples/velapaw/ui/ui_lvgl.c
grep -n "g_edit_meal" apps/examples/velapaw/ui/ui_lvgl.c | head
```

If identity stores meal times per pet, the tool is `set_meal_schedule(pet, slot, hh:mm)` and persistence rides along with the identity record. If they're genuinely global, it's `set_meal_schedule(slot, hh:mm)` and a new VP03 header word (or a small sidecar file) carries them — and the `g_meal_fed_day` fix needs its own day-stamped slot either way.

Worth saying plainly: on the current firmware, the voice dialog you proved working in August was committing meal times that the next power cycle threw away. Fixing persistence makes scheduling real whether the input ends up being voice or `ask`.

`velapaw_identity_update()` **only mutates RAM** — it sets `p->meal_min[k]` and returns 0, with no write to flash. Persistence is a separate function, `velapaw_identity_save()` at [:124](apps/examples/velapaw/identity/identity.c#L124). So whether meal times survive a reboot comes down to whether the UI calls save after update:

```
cd ~/openvela
grep -n "velapaw_identity_save" apps/examples/velapaw/ui/ui_lvgl.c
sed -n '1440,1462p' apps/examples/velapaw/ui/ui_lvgl.c
```

This is the last thing the tool design is waiting on, and either answer is actionable:

- **Save is called there** → meal times persist today, and `set_meal_schedule` is `update()` + `save()`, a small tool with no format work.
- **Save is not called** → my original claim was right after all, just by a different mechanism than the array I blamed: edits live until power-off. Then the fix is one `velapaw_identity_save()` call in the edit-confirm path, which also repairs the touchscreen and voice paths, not just the agent one.

Either way the tool body is the same three steps — resolve name to id, set the slot, update + save — so this only changes whether a one-line fix ships alongside it.

Here's the design, and one decision in it saves real budget.

**Reading meal times costs no tool at all.** The agent currently can't see meal times anywhere — they're not in `status.md`. Rather than add a `get_meal_schedule` tool, add the three times to `vp_status_write()`'s output. `store_stub.c` already prints pet names (`## bob,`), so it already knows the identity table; `p->meal_min[]` is right there. The agent then reads meal times through the `read_file` path it already uses, and we spend schema budget on exactly one tool instead of two.

So three small pieces:

1. **`identity.c` / `identity.h`** — `velapaw_meal_set_by_name(const char *name, int slot, int minute)`. Does the name resolution, copies `p->meal_min[]`, sets one slot, calls `velapaw_identity_update()` + `velapaw_identity_save()`. Name matching must be **tolerant** — case-insensitive and trimming whitespace and trailing punctuation — because `bob,` is literally the name stored on your board right now, and an LLM saying "bob" has to match it.
2. **`store_stub.c`** — emit `- meals: 08:00 12:30 18:00` (and `off` for `-1`) in `vp_status_write()`.
3. **`packages/ai_agent`** — one `set_meal_schedule` tool calling the new entry point, plus its registry line.

Found it, and the fix is already half-written in the file. Look at lines 1269-1289: there's an existing `is_instruction_read` escape hatch whose entire purpose is "this `read_file` returned *material to reason over*, not a finished answer — don't end the turn on it." It covers skill files and the heartbeat file. And lines 1240-1245 show `list_dir` was pulled out of the local set for exactly the same class of bug, with the same symptom: `iters=1` and a raw tool dump handed to the user.

`/data/ai_agent/velapaw/status.md` belongs in that hatch. So this is one condition added to a guard that already exists for this reason — not a new mechanism, and better than rewriting the tool description, because "read the names first, then write" is genuinely the correct behaviour and shouldn't depend on the model choosing to skip the read.

```bash
cd ~/openvela
cat > /tmp/velapaw-shortcut.py <<'PYEOF'
import os

P = os.path.expanduser('~/openvela/packages/ai_agent/src/core/agent_loop.c')

ANCHOR = '''                                || strcmp(path_obj->valuestring,
                                    AGENT_HEARTBEAT_FILE) == 0)) {'''

NEW = '''                                || strcmp(path_obj->valuestring,
                                    AGENT_HEARTBEAT_FILE) == 0
                                /* velapaw: /data/ai_agent/velapaw/ holds
                                 * status.md, feed_log.md and history.bin.
                                 * All three are DATA to reason over, never a
                                 * finished answer.  set_meal_schedule needs
                                 * two rounds -- read the enrolled names and
                                 * current times, then write one slot -- and
                                 * the shortcut ended the turn after the read,
                                 * handing the owner a raw status dump while
                                 * the meal went unset.  Same class of bug as
                                 * list_dir above. */
                                || strstr(path_obj->valuestring,
                                    "/velapaw/") != NULL)) {'''

with open(P, encoding='utf-8', errors='surrogateescape') as f:
    s = f.read()

if '"/velapaw/"' in s:
    print('SKIP  (already applied)')
    raise SystemExit(0)

if s.count(ANCHOR) != 1:
    print('FAIL  anchor x%d' % s.count(ANCHOR))
    raise SystemExit(1)

with open(P, 'w', encoding='utf-8', errors='surrogateescape') as f:
    f.write(s.replace(ANCHOR, NEW))
print('PATCH src/core/agent_loop.c')
PYEOF
python3 /tmp/velapaw-shortcut.py
```

## The three pieces

1. **`velapaw_meal_set_by_name(name, slot, minute)`** in
   `apps/examples/velapaw/identity/identity.c`. Pet ids are array indices that
   renumber on delete (`identity.h:52`), so a **name is the only stable handle**

   leading whitespace, trim trailing non-alphanumerics — because the enrolled

   keyboard. The model sent `"pet": "bob"` and it matched; the normaliser

   three slots** before writing one, because `velapaw_identity_update()` writes
   every slot it is handed; passing 0 for portion/limit means "leave alone".
2. **`vp_status_write()` publishes the meal times** as
   `- scheduled meals: HH:MM HH:MM HH:MM` (or `off`). This is why there is
   **no `get_meal_schedule` tool** — the agent already reaches `status.md`

   recognised at the bowl at or after that time"), or the model promises the
   owner food appears on the clock alone, which is false.

`agent_loop.c` ~1230 short-circuits the turn when a round has exactly one
"local" tool call: it hands the raw tool output to the user as the final reply
and never does another LLM round. **That structurally kills every two-step
plan.** First run of the new tool: the model correctly called `read_file` on

Deliberately did NOT "fix" this by rewriting the tool description to make the
model skip the read. Read-then-write is the correct behaviour (right name,
current times) and must not depend on the model choosing to skip a step.

/**
 * Execute a tool with streaming output. Uses a growable buffer
 * internally, then copies the result to the caller's fixed buffer.
 * This avoids allocating a large fixed buffer upfront for tools
 * that may return small results.
 *
 * Returns the number of bytes written (excluding NUL), or -1 on error.
 *
 * NOTE: tool is executed exactly ONCE. No retry to avoid double
 * side-effects on write/mutating tools.
 */
static inline int agent_tool_exec_streamed(
    const char* name, const char* input_json,
    char* output, size_t output_size)
{
    /* Allocate a buffer sized to output_size so the tool can write its
     * full result without truncation.  We avoid the small-then-retry
     * pattern because retrying would execute the tool twice, which is
     * wrong for write/mutating tools (write_file, cron_add, etc.). */
    size_t buf_size = agent_mem_safe_size(output_size, AGENT_STREAM_INIT_SIZE);
    char* buf = malloc(buf_size);
    if (buf) {
        buf[0] = '\0';
        tool_registry_execute(name, input_json, buf, buf_size);
        size_t result_len = strlen(buf);
        if (result_len >= output_size)
            result_len = output_size - 1;
        memcpy(output, buf, result_len);
        output[result_len] = '\0';
        free(buf);
        return (int)result_len;
    }

    /* OOM fallback: execute directly into caller buffer */
    output[0] = '\0';
    tool_registry_execute(name, input_json, output, output_size);
    return (int)strlen(output);
}

}

## SOLVED: the HTTP 400 invalid unicode code point was a use-after-free

Every successful write used to end with the owner seeing `Sorry, I encountered
an error`, because the round *after* `set_meal_schedule` returned was rejected
with `[llm] API error 400: … messages[N].content: invalid unicode code point`.
The write was already on flash, so a working action reported failure.

**Root cause, in `tool_meal.c`:** `cJSON_Delete(root)` ran while `const char
*pet` still pointed **into** that tree, and all six `switch` branches format
`pet` afterwards. The success string therefore carried raw freed-heap bytes at
the `%s`, and DeepSeek rejected the whole request. Fix is three lines — copy
the name into a `char petbuf[64]` and repoint `pet` at the copy **before** the
delete; reassigning `pet` covers all six branches without renaming anything.
Verified 2026-10-11 on firmware `9242daf64d1c9744f9d1ec917bf13d69`
(1563648 B): `result: 151 bytes`, no sanitiser warning, `status=ok iters=3
tools=2` in 5 s, real owner-facing reply.

**The byte arithmetic was the signal all along.** The log said `result: 163
bytes`; hand-counting the format string twice gave 151. I trusted the count and
hunted an encoder bug instead of asking why the gap existed. `"Meal 2 for "` is
11 bytes and the diagnostic reported only 13 valid — corruption began exactly
at the `%s`, which names the variable.

**Two theories falsified on the way — do not re-derive either.** (1) History
truncation: first failure at column 8230 against `hist=8192` looked conclusive;
`session_clear_all` reproduced it at column 4536 in a 10286-byte body.
(2) A stale over-read of `tool_output`: `cJSON_AddStringToObject` passes bytes
through verbatim and takes its own `strlen`, and `agent_tool_exec_streamed`
(`static inline` in `src/core/agent_mem.h:278`) is a clean malloc/execute/
memcpy with no appending — the message holds exactly our NUL-terminated bytes.
Also wrong: re-indexing `messages[N]` onto the assistant message. `msg[0]
role=user` proves the **system prompt is not in the messages array**.

**Kept as defence:** `utf8_valid_prefix()` + `add_clean_string()` in
`agent_loop.c` now sanitise all four content sites (assistant `content` and
`reasoning_content`, single- and parallel-tool results), logging `[agent]
UTF-8: trimmed N of M byte(s) from "<key>"`. That warning is what localised
this bug; a malformed string no longer hard-fails a turn. The companion

Correction on one point from my last message: the ping loop did **not** prime ARP for that `ask`. The loop ended at 12:34 local; the request's `UNIX=1791717469` puts it at ~13:17 — about 45 minutes later. So the board's `arp_wait failed: -110` against the gateway **self-recovered via retry**, with no host-side priming at all. That's a better outcome than the memory currently records, and worth knowing before anyone adds a priming step to the demo script.

The loop's own output is also not trustworthy as liveness: it printed `board UP` for 12:30:02–12:31:39 and then went silent, and the final neighbour state is `Incomplete` / `Unreachable`. A `-Quiet` ping doesn't reveal the reply source, so those hits are exactly the VPN ICMP-spoof pattern already on file — not evidence the board answered.

301	margin change doing precisely what it was designed to do. 1230 ms against the
302	new 3500 ms timeout is 2.8× margin, so the shortening is empirically safe.
303	But the stall simply **did not occur** this boot — it was always intermittent,
304	and one passing boot proves nothing about it. Needs repeat cold cycles.
305	
306	b81 fixes it in the only order that works:
307	1. **`velapaw_mic_preopen()`** — worker opens the session at init, moving the
308	   5350 ms to boot. Margin 650 ms → ~6 s. Must be called **by the capturing
309	   thread** (session is owned by pid; mismatch = the `-110` reopen path).
310	   Non-fatal: on failure the first capture opens inline exactly as before.
311	2. **`VOICE_CAPTURE_MS` 8000 → 3500** — two attempts now fit in the dialog's
312	   window (3500 + 200 + 3500 = 7200), finally making b79's retry reachable.
313	   Doing (2) without (1) is pointless — retries fire into a half-eaten window.
314	
315	🔴 **The `g_mic_fresh` double-enqueue guard is load-bearing.**
316	`mic_session_open()` returns with 19 buffers **already armed and in flight** —
317	which is why the inline-open path goes straight to collect while the
318	already-open path does flush + arm. A pre-opened session would take the second
319	branch and enqueue on top of buffers the driver still holds. `g_mic_fresh`
320	marks "opened, never captured from" so the first capture skips the re-arm.
321	
322	⚠️ Name trap: `velapaw_mic_open` is a **substring of the existing**
323	`struct velapaw_mic_open_s` and `velapaw_mic_open_log`, so a `grep`-style
324	"already applied?" guard false-positives on it. The function is
325	`velapaw_mic_preopen()`.
326	
327	⚠️ `mic_status()` tag literals (`"rec enq"`, `"rec start"`, `"rec fresh"`…) are
328	**optimized out of the image** — they read 0 under `grep -a` in b80 *and* b81.
329	Do not use them as build-verification markers; use a `printf` string instead.
330	
331	## 🔴 SIX MECHANISMS FALSIFIED — do not rebuild any of them
332	
333	All with hardware counters, builds b70–b80. RX arms and its DMA never signals
334	EOF; nothing reachable from software changes that.
335	
336	1. **Dead TX ⇒ dead clock / TX requeue (b71).** `TX_STOP_EN` clear, `TX_START`
337	   set, `SIG_LOOPBACK` set, TX is master. Falsified at the register level.
338	2. **Descriptor-walk desync (patch #31's missing `else`).** `miss 0` on every
339	   run, every build. #31 is a defensible latent-bug fix but **not this bug** —
340	   kept as `patch31-i2s-rx-eof-walk.NOT-APPLIED.py` in the b68 snapshot.
341	3. **Redundant reconfigures (patch #35 half 1).** b78 measured `cfgskip 20
342	   chst 1 resc 0` — every redundant reconfigure declined, zero restarts — and
343	   the stall was unchanged. Reverted by #36.
344	4. **RX/FIFO/GDMA reset as recovery (patch #36's `velapaw_i2s_rx_kick()`).**
345	   `kick 1`, `ok 0`. The kick provably runs and clears nothing.
346	5. **Lost or masked EOF interrupt.** `isr 0` with `start 2` — there is no
347	   interrupt to lose.
348	6. **RX-before-TX start ordering (b80).** Started rec fd 200 µs before play fd.
349	   **Identical** signature: `isr 0 / eof 0 / start 2`, `desc 80000ff0`,
350	   `intraw 000000a0`. Predicted dead beforehand — RX is the *slave* and an I2S
351	   slave frames on every WS edge, so there is no one-shot sync to miss.
352	
353	**CONFIRMED REAL but non-causal:** channel-restart orphaning. b79/b80 read
354	`chst 11 resc 1` — a restart really does orphan an in-flight container and #35
355	half 2 really does rescue it. Eliminating it did not fix the stall.
356	
357	🔴 **The `intraw 000000a0` "stale boot state" reading is WITHDRAWN.** The kick
358	writes `DMA_IN_INT_CLR = 0xFFFFFFFF` and `kick 1` proves it ran — yet `intraw`
359	still reads `000000a0` afterwards. Those bits (INFIFO_FULL_WM + INFIFO_UDF_L1)
360	are **continuously re-asserting**: live evidence of persistent RX FIFO
361	starvation, not latched history.
362	
363	Standing signature of the stall, invariant across b76–b80:
364	
365	    i2s eof 0 match 0 miss 0 empty 0  start 2 busy 1     (or eof 1 / start 3)
366	    i2s desc 80000ff0 80000010        owner=1, size 4080, length 0
367	    i2s intraw 000000a0 intena 00000002
368	
369	Owner bit set with zero bytes written = **the DMA is armed and no samples are
370	arriving from the codec.** The remaining suspects are below the DMA — ES8311
371	ADC/clock bring-up or the board's mic path — not the NuttX driver.
372	
373	⚠️ `VELAPAW_I2S_PROBES` lives in the **driver** (`esp32s3_i2s.c:88`), not in
374	`mic.c`. Must be 0 in any shipping build.
375	
376	## 🔴🔴 EVERYTHING BELOW ABOUT b84 CAUSING THE STALL IS FALSIFIED (2026-08-07)
377	
378	**Read this before acting on the b84–b88 section.** b83 — the exact image with
379	six previously-good boots, re-flashed from
380	`velapaw-snapshots\2026-08-07-b83-noaudlog\nuttx-b83-noaudlog.bin`,
381	sha `288649a9…`, esptool "Hash of data verified" — **now fails identically**:
382	
383	    cap FAILED -110 at 152370 / 166940 / 178720 ms   (Recognize taps)
384	    rec 0/54   play 3/3
385	    desc 80000ff0   intraw 000000a0   intena 00000002   chst 11
386	    rxconf 0008972c   txconf 08089204
387	
388	Same binary, same late capture timing that used to work, same fingerprint.
389	**So the fault is not in the app at all.** b84 broke nothing; b85, b86, b87 and
390	b88 were four builds spent against a software regression that does not exist.
391	Do not restart that hunt.
392	
393	What survives from those builds is still true and still useful (b86's separate
394	warm-up budget is a genuine fix, b87 falsified capture timing, b88 proved the
395	session rebuild deadlocks) — but the *premise* that b84 caused the stall is dead.
396	
397	**Where it points instead.** TX runs 3/3 through the same GDMA block, same
398	clock, same peripheral. The only signal unique to the failing direction is the
399	codec's ADC data line into the SoC: `CONFIG_ESP32S3_I2S0_DINPIN=14` (BCLK 13,
400	WS 15, MCLK 12, DOUT 16 — and `esp32s3_st7789.c:411` independently warns that
401	IO12–16 are the codec's I2S bus). Next moves are hardware, not software:
402	bisect what changed physically since the last good b83 boot, then put the FX2
403	logic analyzer on GPIO14 + BCLK + WS during a capture. DIN flat while BCLK/WS
404	toggle ⇒ codec/mic side; DIN toggling ⇒ SoC pad/mux side.
405	
406	⚠️ The `mic stage 38 (close-stop)` hang b88 hit is **not a new bug** — it is
407	already documented at `board/patches/i2s-rx-eof-walk.py:28`: es8311's worker
408	thread cannot terminate while it holds stranded buffers, so the `pthread_join`
409	inside `AUDIOIOC_STOP` never returns. A symptom of the stall, not a cause.
410	
411	## b84–b87: WHO arms the mic, and WHEN the first capture happens
412	
413	**b84 removed the Recognize tab's voice arming** — it was a second, spoken
414	feeding path (`voice_apply()` → `velapaw_feeder_dispense()`) that contradicted
415	Model B (scheduled time **AND** recognised pet). Confirmed gone on hardware.
416	Since b84 the **meal dialog is the only thing that ever opens the audio
417	device**, and `voice_apply`, `voice_idle_text`, `g_voice_lbl`,
418	`g_voice_dismissed/hold/shown` are all deleted.
419	
420	That removal exposed two things Recognize had been providing **by accident**:
421	
422	1. **Readiness.** `vsched_tick()` will not prompt until `g_voice_ready`, set in
423	   exactly one place — after a capture **succeeds**. Standing on Recognize had
424	   always supplied that long before the dialog opened. b85 restores it with a
425	   boot warm-up (unarmed captures, result discarded).
426	2. **Unlimited retries.** b85 fed those warm-up failures into the shared
427	   `g_voice_consec`, and `VOICE_MAX_CAPFAIL 3` latches `g_voice_fail` and
428	   `return NULL` — **the worker thread exits and voice is dead for the boot.**
429	   b85 therefore burned the whole budget at boot and was *worse* than b83.
430	   **b86 gives the warm-up its own counter** (`g_voice_warmfail`) that never
431	   touches `g_voice_consec`, retrying forever with backoff (200 ms ×5, 2 s ×10,
432	   then 10 s). Armed/dialog captures keep the old budget.
433	
434	### What b86 proved: retrying within a boot CANNOT recover
435	
436	19 warm-up captures over 217 s, every one `-110`, hardware state **bit-identical
437	each time** and identical to b78/b79/b80:
438	
439	    rec 0/342  play 19/19      342 RX buffers in, none back; TX 19/19 fine
440	    desc 80000ff0              owner 1, length 0
441	    intraw 000000a0            INFIFO_FULL_WM + INFIFO_UDF_L1, RE-RAISED after
442	                               every kick's INT_CLR -> live starvation
443	    intena 00000002            IN_SUC_EOF enabled, never fires
444	    mickick 19 ok 0  resc 19  start 20
445	
446	TX completing 19/19 through the same GDMA proves the clock runs and the block's
447	EOF path works — **it is specifically the RX channel that never fills.**
448	
449	⚠️ **Two of my own readings here were WRONG — don't repeat them.**
450	`velapaw_i2s_rx_kick()` **does** drain `rx.act` (`while (!sq_empty(&rx.act))
451	sq_addfirst(sq_remlast(...), &rx.pend)`) and then `i2s_rxdma_start()` re-arms
452	one immediately — so `act 1 pend 1` after a kick is the kick **working**, not
453	failing. And **nothing in the UI ever closed the session in b83 either**:
454	`velapaw_mic_shutdown()` is called only from `velapaw_main.c`'s
455	`velapaw kws mic` CLI path, never from `ui_lvgl.c`.
456	
457	### The live hypothesis (b87): the FIRST capture decides, and b84 moved it
458	
459	`velapaw_mic_preopen()` opens one session at boot and **nothing ever closes
460	it**, so once that stream wedges every later capture inherits it — the kick
461	resets GDMA + I2S RX but never the ES8311.
462	
463	    b83 and earlier   first capture when the owner tapped Recognize, tens of
464	                      seconds in, board settled            -> 6 good boots
465	    b85 / b86         first capture at ~13.1 s -- mid TFLM model reads, camera
466	                      bring-up, the 5350 ms pre-open       -> 0 good boots
467	
468	**b87 holds unarmed captures until `VOICE_WARMUP_AT_MS` (30 s) after power-on**,
469	tested against `mono_ms()` (monotonic from boot). Armed captures are *not*
470	delayed. Falsifiable: the vlog shows either nothing (warm-up succeeded) or
471	`warmup FAILED -110 (#1)` at ~33 s — and if it fails at 33 s exactly as at 16 s,
472	**timing is not the variable** and the next move is rebuilding the session
473	(close both fds, re-open, which is the only thing that re-runs ES8311
474	configure). b80 removed that path because `mic_session_close()` hung, but that
475	predates b79's fix of the collect hang.
476	
477	Build chain, all esptool hash-verified on-chip:
478	`b83 288649a9` → `b84 a0860dee` → `b85 ec7c1d4d` → `b86 1666c029` →
479	`b87 95a383ed`. Console fix: [[velapaw-console-blocking]].
480	
481	## ✅ SOLVED: the `es8311 -22` boot spam is cosmetic — never chase it
482	
483	    es8311_getcoeff: MCLK = 4096000 and samplerate = 48000 not supported
484	    es8311_setsamplerate: Failed to set sample rate: -22
485	
486	The driver does it to itself. `es8311.c:2153` sets
487	`priv->samprate = ES8311_DEFAULT_SAMPRATE` (48000), then `:2191` calls
488	`es8311_setsamplerate()` during init while MCLK is 4096000 (= 256 × 16000).
489	`getcoeff(4096000, 48000)` has no table entry → `-22`. The real rate is
490	programmed later from `caps->ac_controls.hw[0]`, and `:1039` already calls
491	`es8311_reset()` *before* `:1046`'s `setsamplerate()`. **It appears in working
492	boots too**, so its presence in a failing log means nothing. This misled a
493	third-party analysis into proposing an ES8311 power-up clock race; that was
494	rejected on evidence.
495	
496	## Session shape
497	
498	Open, configure, `AUDIOIOC_START` **once**; each capture only enqueues and
499	collects. Between captures the session is running but idle. Free-running RX is
500	not an option: `mq_maxmsg = nbuffers + 8`, so with no reader the driver's
501	`mq_send` would drop buffer pointers. `mic_flush_mq()` before each re-arm.
502	
503	⚠️ **`apb->nbytes` is read by the driver *during* the enqueue ioctl** — the
504	caller sets it: record side `0`, playback side `nmaxbytes`. Zeroing it in a
505	shared helper silently sends a zero-length TX buffer → no clock → hang. TX
506	must stay primed; RX borrows BCLK/WS from TX (see [[velapaw-audio-bringup]]).
507	
508	⚠️ Do not conflate this with the falsified theory above. A **zero-length first**
509	TX buffer means `I2S_TX_START` is never set, so the clock never starts — real.
510	TX **draining after** a good buffer is harmless, because `TX_START` stays set
511	and `#16` cleared `TX_STOP_EN`.
512	
513	## Measurement, not ears
514	
515	`velapaw_mic_stats()` prints `peak N@index`, `rms`, `dc`, `rail` and an
516	8-segment peak profile. Reference at 30 dB, build 52, de-interleaved:
517	
518	    silence  rms  26  profile    87    82    87    68    55    67    56    60
519	    "yes"    rms 645  profile   447    90   107   100  4085  5019  1426  1724
520	    "no"     rms 791  profile  1949  5402  3534   596    74    66    87    94
521	
522	`MIC_TRACE` (default 0) prints one line per buffer with the `apb` pointer and
523	four samples — the check on both fixes at once: pointers must all be distinct,
524	`s` must alternate live/0. Turn it on for any future capture regression.
525	Do **not** read a full-scale spike at a fixed index as clipping — that is the
526	start-of-stream transient, see [[velapaw-audio-gain]].

Nowhere, right now. That's the honest answer, and it's worth being precise about because the boot log has a line that looks like it says otherwise.

Three separate things get called "voice" in this project:

1. **The on-device spoken dialog** (`My Pets → Edit`, MEAL→HOUR→CONFIRM). This *did* work — b81, 2026-08-07, `COMMIT meal 1 = 09:00`. It is **dead on this board**: a hash-verified known-good Aug 7 image fails today, which is why the verdict in `velapaw-mic-capture.md` is hardware (RX DMA armed, owner bit set, zero bytes arriving from the codec). Not recoverable in software.
2. **`set_meal_schedule` via `ask`** — what we just shipped and verified. That's **typed text** at the `vela>` prompt. No speech anywhere in that path.
3. **`[agent] voice_channel_init (rc=0)`** in the boot log — that's an ai_agent subsystem initialising, not evidence of a working mic.

Let me pin down what #3 actually is rather than guess.

Understood — voice in, agent sets the meal. One constraint to state once and then work around: the board's microphone is hardware-dead (`velapaw-mic-capture.md`, verdict 2026-09-22 — a hash-verified known-good image fails on this board, RX DMA armed with zero bytes arriving from the codec). So the speech cannot be captured *by the board*. Everything after capture is available.

That leaves one working shape: **capture and transcribe on the host, feed the text into the agent over a transport it already has, and let `set_meal_schedule` do the rest.** The agent is already listening — `[ws] WebSocket server started on port 28789` — and it's already reachable at 192.168.137.2. So "speak a meal time, the feeder schedules it" works end to end, with the mic on the PC instead of the board.

Before I write any of it I need to know what the agent's existing input paths actually accept — in particular whether `voice_channel` is already built for this. From the VM:

```bash
cd ~/openvela/packages/ai_agent
ls src/core src/channels 2>/dev/null
grep -rn "voice_channel" --include=*.c --include=*.h src/ | head -40
grep -rn "28789" --include=*.c --include=*.h src/ | head -20
```

Paste that and I'll tell you whether we're writing a new channel or just filling in one that's already wired.

That changes the plan — we're not writing a voice channel, there already is one, and it's cloud ASR/TTS, not the dead on-device KWS model:

| | |
|---|---|
| `voice_channel_start()` | begin recording |
| `voice_channel_stop_with_text()` | stop and **return the transcript** |
| `voice_channel_speak()` | TTS reply |
| `voice_channel_test_asr(pcm_path)` | **transcribe a PCM file from disk** |

`src/ui/lvgl_ui_channel.c:712`/`:734` already does start → stop_with_text, so speech→text→agent is wired. And `test_asr` taking a *file path* is the opening: it's ASR with no microphone in the loop at all, which is exactly the hole the dead mic leaves.

So the question is no longer "how do we build this" but "which of these two paths touches the broken hardware." `start()` almost certainly opens the same ES8311/I²S capture that's dead; the file path doesn't.

Four things to confirm:

```bash
cd ~/openvela/packages/ai_agent
sed -n '1,90p' src/voice/voice_channel.c
grep -n '"/dev/\|AUDIO_\|AUDIOIOC\|pcm\|16000' src/voice/voice_channel.c | head -40
sed -n '1198,1232p' src/voice/voice_channel.c
sed -n '705,765p' src/ui/lvgl_ui_channel.c
```

I'm looking for: which device `start()` opens, who the ASR provider is and whether its key is configured, whether `test_asr` just prints the transcript or actually injects it into the agent loop, and how the UI hands `asr_text` to the agent. That tells us whether the shortest route is "host records → board transcribes the file → agent schedules the meal."

That's the whole chain already built, and it tells us exactly where the one broken link is.

`src/ui/lvgl_ui_channel.c` does: record → `voice_channel_stop_with_text()` → build an `agent_msg_t` on channel `lvgl_ui` → publish to the bus → agent loop → tools. So **voice → transcript → agent → `set_meal_schedule` is already wired end to end.** The ASR is cloud (Volcano Engine — `volc_asr.h`/`volc_tts.h`), not the dead on-device KWS model. The only thing that touches broken hardware is the capture inside `voice_channel_start()` → `audio_capture` → ES8311/I²S.

And there's a bypass sitting right there: `voice_channel_test_asr(pcm_path)` reads a **PCM file** (`read_pcm_file()` at :228) and runs it through the same `voice_asr_recognize()` the microphone path uses.

So the plan is: **host records the speech → the PCM lands on the board's `/data` → the board transcribes it with its own ASR → the transcript goes onto the bus exactly as the mic's would → the agent calls `set_meal_schedule`.** Only the source of the bytes differs from production; every line of product code after capture is the real one.

Four unknowns stand between here and that, all checkable:

```bash

grep -n "WGET\|WEBCLIENT\|TFTP\|NFS" ~/openvela/nuttx/.config
```

What each one decides:

1. **Does `asr_file_worker` publish its transcript to the message bus, or only `printf` it?** If it publishes, `voice_test_asr /data/meal.pcm` *is* the feature. If it prints, we add ~10 lines copied from the UI channel's publish block.
2. The exact CLI command names and arg forms.
3. PCM format to record on the host — expecting 16 kHz mono s16le.
4. Whether Volcano ASR needs credentials we haven't set (and the config key names — I won't read `config.json`, the API key is in it).
5. Whether the board can pull the file over HTTP at all. A `wget` builtin makes the transfer one line; without it we need another route onto littlefs.

`asr_file_worker` ends with `message_bus_push_inbound(&msg)` on channel `AGENT_CHAN_VOICE`. That's the answer: **voice→agent→meal needs no new code at all.** A PCM file in, a transcript on the bus, the agent loop picks it up and calls `set_meal_schedule` exactly as it did for your typed `ask`.

And you don't need the host mic for the first proof, because the board can make the audio itself:

```
voice_test_tts "Set Bob's lunch to 11:30" /data/meal.pcm
```
wait for it to finish, then

```
voice_test_asr /data/meal.pcm
```

That runs the real chain — Volcano ASR → `message_bus_push_inbound` → agent loop → `set_meal_schedule` → flash — with no microphone anywhere in it. Expect `ASR: recognizing N bytes`, `ASR result: …`, `Sent to agent.`, then the familiar `[agent] Tool call: set_meal_schedule`. I picked 11:30 because the current state is `07:30 13:00 18:45`, so `status.md` can't give a false pass.

Three failure modes, each with a different meaning:

- **Credentials.** Volcano ASR needs `set_volc_asr <app_id> <token> <cluster>` and TTS needs `set_volc_key <api_key>`. If these were never set, both commands fail at the API, not in our chain. That's a real external dependency — a Volcano Engine (Doubao) account — and it's the one thing that could block this outright.
- **Garbled transcript.** Means a sample-rate mismatch: ASR expects 16000 (`AGENT_VOICE_SAMPLE_RATE`), and volc TTS may emit 24 k. Fixable, and it doesn't indict the chain.
- **`voice_test_asr: command not found`** — the CLI wasn't registered in this build; tell me and I'll check `nsh_commands.c`.

For a **human** voice afterwards, the gap is only file transfer: `CONFIG_NETUTILS_WEBCLIENT is not set`, so nsh `wget` won't work despite `NSH_DISABLE_WGET` being unset. Enabling that one symbol gets you `wget -o /data/meal.pcm http://192.168.137.1:8000/meal.pcm`, with the clip recorded on Windows as 16 kHz mono s16le. One Kconfig symbol and a reflash — but run the TTS loop above first, since it proves the whole path for free.

That reframes it, and in our favour.

`audio_capture.c` includes `<media_recorder.h>` and `CONFIG_MEDIA is not set` — so the `#ifndef CONFIG_MEDIA` gate is deliberate, not a mistake. Voice only links when the Vela media framework is present. The whole `src/voice/` subtree compiles but is never linked, which is why its unresolved `media_*` references have never broken a build.

But here's the thing: **the file-ASR path needs no audio device at all.** `asr_file_worker` → `read_pcm_file()` → `voice_asr_recognize()` → Volcano over TLS. No `media_recorder`, no ES8311, no mic. The media framework is only needed by `voice_channel_start()` (capture, hardware-dead anyway) and `voice_channel_speak()` (playback).

So we don't enable `CONFIG_MEDIA`. We **invert the stub block**: drop the `voice_channel_*` stubs so the real code links, and add weak stubs for the handful of `media_*` functions instead. Result: `voice_test_asr` works for real, and `voice_start`/`speak` fail with `-1` — which is the truth about this board's microphone regardless.

text:
This session is being continued from a previous conversation that ran out of context. The summary below covers the earlier portion of the conversation.

Summary:
1. **Primary Request and Intent**

   The governing intent across this session has been **voice-driven meal scheduling for VelaPaw**. Within this window it progressed through two phases:

   **Phase A (completed):** finish and verify the `set_meal_schedule` agent tool — specifically, flash the use-after-free fix in `tool_meal.c` and prove it corrected the HTTP 400 `invalid unicode code point` rather than merely masking it with the UTF-8 sanitiser.

   **Phase B (active):** the user pivoted with two explicit prose turns:
   - **"but where is voice being used"** — challenging that the shipped feature is typed text, not voice.
   - **"no i want to set the meal times through voice using the agent"** — stated as a rejection reason on a tool call, i.e. an explicit redirection: the goal is speech → agent → meal times set, not typed `ask`.
   - **"what should i do?"** — a request for one directive, not a menu. The standing style signal (from earlier: "so what to do") is: be terse and prescriptive.

2. **Key Technical Concepts**

   - **Build/flash loop.** Build is `./build.sh esp32s3-devkit:waveshare_lcd -j4` from `~/openvela`. Stale-dep traps cleared first: `rm -f packages/ai_agent/{Make.dep,.depend,.built}`. Flashing is from **Windows**: `python -m esptool --chip esp32s3 --port COM3 --baud 921600 write-flash 0x0 D:\openVela\nuttx.bin`.
   - **VM→Windows transfer.** VM serves `python3 -m http.server 8000` from `~/openvela/nuttx`; Windows fetches `http://192.168.160.128:8000/nuttx.bin`. VMnet8 (NAT) host = 192.168.160.1, VM = 192.168.160.128. Ethernet 2 (ICS) = 192.168.137.1, board = 192.168.137.2.
   - **Boot pattern (user-dictated).** Power/reset → Enter ×3 → `ifconfig eth0 192.168.137.2 netmask 255.255.255.0 gw 192.168.137.1` → `ai_agent &` → wait for `[netmgr] Network connected: 192.168.137.2` → `ask …`.
   - **Static-archive weak-symbol trap (the central discovery).** `src/stubs.c` compiles weak `voice_channel_*` stubs under `#ifndef CONFIG_MEDIA`. `stubs.o` is pulled into the link for an unrelated symbol (`arm_netinitialize`); its weak definitions then satisfy every `voice_channel_*` reference, so **`voice_channel.o` is never extracted from the archive** — nothing is left undefined to force it. `nm` therefore reports `W`, not `T`, and `volc_asr_*` is absent from the image entirely. This is why `voice_test_asr /data/meal.pcm` printed nothing.
   - **Agent voice architecture (all already built, none of it linked).** `src/voice/voice_channel.c` provides `voice_channel_init/start/stop/stop_with_text/speak/test_tts/test_asr`. Cloud ASR/TTS via **Volcano Engine (Doubao)** — `volc_asr.c`, `volc_tts.c`, `volc_tts_ws.c`, behind the `voice_asr.c`/`voice_tts.c` backend-registry abstraction. `asr_file_worker` (voice_channel.c:1153) reads a PCM file via `read_pcm_file()` (:228), calls `voice_asr_recognize()`, then does `message_bus_push_inbound(&msg)` on `AGENT_CHAN_VOICE` / chat_id `"voice"` and prints `Sent to agent.` — so **file→ASR→agent→`set_meal_schedule` needs no new code**.
   - **Audio format.** `AGENT_VOICE_SAMPLE_RATE 16000`, `AGENT_VOICE_PCM_BUF_SIZE (128 * 1024)` (both in `include/agent_config.h:376,385`).
   - **CLI.** `tokenise()` (nsh_commands.c:87) is plain `strtok(line, " \t\r\n")` — **no quote handling**, so multi-word text cannot reach a handler as one argument. `cmd_ask` works around this by rejoining `argv[1..argc-1]`, which is why `ask set bob's dinner to 18:45` worked unquoted. The `vela>` CLI's line reader also **eats multi-line pastes** — commands must be typed one at a time.
   - **Board file transfer is currently impossible.** `# CONFIG_NETUTILS_WEBCLIENT is not set` and `# CONFIG_NETUTILS_TFTPC is not set`, so nsh `wget` won't work despite `CONFIG_NSH_DISABLE_WGET` being unset (`CONFIG_NSH_WGET_BUFF_SIZE=512`).
   - **On-device KWS voice is hardware-blocked.** `velapaw-mic-capture.md` FINAL VERDICT 2026-09-22 — a hash-verified known-good Aug 7 image fails on this board; RX DMA armed (owner bit set) with zero bytes arriving from the codec. Not fixable in software.
   - **Stale `.o` hazard in this tree.** Object files sit beside sources named e.g. `agent_loop.c.home.king.openvela.packages.ai_agent.o` (and `..._1.o` variants), so a plain `grep -r` can match last build's object rather than source. Use `--include=*.c --include=*.h`.
   - **ARP.** `arp_send: ERROR: arp_wait failed: -110` against the gateway **self-recovers via retry** — confirmed this window with no host-side priming in play.

3. **Files and Code Sections**

   **`packages/ai_agent/src/tools/tool_meal.c`** — the use-after-free fix, flashed and verified this window. `pet` pointed into the cJSON tree that `cJSON_Delete(root)` freed, and all six `switch` branches format it afterwards. Fix copies the name first and repoints `pet`:
   ```c
     char petbuf[64];
     strncpy(petbuf, pet, sizeof(petbuf) - 1);
     petbuf[sizeof(petbuf) - 1] = '\0';
     pet = petbuf;

     int rc = velapaw_meal_set_by_name(pet, slot - 1, minute);
     cJSON_Delete(root);
   ```

   **`packages/ai_agent/src/stubs.c:36-63`** — THE BLOCKER. Read verbatim:
   ```c
   /* Voice channel stubs for sim build */
   #ifndef CONFIG_MEDIA
   __attribute__((weak)) int voice_channel_init(void) { return 0; }
   __attribute__((weak)) int voice_channel_start(void) { return -1; }
   __attribute__((weak)) int voice_channel_stop(void) { return 0; }
   __attribute__((weak)) int voice_channel_speak(const char* text)
   { (void)text; return -1; }
   __attribute__((weak)) int voice_channel_test_tts(const char* text)
   { (void)text; return -1; }
   __attribute__((weak)) int voice_channel_test_asr(void) { return -1; }
   __attribute__((weak)) const char* voice_tts_get_backend(void) { return "none"; }
   __attribute__((weak)) int voice_tts_set_backend(const char* name)
   { (void)name; return -1; }
   __attribute__((weak)) const char* voice_asr_get_backend(void) { return "none"; }
   __attribute__((weak)) int voice_asr_set_backend(const char* name)
   { (void)name; return -1; }
   #endif
   ```
   Followed by an MQTT stub block under `#ifndef CONFIG_NETUTILS_MQTTC`. The stub signatures are **stale**: `voice_channel_test_tts` takes one arg here vs `(text, out_path)` in the real header; `voice_channel_test_asr` takes none vs `(pcm_path)`. That is why `voice_test_asr /data/meal.pcm` ignored its argument and returned −1 silently.

   **`packages/ai_agent/src/voice/voice_channel.c:1153-1226`** — `asr_file_worker` + `voice_channel_test_asr`, verbatim essentials:
   ```c
   static void* asr_file_worker(void* arg)
   {
       asr_task_args_t* a = (asr_task_args_t*)arg;
       unsigned char* pcm = NULL;
       size_t pcm_len = 0;
       int ret = read_pcm_file(a->pcm_path, &pcm, &pcm_len);
       if (ret != 0) { printf("Failed to read %s: %d\n", a->pcm_path, ret); free(a); return NULL; }
       printf("ASR: recognizing %zu bytes from %s ...\n", pcm_len, a->pcm_path);
       char text[512];
       ret = voice_asr_recognize(pcm, pcm_len, text, sizeof(text));
       free(pcm);
       if (ret == 0) {
           printf("ASR result: %s\n", text);
           agent_msg_t msg;
           memset(&msg, 0, sizeof(msg));
           strncpy(msg.channel, AGENT_CHAN_VOICE, sizeof(msg.channel) - 1);
           strncpy(msg.chat_id, "voice", sizeof(msg.chat_id) - 1);
           msg.content = strdup(text);
           if (msg.content) { message_bus_push_inbound(&msg); printf("Sent to agent.\n"); }
       } else { printf("ASR failed: %d\n", ret); }
       free(a);
       return NULL;
   }
   ```

   **`packages/ai_agent/src/voice/audio_capture.c`** — header comment states the direct-ALSA backend is behind `CONFIG_AI_AGENT_AUDIO_ALSA_DIRECT` and the default is "the portable media_recorder backend that works on any board with the Vela media framework". It `#include <media_recorder.h>`. This is the source of the seven unresolved `media_*` symbols.

   **`packages/ai_agent/src/channels/nsh_commands.c`** — `tokenise()` at :87 (plain strtok, no quotes); help strings at :138-144; dispatch entries at :1009-1022, all unconditional; `printf("Unknown command: %s (type 'help')\n", cmd)` at :1078.

   **`packages/ai_agent/src/channels/cmd_voice.c`** — `cmd_set_volc_key`, `cmd_set_volc_speaker`, `cmd_set_volc_asr <app_id> <token> <cluster>`, `cmd_voice_start/stop`, `cmd_voice_test_tts` (defaults output to `AGENT_DATA_DIR "/tts_out.pcm"`), `cmd_voice_test_asr`, `cmd_set_voice_tts`.

   **`packages/ai_agent/src/ui/lvgl_ui_channel.c:705-765`** — the production voice flow: first click `voice_channel_start()`, second click `voice_channel_stop_with_text(asr_text, sizeof(asr_text))` → build `agent_msg_t` with `AGENT_CHAN_LVGL_UI` / chat_id `"lvgl_ui"` → `msg.content = strdup(asr_text)` → push to bus. Proves speech→transcript→agent is already wired.

   **`packages/ai_agent/Makefile`** — `src/channels/cmd_voice.c` at :97; `src/voice/{voice_channel,voice_tts,voice_asr,volc_tts,volc_tts_ws,volc_asr,audio_capture,audio_playback}.c` at :118-126, **all unconditional** (no `ifeq` guard). Same set in `CMakeLists.txt:40,62-69`.

   **`~/openvela/nuttx/.config`** — `# CONFIG_ARCH_SIM is not set` (:148), `# CONFIG_MEDIA is not set` (:2917), `# CONFIG_MEDIA_TRIGGER is not set` (:2918).

   **Memory files updated this window:**
   - `velapaw-agent-meal-scheduling.md` — replaced the "STILL OPEN: HTTP 400" section with "SOLVED: … was a use-after-free", recording the root cause, the 163-vs-151 byte-arithmetic signal, both falsified theories (history truncation; stale over-read of `tool_output`), the wrong `messages[N]` re-indexing, the verified firmware `9242daf64d1c9744f9d1ec917bf13d69` (1563648 B), the four landed writes (07:30 / 13:00 / 19:15 / 18:45), and the instruction to keep the sanitiser but remove the `msg[N]` dump. Description frontmatter updated.
   - `MEMORY.md` — index line updated to mark the 400 as solved.

4. **Errors and fixes**

   - **Firmware hash mismatch (carried in).** VM reported `f3179376…`, the HTTP fetch served `9242daf6…`. **Refused to flash.** Resolved when the user cleared deps, rebuilt, and `md5sum` returned `9242daf64d1c9744f9d1ec917bf13d69` — same as the fetched copy. The earlier hash was simply a superseded build of identical sources.
   - **My own wrong claim about ARP priming.** I wrote that the host ping loop "had it primed" for the successful `ask`. The loop ended 12:34 local; the request's `UNIX=1791717469` is ~13:17 — 45 minutes later. **Corrected explicitly:** the `-110` self-recovered via retry with no host priming. Also noted the loop's `board UP` hits are untrustworthy (`-Quiet` hides the reply source; matches the known VPN ICMP-spoof pattern) and the final neighbour state was `Incomplete`/`Unreachable`.
   - **`voice_test_tts`/`voice_test_asr` silent — three wrong diagnoses before the right one.**
     1. *Commands not registered* — falsified by `help` listing both.
     2. *Help text vs a separate dispatcher* — falsified by the greps: one dispatcher, entries at :1009-1022, unconditional, `Unknown command` at :1078.
     3. *Argument parsing / the apostrophe in `"Bob's"`* — partially right (the first attempt was a two-line paste eaten as one line), but falsified as the whole story when a hand-typed single-token `voice_test_tts Hello /data/meal.pcm` was also silent.
     **Actual root cause:** weak stubs in `src/stubs.c` winning the link by archive position. Found via `nm ~/openvela/nuttx/nuttx` showing `W` for every `voice_channel_*` symbol and `src/stubs.c` in the list of defining files.

<#
    voice_ask.ps1 - speak a meal time, the VelaPaw agent sets it.

    Microphone and speech recognition live here on the PC; the board does the
    reasoning and the flash write. The recognised sentence is sent verbatim to
    the board's console as:

        ask set bob's dinner to 19:15

    which is the path already verified on hardware (agent -> set_meal_schedule
    -> history/identity on flash -> status.md).

    This script IS the terminal while it runs: it prints everything the board
    says and you can type into it, so run the usual boot sequence here rather
    than in PuTTY (only one program may hold the COM port).

        ifconfig eth0 192.168.137.2 netmask 255.255.255.0 gw 192.168.137.1
        ai_agent &

    Then just talk.

    Usage
        .\voice_ask.ps1                       # auto-detect port, listen
        .\voice_ask.ps1 -Port COM3
        .\voice_ask.ps1 -Pets bob,jay
        .\voice_ask.ps1 -DryRun               # grammar only, no port, no board
        .\voice_ask.ps1 -Text "set bob's dinner to 19:15"   # no mic, send once
        .\voice_ask.ps1 -Confirm              # ask y/n before each send
        .\voice_ask.ps1 -ListPorts

    Type 'exit' (then Enter) to quit.

    Phrasing it understands
        "set bob's dinner to seven thirty p m"
        "set jay's breakfast to seven o'clock"
        "set bob's lunch to twelve thirty"
        "set bob's third meal to nineteen fifteen"
    Say the minutes - "to seven" alone is not a complete phrase.
    With no a m / p m, the hour is resolved from the meal (dinner 4-11 -> PM,
    lunch 1-4 -> PM, breakfast as spoken) and the resolved HH:MM is printed
    before it is sent.
#>

[CmdletBinding()]
param(
    [string]   $Port,
    [int]      $Baud    = 115200,
    [string[]] $Pets    = @('bob','jay'),
    [string]   $Text,
    [switch]   $DryRun,
    [switch]   $Confirm,
    [switch]   $ListPorts
)

$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- word tables

$HourWords = [ordered]@{
    'twenty three' = 23; 'twenty two' = 22; 'twenty one' = 21
    'nineteen' = 19; 'eighteen' = 18; 'seventeen' = 17; 'sixteen' = 16
    'fifteen' = 15; 'fourteen' = 14; 'thirteen' = 13; 'twelve' = 12
    'eleven' = 11; 'twenty' = 20; 'ten' = 10; 'nine' = 9; 'eight' = 8
    'seven' = 7; 'six' = 6; 'five' = 5; 'four' = 4; 'three' = 3
    'two' = 2; 'one' = 1
}

$MinuteWords = [ordered]@{
    "o'clock" = 0; 'zero zero' = 0; 'oh five' = 5; 'fifty five' = 55
    'forty five' = 45; 'thirty five' = 35; 'twenty five' = 25
    'fifty' = 50; 'forty' = 40; 'thirty' = 30; 'twenty' = 20
    'fifteen' = 15; 'ten' = 10
}

$MealWords = [ordered]@{
    'breakfast'   = 'breakfast'
    'lunch'       = 'lunch'
    'dinner'      = 'dinner'
    'supper'      = 'dinner'
    'first meal'  = 'first meal'
    'second meal' = 'second meal'
    'third meal'  = 'third meal'
}

# ------------------------------------------------------------------ port setup

function Get-Ports { [System.IO.Ports.SerialPort]::GetPortNames() | Sort-Object }

if ($ListPorts) {
    $p = Get-Ports
    if ($p) { Write-Host ("Serial ports: " + ($p -join ', ')) }
    else    { Write-Host "No serial ports present." }
    return
}

$port = $null
if (-not $DryRun) {
    $available = Get-Ports
    if (-not $available) {
        throw "No serial ports present. Is the board plugged in? (-DryRun works without one.)"
    }
    if (-not $Port) {
        if ($available -contains 'COM3')    { $Port = 'COM3' }
        elseif ($available.Count -eq 1)     { $Port = $available[0] }
        else { throw ("Several ports present (" + ($available -join ', ') + "). Pick one with -Port.") }
    }
    if ($available -notcontains $Port) {
        throw ("$Port does not exist. Present: " + ($available -join ', '))
    }

    $port = New-Object System.IO.Ports.SerialPort $Port, $Baud, 'None', 8, 'One'
    $port.ReadBufferSize  = 65536
    $port.WriteTimeout    = 2000
    $port.NewLine         = "`r`n"
    $port.DtrEnable       = $true
    $port.RtsEnable       = $true
    try { $port.Open() }
    catch { throw "Could not open $Port - close PuTTY (or whatever holds it) and retry. $($_.Exception.Message)" }
    Write-Host "[port] $Port open at $Baud" -ForegroundColor DarkGray
}

function Send-Line([string]$line) {
    if ($DryRun -or -not $port) { Write-Host "[dry-run] would send: $line" -ForegroundColor Yellow; return }
    $port.Write($line + "`r`n")
}

# --------------------------------------------------------------- phrase -> cmd

function Resolve-Hour([int]$hour, [string]$meal, [string]$ampm) {
    if ($ampm -eq 'pm') { if ($hour -lt 12) { return $hour + 12 } else { return $hour } }
    if ($ampm -eq 'am') { if ($hour -eq 12) { return 0 } else { return $hour } }
    if ($hour -gt 12)   { return $hour }          # already 24-hour

    switch -Regex ($meal) {
        'dinner|third'  { if ($hour -ge 4 -and $hour -le 11) { return $hour + 12 } }
        'lunch|second'  { if ($hour -ge 1 -and $hour -le 4)  { return $hour + 12 } }
    }
    return $hour
}

function Match-Leading($table, [string]$s) {
    # longest-first match of a word phrase at the start of $s
    foreach ($k in $table.Keys) {
        if ($s -eq $k -or $s.StartsWith($k + ' ')) {
            return @{ Value = $table[$k]; Rest = $s.Substring([Math]::Min($k.Length + 1, $s.Length)).Trim() }
        }
    }
    return $null
}

function ConvertTo-AskCommand([string]$heard) {
    $s = $heard.ToLower().Trim() -replace '\s+', ' '
    if ($s -notmatch '^set (.+?) to (.+)$') { return $null }
    $who  = $Matches[1].Trim()
    $when = $Matches[2].Trim()

    # pet: first word, with the possessive 's that SAPI hears as a plural
    $parts = $who -split ' ', 2
    if ($parts.Count -lt 2) { return $null }
    $pet = $parts[0]
    if ($Pets -notcontains $pet) {
        $bare = $pet -replace 's$', ''
        if ($Pets -contains $bare) { $pet = $bare } else { return $null }
    }

    $m = Match-Leading $MealWords $parts[1].Trim()
    if (-not $m) { return $null }
    $meal = $m.Value

    $ampm = ''
    if ($when -match '\bp m$|\bpm$') { $ampm = 'pm'; $when = ($when -replace '\bp m$|\bpm$', '').Trim() }
    elseif ($when -match '\ba m$|\bam$') { $ampm = 'am'; $when = ($when -replace '\ba m$|\bam$', '').Trim() }

    $h = Match-Leading $HourWords $when
    if (-not $h) { return $null }
    $mi = Match-Leading $MinuteWords $h.Rest
    if (-not $mi) { return $null }

    $hour = Resolve-Hour -hour $h.Value -meal $meal -ampm $ampm
    if ($hour -lt 0 -or $hour -gt 23) { return $null }

    $hhmm = '{0:00}:{1:00}' -f $hour, $mi.Value
    return [pscustomobject]@{
        Command = "ask set $($pet)'s $meal to $hhmm"
        Pet     = $pet
        Meal    = $meal
        Time    = $hhmm
    }
}

# ------------------------------------------------------------------ -Text mode

if ($Text) {
    Write-Host "> $Text" -ForegroundColor Cyan
    Send-Line $Text
    if ($port) {
        Start-Sleep -Milliseconds 400
        $deadline = (Get-Date).AddSeconds(90)
        while ((Get-Date) -lt $deadline) {
            if ($port.BytesToRead -gt 0) { Write-Host -NoNewline $port.ReadExisting() }
            Start-Sleep -Milliseconds 50
        }
        $port.Close()
    }
    return
}

# -------------------------------------------------------------- speech grammar

Add-Type -AssemblyName System.Speech

$installed = [System.Speech.Recognition.SpeechRecognitionEngine]::InstalledRecognizers()
if (-not $installed -or $installed.Count -eq 0) {
    if ($port) { $port.Close() }
    throw "No SAPI speech recogniser installed. Settings > Time & language > Speech, add the English (United States) speech pack, then retry. -Text still works without a mic."
}
$rec = $installed | Where-Object { $_.Culture.Name -eq 'en-US' } | Select-Object -First 1
if (-not $rec) { $rec = $installed[0] }
$engine = New-Object System.Speech.Recognition.SpeechRecognitionEngine $rec.Id
Write-Host "[asr] $($rec.Description) ($($rec.Culture.Name))" -ForegroundColor DarkGray

function New-Choices([string[]]$words) {
    $c = New-Object System.Speech.Recognition.Choices
    foreach ($w in $words) { $c.Add([string[]]@($w)) }
    return $c
}

$petWords = @()
foreach ($p in $Pets) { $petWords += $p; $petWords += ($p + 's') }

$cPets    = New-Choices $petWords
$cMeals   = New-Choices @($MealWords.Keys)
$cHours   = New-Choices @($HourWords.Keys)
$cMinutes = New-Choices @($MinuteWords.Keys)
$cAmPm    = New-Choices @('a m','p m')

function New-BasePhrase {
    $b = New-Object System.Speech.Recognition.GrammarBuilder
    $b.Append('set')
    $b.Append($cPets)
    $b.Append($cMeals)
    $b.Append('to')
    $b.Append($cHours)
    $b.Append($cMinutes)
    return $b
}

$plain = New-BasePhrase
$withMeridiem = New-BasePhrase
$withMeridiem.Append($cAmPm)

$alts = New-Object System.Speech.Recognition.Choices
$alts.Add([System.Speech.Recognition.GrammarBuilder[]]@($plain, $withMeridiem))

$grammar = New-Object System.Speech.Recognition.Grammar (New-Object System.Speech.Recognition.GrammarBuilder $alts)
$grammar.Name = 'velapaw-meal'
$engine.LoadGrammar($grammar)

# the recognition callback runs in its own runspace, so hand results back
# through a synchronised queue rather than touching script scope
$heardQueue = [System.Collections.Queue]::Synchronized((New-Object System.Collections.Queue))
$null = Register-ObjectEvent -InputObject $engine -EventName SpeechRecognized `
    -MessageData $heardQueue -Action {
        $Event.MessageData.Enqueue([pscustomobject]@{
            Text       = $EventArgs.Result.Text
            Confidence = $EventArgs.Result.Confidence
        })
    }

$engine.SetInputToDefaultAudioDevice()
$engine.RecognizeAsync([System.Speech.Recognition.RecognizeMode]::Multiple)

Write-Host ""
Write-Host "Listening. Pets: $($Pets -join ', ')" -ForegroundColor Green
Write-Host "  e.g. `"set bob's dinner to seven thirty p m`"" -ForegroundColor Green
Write-Host "  type board commands here as usual; 'exit' quits" -ForegroundColor Green
Write-Host ""

# ------------------------------------------------------------------- main loop

$typed = ''
try {
    while ($true) {
        if ($port -and $port.BytesToRead -gt 0) {
            Write-Host -NoNewline $port.ReadExisting()
        }

        while ($heardQueue.Count -gt 0) {
            $h = $heardQueue.Dequeue()
            $conf = [int]($h.Confidence * 100)
            Write-Host ""
            Write-Host "[heard $conf%] $($h.Text)" -ForegroundColor Cyan

            if ($h.Confidence -lt 0.55) {
                Write-Host "[skipped] too uncertain - say it again" -ForegroundColor DarkYellow
                continue
            }
            $cmd = ConvertTo-AskCommand $h.Text
            if (-not $cmd) {
                Write-Host "[skipped] could not read a pet/meal/time out of that" -ForegroundColor DarkYellow
                continue
            }
            Write-Host "[meal] $($cmd.Pet) / $($cmd.Meal) -> $($cmd.Time)" -ForegroundColor Magenta
            Write-Host "> $($cmd.Command)" -ForegroundColor Cyan

            $go = $true
            if ($Confirm) {
                Write-Host -NoNewline "send? [y/N] " -ForegroundColor Yellow
                $k = [Console]::ReadKey($false)
                Write-Host ""
                $go = ($k.KeyChar -eq 'y' -or $k.KeyChar -eq 'Y')
            }
            if ($go) { Send-Line $cmd.Command } else { Write-Host "[not sent]" -ForegroundColor DarkYellow }
        }

        while ([Console]::KeyAvailable) {
            $k = [Console]::ReadKey($true)
            switch ($k.Key) {
                'Enter' {
                    Write-Host ""
                    if ($typed -eq 'exit') { $typed = ''; return }
                    Send-Line $typed
                    $typed = ''
                }
                'Backspace' {
                    if ($typed.Length -gt 0) {
                        $typed = $typed.Substring(0, $typed.Length - 1)
                        Write-Host -NoNewline "`b `b"
                    }
                }
                default {
                    if ($k.KeyChar -and [int]$k.KeyChar -ge 32) {
                        $typed += $k.KeyChar
                        Write-Host -NoNewline $k.KeyChar
                    }
                }
            }
        }

        Start-Sleep -Milliseconds 30
    }
}
finally {
    Write-Host ""
    Write-Host "[stopping]" -ForegroundColor DarkGray
    try { $engine.RecognizeAsyncStop() } catch { }
    Get-EventSubscriber | Where-Object { $_.SourceObject -eq $engine } | Unregister-Event
    try { $engine.Dispose() } catch { }
    if ($port -and $port.IsOpen) { $port.Close() }
}

No. A PowerShell script on a laptop tethered to the feeder over USB serial is a demo prop, not the feature — the owner would be talking to a PC that happens to be wired to a pet feeder. It proves only the agent half, which `ask set bob's dinner to 18:45` already proved today. Good question to stop me on; I was solving for "get audio into the agent" when the requirement is "the owner speaks to the feeder."

Three honest candidates for who holds the microphone:

**The feeder itself** — what the product wants, and what [[velapaw-voice-dialog]] already did end to end (COMMIT meal 2 = 08:00) before the mic died. Blocked on hardware: RX DMA arms, zero bytes arrive from the codec, and a hash-verified known-good image fails on this board. No spare GPIOs for a replacement I²S mic either. Dead end unless the board gets repaired or swapped.

**The owner's phone** — a real product architecture, not a prop: phone captures and transcribes (browser Web Speech API, no API key, no app store), sends the sentence to the feeder's agent, feeder reasons and writes flash. The device keeps the part that matters — agent, schedule, actuation. The phone is just a better microphone than the one that broke. The agent already has a network channel listening on **28789**, so the receiving end mostly exists.

**A PC script** — prop. Already dismissed.

So the path is phone-as-mic, and it has exactly one blocker worth testing: the board currently reaches the network only through USB CDC-NCM and Windows ICS (192.168.137.2), which a phone cannot route to. It needs **WiFi station mode on the same network as the phone**. Per [[velapaw-wifi-station-fix]], `esp_wifi_init()` is fixed, DHCP is enabled, and the one thing never tried is a **real router** — every failure so far was against a Windows Mobile Hotspot or an iPhone hotspot, both of which produced AUTH_EXPIRE/NO_AP_FOUND cycling.

That makes the next step cheap and decisive: associate the board to a real router. If it gets a DHCP lease, phone-as-mic is a day's work on top of a channel that already exists. If it won't associate, voice is off the table for this build and the typed `ask` path is what ships.

Do you have a normal WiFi router here — not a phone or Windows hotspot — that I can give you the `wapi` sequence for?
do i dont have a router which means we go back to feeder itself?

No — a missing router doesn't push us back to the dead mic. **The board can be the access point itself.** The ESP32-S3 does SoftAP, so the feeder publishes its own SSID, your phone joins the feeder directly, and no router is involved at any point. That's also a normal product pattern — most IoT hardware ships exactly this way for setup.

That matters doubly here because every WiFi failure in [[velapaw-wifi-station-fix]] was the board trying to *join* a flaky hotspot and getting AUTH_EXPIRE/NO_AP_FOUND. SoftAP is the other direction entirely — the board sets the auth terms instead of negotiating with someone else's. Different code path, and generally the easier one.

The feeder itself stays blocked: hash-verified known-good image, RX DMA armed, zero bytes from the codec, and no free GPIOs for a replacement I²S mic. That's a repair, not a patch.

One caveat I'd rather state now than discover later: while your phone is joined to the board's AP it has no internet, and browser speech recognition (`webkitSpeechRecognition`) is server-based — it would fail. The way around it is your phone's **own keyboard dictation**, which is on-device and offline on any recent iPhone or on Gboard with the language pack installed: tap the mic on the keyboard, speak, the words land in a text box, the page sends them to the feeder. You still just talk; the transcription happens in hardware you already own that works.

Two cheap reads before anything gets built or flashed — one tells us whether SoftAP and a DHCP server are even in this build, the other tells us what protocol the phone would have to speak to reach the agent:

```bash
cd ~/openvela

echo "=== SoftAP + DHCP server + any HTTP server in this build ==="
grep -nE "CONFIG_ESP32S3_WIFI|CONFIG_WAPI|SOFTAP|CONFIG_NETUTILS_DHCPD|CONFIG_NETUTILS_WEBSERVER|CONFIG_NETUTILS_HTTPD|CONFIG_NET_TCP=|CONFIG_WIRELESS=" nuttx/.config

echo "=== what is listening on 28789 ==="
grep -rn --include=*.c --include=*.h "28789" packages/ai_agent/src packages/ai_agent/include | head -20

echo "=== and how that channel speaks (websocket? raw tcp? http?) ==="
ls packages/ai_agent/src/channels/
```

If `CONFIG_NETUTILS_DHCPD` is off, the phone joins the AP and sits there with no address — that's the one symbol most likely to be missing, and it's a Kconfig flip rather than new code. And if 28789 turns out to be a raw TCP line protocol rather than a WebSocket, the phone page gets simpler, not harder.

Read it. It changes my confidence in SoftAP from "probably easier" to "the failures on record are specifically the half SoftAP doesn't do."

**What the memory establishes as fixed:** `esp_wifi_init()` works (`CONFIG_PTHREAD_MUTEX_TYPES=y`, 5+ clean boots), the driver brings up (`pp rom version:` / `net80211 rom version:`), and the `ifup wlan0`-before-`wapi essid` ordering bug is solved. The radio is alive — one association reached RSSI −33 dBm on a home SSID.

**What's still broken, and why it's the supplicant half:** the patched `esp_evt_work_cb()` surfaces `reason=2` (`WIFI_REASON_AUTH_EXPIRE`) at real RSSI (−45 to −51), immediately followed by `reason=201`/`205` at −128, cycling ~5× before giving up. Reason 2 is sent *by the AP* when it doesn't recognise us as previously authenticated — the WPA2 4-way handshake never completes, so there's never an L2 link and DHCP has nothing to run on (`netlib_obtain_ipv4addr() failed` even at `ESSID_ON` / `Sense: −48`). Power-save is ruled out (`CONFIG_ESP32S3_POWER_SAVE_NONE=y`). Both APs tried were software hotspots.

**In SoftAP the board is the authenticator, not the supplicant.** It never calls `esp_wifi_connect()`, never polls `g_sta_connected`, never runs the scan/reconnect logic that loses the AP at −128, and never waits on another device's handshake timing. Every recorded failure mode is in code SoftAP doesn't execute. That's not a guarantee, but it's the opposite of a coin flip — and it explains why no router is actually the blocker it looked like.

Two things the memory also hands us:

- **The uplink survives.** eth0 (CDC-NCM → ICS, 192.168.137.2) stays up independently of the radio, so the board keeps its internet path to DeepSeek while wlan serves the phone on a different subnet. No forwarding needed — the board talks out via eth0, the phone talks in via wlan. That's the whole architecture, on two interfaces that don't contend.
- **The Kconfig pain is known and has a shape.** `make olddefconfig` is broken on this tree, so `kconfig-tweak` writes `.config` directly and every dependent symbol must be set by hand. The DHCPC precedent is the warning: a missing `PROGNAME` default corrupted the builtin-app `-Dmain=` macro and surfaced as a nonsense C syntax error (`int int(...)`) in a file that was perfectly correct. Expect the same for `CONFIG_NETUTILS_DHCPD` — the phone needs an address when it joins, and DHCPC (client) being enabled does nothing for that.

One correction to what I said earlier: `wapi mode wlan0 3` is not the command. On esp32s3 the AP is a **separate netdev** (typically `wlan1`), gated by a Kconfig *choice* — `CONFIG_ESP32S3_WIFI_STATION` vs `_SOFTAP` vs `_STATION_SOFTAP_COEXISTENCE`. That output changes the economics, and the key line is the one that *didn't* print: `CONFIG_ESP32S3_WIFI=` matched nothing, and all three mode symbols are unset. **WiFi isn't disabled-in-station-mode — it's absent from this firmware entirely.** The fix from [[velapaw-wifi-station-fix]] lives in the golden snapshot; the shipping config dropped the whole subsystem when networking moved to USB CDC-NCM.

So SoftAP is no longer a config flip. It's: enable `CONFIG_ESP32S3_WIFI` from zero, pick the AP mode choice, add `CONFIG_NETUTILS_DHCPD` with every dependent symbol by hand (`olddefconfig` is broken here, and the DHCPC precedent says a missing `PROGNAME` default surfaces as a bogus `int int(...)` syntax error), then survive the internal-SRAM hit — WiFi wants ~40 KB of exactly the memory this app already fights for via the PSRAM-stack fix in [[velapaw-ai-agent-psram-stack-freeze]]. On a radio that has never once completed a DHCP lease on this board. That's a multi-day gamble, not an evening.

The better news is in the other half of the output: **`ws_server.c` exists, and `AGENT_WS_PORT 28789` is a WebSocket server.** A browser page can talk to that directly — which means the phone-as-mic UI has a receiving end already written.

And there's a transport that needs no WiFi on the board at all. You have no router because the host's internet comes from your iPhone hotspot — which means **the phone and the Windows host are already on the same L2 network**. So: phone → hotspot LAN → Windows host → ICS port-forward 28789 → board `eth0` 192.168.137.2 → agent. Zero firmware change, zero rebuild. ICS does the forwarding natively (ncpa.cpl → shared adapter → Sharing → Settings → add a TCP 28789 service mapping), so there's no helper process in the path — the host acts as the router that a real deployment would have.

That's the one to do first. It proves phone → transcript → agent → `set_meal_schedule` → flash end to end, and leaves only the radio unproven. If it works and there's time before the deadline, Route 2 (SoftAP) becomes a pure transport swap — same page, different IP.

    int received = 0;

{
    client_arg_t ca = *(client_arg_t*)arg;

kill -9 38
```

net_test
```

`net_test` is the discriminator from [[velapaw-ai-agent-iob-sizing]] — a small request that isolates connectivity from payload size, and unlike `ask hello` it isn't cache-poisoned.
