358	writes `DMA_IN_INT_CLR = 0xFFFFFFFF` and `kick 1` proves it ran — yet `intraw`
359	still reads `000000a0` afterwards. Those bits (INFIFO_FULL_WM + INFIFO_UDF_L1)
360	are **continuously re-asserting**: live evidence of persistent RX FIFO
361	starvation, not latched history.
362	
363	Standing signature of the stall, invariant across b76–b80:
364	
365	    i2s eof 0 match 0 miss 0 empty 0  start 2 busy 1     (or eof 1 / start 3)
366	    i2s desc 80000ff0 80000010        owner=1, size 4080, length 0
367	    i2s intraw 000000a0 intena 00000002
368	
369	Owner bit set with zero bytes written = **the DMA is armed and no samples are
370	arriving from the codec.** The remaining suspects are below the DMA — ES8311
371	ADC/clock bring-up or the board's mic path — not the NuttX driver.
372	
373	⚠️ `VELAPAW_I2S_PROBES` lives in the **driver** (`esp32s3_i2s.c:88`), not in
374	`mic.c`. Must be 0 in any shipping build.
375	
376	## 🔴🔴 EVERYTHING BELOW ABOUT b84 CAUSING THE STALL IS FALSIFIED (2026-08-07)
377	
378	**Read this before acting on the b84–b88 section.** b83 — the exact image with
379	six previously-good boots, re-flashed from
380	`velapaw-snapshots\2026-08-07-b83-noaudlog\nuttx-b83-noaudlog.bin`,
381	sha `288649a9…`, esptool "Hash of data verified" — **now fails identically**:
382	
383	    cap FAILED -110 at 152370 / 166940 / 178720 ms   (Recognize taps)
384	    rec 0/54   play 3/3
385	    desc 80000ff0   intraw 000000a0   intena 00000002   chst 11
386	    rxconf 0008972c   txconf 08089204
387	
388	Same binary, same late capture timing that used to work, same fingerprint.
389	**So the fault is not in the app at all.** b84 broke nothing; b85, b86, b87 and
390	b88 were four builds spent against a software regression that does not exist.
391	Do not restart that hunt.
392	
393	What survives from those builds is still true and still useful (b86's separate
394	warm-up budget is a genuine fix, b87 falsified capture timing, b88 proved the
395	session rebuild deadlocks) — but the *premise* that b84 caused the stall is dead.
396	
397	**Where it points instead.** TX runs 3/3 through the same GDMA block, same
398	clock, same peripheral. The only signal unique to the failing direction is the
399	codec's ADC data line into the SoC: `CONFIG_ESP32S3_I2S0_DINPIN=14` (BCLK 13,
400	WS 15, MCLK 12, DOUT 16 — and `esp32s3_st7789.c:411` independently warns that
401	IO12–16 are the codec's I2S bus). Next moves are hardware, not software:
402	bisect what changed physically since the last good b83 boot, then put the FX2
403	logic analyzer on GPIO14 + BCLK + WS during a capture. DIN flat while BCLK/WS
404	toggle ⇒ codec/mic side; DIN toggling ⇒ SoC pad/mux side.
405	
406	⚠️ The `mic stage 38 (close-stop)` hang b88 hit is **not a new bug** — it is
407	already documented at `board/patches/i2s-rx-eof-walk.py:28`: es8311's worker
408	thread cannot terminate while it holds stranded buffers, so the `pthread_join`
409	inside `AUDIOIOC_STOP` never returns. A symptom of the stall, not a cause.
410	
411	## b84–b87: WHO arms the mic, and WHEN the first capture happens
412	
413	**b84 removed the Recognize tab's voice arming** — it was a second, spoken
414	feeding path (`voice_apply()` → `velapaw_feeder_dispense()`) that contradicted
415	Model B (scheduled time **AND** recognised pet). Confirmed gone on hardware.
416	Since b84 the **meal dialog is the only thing that ever opens the audio
417	device**, and `voice_apply`, `voice_idle_text`, `g_voice_lbl`,
418	`g_voice_dismissed/hold/shown` are all deleted.
419	
420	That removal exposed two things Recognize had been providing **by accident**:
421	
422	1. **Readiness.** `vsched_tick()` will not prompt until `g_voice_ready`, set in
423	   exactly one place — after a capture **succeeds**. Standing on Recognize had
424	   always supplied that long before the dialog opened. b85 restores it with a
425	   boot warm-up (unarmed captures, result discarded).
426	2. **Unlimited retries.** b85 fed those warm-up failures into the shared
427	   `g_voice_consec`, and `VOICE_MAX_CAPFAIL 3` latches `g_voice_fail` and
428	   `return NULL` — **the worker thread exits and voice is dead for the boot.**
429	   b85 therefore burned the whole budget at boot and was *worse* than b83.
430	   **b86 gives the warm-up its own counter** (`g_voice_warmfail`) that never
431	   touches `g_voice_consec`, retrying forever with backoff (200 ms ×5, 2 s ×10,
432	   then 10 s). Armed/dialog captures keep the old budget.
433	
434	### What b86 proved: retrying within a boot CANNOT recover
435	
436	19 warm-up captures over 217 s, every one `-110`, hardware state **bit-identical
437	each time** and identical to b78/b79/b80:
438	
439	    rec 0/342  play 19/19      342 RX buffers in, none back; TX 19/19 fine
440	    desc 80000ff0              owner 1, length 0
441	    intraw 000000a0            INFIFO_FULL_WM + INFIFO_UDF_L1, RE-RAISED after
442	                               every kick's INT_CLR -> live starvation
443	    intena 00000002            IN_SUC_EOF enabled, never fires
444	    mickick 19 ok 0  resc 19  start 20
445	
446	TX completing 19/19 through the same GDMA proves the clock runs and the block's
447	EOF path works — **it is specifically the RX channel that never fills.**
448	
449	⚠️ **Two of my own readings here were WRONG — don't repeat them.**
450	`velapaw_i2s_rx_kick()` **does** drain `rx.act` (`while (!sq_empty(&rx.act))
451	sq_addfirst(sq_remlast(...), &rx.pend)`) and then `i2s_rxdma_start()` re-arms
452	one immediately — so `act 1 pend 1` after a kick is the kick **working**, not
453	failing. And **nothing in the UI ever closed the session in b83 either**:
454	`velapaw_mic_shutdown()` is called only from `velapaw_main.c`'s
455	`velapaw kws mic` CLI path, never from `ui_lvgl.c`.
456	
457	### The live hypothesis (b87): the FIRST capture decides, and b84 moved it
458	
459	`velapaw_mic_preopen()` opens one session at boot and **nothing ever closes
460	it**, so once that stream wedges every later capture inherits it — the kick
461	resets GDMA + I2S RX but never the ES8311.
462	
463	    b83 and earlier   first capture when the owner tapped Recognize, tens of
464	                      seconds in, board settled            -> 6 good boots
465	    b85 / b86         first capture at ~13.1 s -- mid TFLM model reads, camera
466	                      bring-up, the 5350 ms pre-open       -> 0 good boots
467	
468	**b87 holds unarmed captures until `VOICE_WARMUP_AT_MS` (30 s) after power-on**,
469	tested against `mono_ms()` (monotonic from boot). Armed captures are *not*
470	delayed. Falsifiable: the vlog shows either nothing (warm-up succeeded) or
471	`warmup FAILED -110 (#1)` at ~33 s — and if it fails at 33 s exactly as at 16 s,
472	**timing is not the variable** and the next move is rebuilding the session
473	(close both fds, re-open, which is the only thing that re-runs ES8311
474	configure). b80 removed that path because `mic_session_close()` hung, but that
475	predates b79's fix of the collect hang.
476	
477	Build chain, all esptool hash-verified on-chip:
478	`b83 288649a9` → `b84 a0860dee` → `b85 ec7c1d4d` → `b86 1666c029` →
479	`b87 95a383ed`. Console fix: [[velapaw-console-blocking]].
480	
481	## ✅ SOLVED: the `es8311 -22` boot spam is cosmetic — never chase it
482	
483	    es8311_getcoeff: MCLK = 4096000 and samplerate = 48000 not supported
484	    es8311_setsamplerate: Failed to set sample rate: -22
485	
486	The driver does it to itself. `es8311.c:2153` sets
487	`priv->samprate = ES8311_DEFAULT_SAMPRATE` (48000), then `:2191` calls
488	`es8311_setsamplerate()` during init while MCLK is 4096000 (= 256 × 16000).
489	`getcoeff(4096000, 48000)` has no table entry → `-22`. The real rate is
490	programmed later from `caps->ac_controls.hw[0]`, and `:1039` already calls
491	`es8311_reset()` *before* `:1046`'s `setsamplerate()`. **It appears in working
492	boots too**, so its presence in a failing log means nothing. This misled a
493	third-party analysis into proposing an ES8311 power-up clock race; that was
494	rejected on evidence.
495	
496	## Session shape
497	
498	Open, configure, `AUDIOIOC_START` **once**; each capture only enqueues and
499	collects. Between captures the session is running but idle. Free-running RX is
500	not an option: `mq_maxmsg = nbuffers + 8`, so with no reader the driver's
501	`mq_send` would drop buffer pointers. `mic_flush_mq()` before each re-arm.
502	
503	⚠️ **`apb->nbytes` is read by the driver *during* the enqueue ioctl** — the
504	caller sets it: record side `0`, playback side `nmaxbytes`. Zeroing it in a
505	shared helper silently sends a zero-length TX buffer → no clock → hang. TX
506	must stay primed; RX borrows BCLK/WS from TX (see [[velapaw-audio-bringup]]).
507	
508	⚠️ Do not conflate this with the falsified theory above. A **zero-length first**
509	TX buffer means `I2S_TX_START` is never set, so the clock never starts — real.
510	TX **draining after** a good buffer is harmless, because `TX_START` stays set
511	and `#16` cleared `TX_STOP_EN`.
512	
513	## Measurement, not ears
514	
515	`velapaw_mic_stats()` prints `peak N@index`, `rms`, `dc`, `rail` and an
516	8-segment peak profile. Reference at 30 dB, build 52, de-interleaved:
517	
518	    silence  rms  26  profile    87    82    87    68    55    67    56    60
519	    "yes"    rms 645  profile   447    90   107   100  4085  5019  1426  1724
520	    "no"     rms 791  profile  1949  5402  3534   596    74    66    87    94
521	
522	`MIC_TRACE` (default 0) prints one line per buffer with the `apb` pointer and
523	four samples — the check on both fixes at once: pointers must all be distinct,
524	`s` must alternate live/0. Turn it on for any future capture regression.
525	Do **not** read a full-scale spike at a fixed index as clipping — that is the
526	start-of-stream transient, see [[velapaw-audio-gain]].

This session is being continued from a previous conversation that ran out of context. The summary below covers the earlier portion of the conversation.

Summary:
1. **Primary Request and Intent**

   The governing intent this whole window has been **voice-driven meal scheduling for VelaPaw** — specifically the user's standing redirection from a prior window: *"no i want to set the meal times through voice using the agent."* Within this window the intent moved through four distinct phases, driven by explicit user turns:

   - **Phase A — find a second on-board ASR backend.** Answering my credentials question, the user chose **"No — check for another on-board backend first."**
   - **Phase B — rejection of PC-side voice.** The user rejected my `voice_ask.ps1` write with the reason **"will the user use voice to schedule?"** — i.e. the requirement is that the *owner speaks to the feeder*, not that audio reaches the agent by any means. I conceded the script was a demo prop.
   - **Phase C — phone-as-mic, and the no-router question.** The user asked **"do i dont have a router which means we go back to feeder itself?"** then **"look into memory about wifi"**. This produced the SoftAP idea, then the discovery that WiFi is absent from the firmware entirely, then the pivot to the already-linked WebSocket server on port 28789, then a written phone/browser UI, then live debugging of a `code 1006` failure.
   - **Phase D — THE CURRENT INTENT, stated in the final user message: "I think lets make the real mic work."** This is a deliberate pivot back to the on-board microphone, and it overrides my earlier conclusion that on-board voice was out on three grounds. I have not yet responded to it.

2. **Key Technical Concepts**

   - **Static-archive weak-symbol trap** (carried in, now moot): weak `voice_channel_*` stubs in `src/stubs.c` under `#ifndef CONFIG_MEDIA` satisfy every reference, so `voice_channel.o` is never extracted from the archive — `nm` shows `W`, not `T`.
   - **Linker garbage collection masquerading as missing symbols — THE reusable lesson from this window.** `cJSON_AddItemToObject`, `mbedtls_base64_encode`, `sem_post`, `sem_timedwait` are all `T` in the image while their siblings `cJSON_AddObjectToObject`, `mbedtls_base64_decode`, `sem_wait` are absent. Sibling functions live in the same translation unit, so the absences are `--gc-sections` artifacts, not genuine absences; a link that references them pulls them back for free. **`nm` on a linked image tells you what was *retained*, not what's *available*.**
   - **Single ASR backend.** `voice_asr_register` has exactly one caller — `src/voice/volc_asr.c:1105`. Volcano Engine (Doubao) cloud is the only registered backend; `set_voice_asr <name>` has nothing else to select.
   - **WiFi is absent from the shipping firmware.** `CONFIG_ESP32S3_WIFI=` matches nothing in `nuttx/.config`; all three mode symbols (`_WIFI_STATION`, `_WIFI_SOFTAP`, `_WIFI_STATION_SOFTAP`) are unset. `CONFIG_NETUTILS_DHCPD` and `CONFIG_NETUTILS_WEBSERVER` are also unset. `CONFIG_NET_TCP=y`, `CONFIG_WIRELESS=y`, `CONFIG_PTHREAD_MUTEX_TYPES=y`.
   - **SoftAP vs station asymmetry.** Every recorded WiFi failure is supplicant-side (`reason=2` AUTH_EXPIRE at RSSI −45 to −51, then `reason=201`/`205` at −128, cycling ~5×; WPA2 4-way handshake never completes; `netlib_obtain_ipv4addr() failed`). In AP mode the board is the authenticator and never executes that path. Power-save already ruled out (`CONFIG_ESP32S3_POWER_SAVE_NONE=y`). On esp32s3 the AP is a separate netdev (typically `wlan1`) gated by a Kconfig *choice* — `wapi mode wlan0 3` is NOT the command.
   - **The agent's WebSocket server.** `AGENT_WS_PORT 28789`, real RFC6455 (SHA1+base64 accept, `101 Switching Protocols`, `hdr[0] = 0x81` text frames, browser masking XOR'd, ping/pong, 126-extended lengths OK, `plen == 127` 64-bit rejected, `frame_buf[4096]`). Inbound contract: `{"type":"message","content":"…","chat_id":"…"}` — `cJSON_Parse` first, so raw text is silently dropped; `chat_id` buffer is `char chat_id[32]`, defaulting to `ws_<fd>`. Outbound: `{"type":"response","content":"…","chat_id":"…"}`, matched by `find_by_chat_id_locked`, logging `No WS client for chat_id=%s` on miss.
   - **ws_server is already in the flashed firmware**: `420e3cfc T ws_server_start`, `420e3e34 T ws_server_send`, `420e3f84 T ws_server_stop`.
   - **`CONFIG_AI_AGENT_REST_API`, `_NODE`, `_NET_RPMSG` are all unset** — so `api_try_handle` isn't linked (the board cannot serve an HTML page) and `agent_main.c:171` is the live unconditional `ws_server_start()` call site.
   - **https cannot open ws://** — mixed content. The phone UI must be loaded over `http://` or `file://`, which is why it is a local file and not a published Artifact.
   - **Browser speech recognition is server-based** (Chrome and Safari both), so it needs internet. Phone *keyboard* dictation is on-device/offline on recent iPhones and Gboard with the language pack — the offline fallback.
   - **VPN spoofs host-side probes.** `ping` returned TTL=128 at 32 ms (NuttX sends 64; 32 ms over USB is absurd) and `Test-NetConnection` reported `TcpTestSucceeded: True` while a real `TcpClient.Connect` timed out. Host-side probes cannot establish board state with HotspotShield in path.
   - **Dropped SYN vs refused connection** as a diagnostic: a timeout means SYNs are being silently dropped (exhausted TCP slots / backlog), while a missing listener refuses instantly with RST.
   - **Stale `.o` litter** in this tree: objects sit beside sources as e.g. `ws_server.c.home.king.openvela.packages.ai_agent.o` (and `_1.o` variants), so `grep -r` must use `--include=*.c --include=*.h`.

3. **Files and Code Sections**

   - **`packages/ai_agent/src/voice/voice_asr.c`** — the backend registry. Decisive because it proved there is no alternative ASR. `s_backends[VOICE_ASR_MAX_BACKENDS]` at :29, `voice_asr_register` at :33 (requires `ops->name` and `ops->recognize`), "First registered backend becomes the default" at :47, `voice_asr_set_backend` at :58, `voice_asr_get_backend` at :85, `No ASR backend registered` at :96.
   - **`packages/ai_agent/src/voice/volc_asr.c:1105`** — `return voice_asr_register(&s_volc_asr_ops);` — the only registration call in the entire `src/voice/` tree.
   - **`packages/ai_agent/src/channels/ws_server.c`** — the receiving end of the phone UI. Inbound path verbatim:
     ```c
     cJSON* root = cJSON_Parse(frame_buf);
     if (!root) {
         syslog(LOG_WARNING, "[%s] Invalid JSON from fd=%d (%d bytes): %.200s\n",
             TAG, fd, n, frame_buf);
         continue;
     }

     cJSON* type_item = cJSON_GetObjectItem(root, "type");
     cJSON* content_item = cJSON_GetObjectItem(root, "content");

     if (cJSON_IsString(type_item) && strcmp(type_item->valuestring, "message") == 0 && cJSON_IsString(content_item)) {
         cJSON* cid_item = cJSON_GetObjectItem(root, "chat_id");
         ...
         agent_msg_t msg = { 0 };
         strncpy(msg.channel, AGENT_CHAN_WEBSOCKET, sizeof(msg.channel) - 1);
         strncpy(msg.chat_id, chat_id, sizeof(msg.chat_id) - 1);
         msg.content = strdup(content_item->valuestring);
         if (msg.content)
             message_bus_push_inbound(&msg);
     }
     cJSON_Delete(root);
     ```
     Outbound:
     ```c
     cJSON* resp = cJSON_CreateObject();
     cJSON_AddStringToObject(resp, "type", "response");
     cJSON_AddStringToObject(resp, "content", text);
     cJSON_AddStringToObject(resp, "chat_id", chat_id);
     ```
     Also: `client_thread` peeks up to 2048 bytes for `\r\n\r\n`, tries `api_try_handle` under `#ifdef CONFIG_AI_AGENT_REST_API` (not compiled), then `do_ws_handshake_ex`, logging `Handshake failed for fd=%d`; `add_client_locked` failure sends `{0x88,0x00}` and closes.
   - **`packages/ai_agent/src/channels/ws_server.h`** — the whole API is three functions: `ws_server_start(void)`, `ws_server_send(const char *chat_id, const char *text)`, `ws_server_stop(void)`. Header notes code derived from MimiClaw (MIT).
   - **`packages/ai_agent/include/agent_config.h:238`** — `#define AGENT_WS_PORT 28789`.
   - **`packages/ai_agent/src/agent_main.c`** — `ws_server_start()` at :123 (inside `#ifdef CONFIG_AI_AGENT_NET_RPMSG`, dead) and :171 (`if (ws_server_start() != OK) syslog(LOG_WARNING, ...)`, the live unconditional path).
   - **`packages/ai_agent/Makefile:116` / `CMakeLists.txt:42`** — `src/channels/ws_server.c` compiled unconditionally.
   - **`~/openvela/nuttx/.config`** — lines 406–408 all three WiFi modes unset, 714 `CONFIG_PTHREAD_MUTEX_TYPES=y`, 1582 `CONFIG_NET_TCP=y`, 1942 `CONFIG_WIRELESS=y`, 3576 `# CONFIG_NETUTILS_DHCPD is not set`, 3669 `# CONFIG_NETUTILS_WEBSERVER is not set`, 3850 `# CONFIG_AI_AGENT_NODE is not set`, 3853 `# CONFIG_AI_AGENT_NET_RPMSG is not set`, 3858 `# CONFIG_AI_AGENT_REST_API is not set`.
   - **`D:\openVela\host\voice_ask\voice_ask.ps1` — WRITE REJECTED, file does not exist.** ~400-line PowerShell: System.Speech constrained grammar (pet/meal/hour/minute/am-pm `Choices`), hour inference from meal, serial injection to COM3, synchronized queue for the recognition callback. Rejected with "will the user use voice to schedule?"
   - **`D:\openVela\host\phone_mic\velapaw_voice.html` — WRITTEN AND ACCEPTED.** Self-contained, no CDN. Address field defaulting to `192.168.137.2:28789` persisted in localStorage inside try/catch; Connect/Disconnect with a status dot; textarea + Send (Enter sends, Shift+Enter newlines); three tap chips (`set bob's breakfast to 07:30`, `set bob's dinner to 19:15`, `what meals are scheduled?`); transcript bubbles. Sends `ws.send(JSON.stringify({ type: "message", content: text, chat_id: CHAT_ID }))` with `CHAT_ID = "phone"`; renders only `data.type === "response"`. Explicit 1006 message: *"Connection closed before the handshake finished (code 1006). Is ai_agent running, and is eth0 up on the feeder?"*. Notes that the agent sends a placeholder then the real answer. 🎤 button uses `window.SpeechRecognition || window.webkitSpeechRecognition`, and on `ev.error === "network"` tells the user to use keyboard dictation instead. Three-state theme tokens (bare `:root`, `@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark)` guarded by `:root:not([data-theme="light"])`, and `:root[data-theme="dark"]`). Adding this file added `D:\openVela\host\phone_mic` as a working directory.
   - **Memory files read this window:** `velapaw-agent-meal-scheduling.md`, `velapaw-feeding-history-daystamp.md`, `velapaw-wifi-station-fix.md`. **`velapaw-mic-capture.md` was NOT read — the system reported it as too large to include and said to use Read if needed.** That is now the directly relevant file.

4. **Errors and fixes**

   - **My `voice_ask.ps1` write was rejected** with **"will the user use voice to schedule?"** — Fixed by conceding the PC script is a demo prop and reframing around who holds the microphone. This is the most important feedback of the window: solve for *the owner speaking to the feeder*, not for *audio reaching the agent*.
   - **Three "missing" symbols misdiagnosed as needing shims.** I had planned weak stubs for `cJSON_AddObjectToObject`, `mbedtls_base64_decode`, `sem_wait`. The `nm` result showing their siblings as `T` proved they were garbage-collected, not absent — no shims needed.
   - **My claim that `wapi mode wlan0 3` would enable AP mode.** Corrected: AP is a separate netdev gated by a Kconfig choice.
   - **My claim that the phone is the host's hotspot AP.** Corrected from the route table — the host's default route is Wi-Fi via NextHop **10.29.0.1** with DNS 10.3.9.4–6, a real network. I noted this is better for stage 2 (the phone can join the same Wi-Fi) subject to client isolation.
   - **My claim "ai_agent is running and ws_server is bound" from `Test-NetConnection`.** I corrected this explicitly and plainly: TTL=128 cannot come from NuttX, 32 ms over USB is absurd, and a real `TcpClient.Connect` timed out against the port `Test-NetConnection` had just called open. That is the HotspotShield ICMP/TCP spoofing pattern; host probes cannot establish board state with the VPN in path.
   - **`code 1006` × 4 from the browser** — root cause narrowed to two concurrent faults by the `ps`/`ifconfig` paste, not yet fixed:
     1. **Two `ai_agent` instances** (PID 14 group 14 with threads 15/22/23/27/28/29; PID 38 group 38 with threads 39/43). `ai_agent &` was run twice; the second `bind()` fails `EADDRINUSE` and between them TCP slots are consumed, which is why a SYN times out rather than being refused.
     2. **The board has no internet**: `dns_recv_response: ERROR: recv failed: -11` against 192.168.137.1, `[vela_tls] net_connect api.deepseek.com:443 ret=0x52`, `[llm] HTTP call failed in 90s (attempt 3/3)`, `[trace:6acb820835c3b13a] END status=fail iters=1 tools=0 llm_ms=276130 elapsed=276s`, heartbeat reply "Sorry, I encountered an error."
   - **The stopped-NlaSvc ICS trap was ruled out**: `SharedAccess` PID 6380 Running and owning UDP `0.0.0.0:53` and `192.168.137.1:67`; `NlaSvc` and `iphlpsvc` Running/Automatic. Host resolves `api.deepseek.com` → 3.173.21.63 and completes TLS from 10.234.0.31 over `HotspotShield_Wireguard`. So the host half is healthy and the board's `-11` is its own packets not getting serviced.

5. **Problem Solving**

   - **Killed the stub-inversion patch on evidence, not guesswork.** It would have linked fine, but `volc_asr.c` is the only backend, there are no credentials, the mic is dead, and no PCM file can reach `/data` (`CONFIG_NETUTILS_WEBCLIENT` off). Three independent grounds.
   - **Established that no router is not the blocker it appeared to be** — SoftAP means the board is the AP — but then found WiFi is absent from the firmware entirely, making SoftAP a multi-day change (enable `CONFIG_ESP32S3_WIFI` from zero + mode choice + `CONFIG_NETUTILS_DHCPD` with every dependent symbol by hand since `olddefconfig` is broken + ~40 KB internal SRAM hit against the PSRAM-stack fix) on a radio that has never completed a DHCP lease on this board.
   - **Found a zero-firmware-change transport**: `ws_server` is already linked and running, with a real RFC6455 handshake and a reply path, so a browser page can drive the agent directly.
   - **Staged the plan to need no flashing**: (1) host browser → `ws://192.168.137.2:28789`; (2) host-side relay + serving the page over plain http for the phone; (3) phone keyboard dictation.
   - **Open and parked mid-flight:** the `1006` is not yet resolved. The next two board commands — `kill -9 38` then `net_test` — were issued but **never run**, because the user pivoted to the mic.

6. **All user messages**

   - AskUserQuestion answer: **"No — check for another on-board backend first."**

13	**Root cause of the long "vibrates but shaft won't turn" saga:** IN4 on **GPIO44 (U0RXD)** stayed clamped high even after re-asserting `esp32s3_configgpio(pin, OUTPUT)` before every dispense — the UART0 re-mux wins over the GPIO reclaim on that pin. Moving IN4 to **GPIO43 (U0TXD)** fixed it instantly; shaft turns on the first feed.
14	
15	**Second root cause, found 2026-08-02 from the schematic netlist:** the pre-bring-up code had IN1/IN2/IN3 on **GPIO12/13/15**, which are the ES8311 codec's I²S lines and are **not routed to the J8 header at all** (each net has exactly two nodes: ESP32 + codec). So for part of the saga three of the four coils were electrically unconnected — no coil-order table could ever have worked. Moving them to 9/10/11 (the unused microSD pins, the board's only reusable native GPIOs) is what made all four coils real. See [[velapaw-hardware]] for the full J8 map.
16	
17	**Why:** we burned many build/flash cycles chasing coil-order tables. Don't. The straight full-step table `{0x3,0x6,0xC,0x9}` (bit0=IN1..bit3=IN4) is the correct textbook 28BYJ-48 sequence. All 3 distinct coil-order topologies were swept and NONE turned — because the fault was one dead pin (44), not the sequence. A confident external "fix" to `{0x5,0x6,0xA,0x9}` was just re-proposing a sweep candidate we'd already tested.
18	
19	**How to apply:** keep IN4 on GPIO43. `feeder_pins_output()` (configgpio OUTPUT on all four) is still called at the start of `board_feeder_dispense` — harmless, keep it. STEP_PER_REV 2048 full-step, STEP_DELAY_US 3000 (~333 steps/s, within pull-in torque), one-direction ratchet.

A stepper rotates CONTINUOUSLY one direction → pockets ratchet inlet→outlet → true per-pocket dosing, and "grams = pockets × GRAMS_PER_POCKET" becomes literally true. Geared 28BYJ-48 also has strong low-speed torque (resists kibble jams).

42	- Board: ESP32-S3-Touch-LCD-3.5-C (camera+case included).

49	## Pinout — VERIFIED against the official ESP32-S3-Touch-LCD-3.5 schematic netlist (2026-08-02)
50	Native GPIO map:
51	- LCD (ST7796 SPI): IO1 MOSI, **IO3 DC**, **IO4 CS**, IO5 SCLK, IO6 BL. **IO2 is a DEAD PIN** — its net has exactly one node (the SoC). Waveshare never routed the display read-back line, and the LCD connector's SDO (L1.22) is dangling too. This is why the defconfig has `CONFIG_ESP32S3_SPI2_MISOPIN=-1`. IO2 is NOT on the header and cannot be used for anything.
52	- I2C bus (touch/RTC/IMU/audio codec/AXP/expander all shared): **IO7 SCL, IO8 SDA**
53	- microSD (SPI): IO9 MISO, IO10 MOSI, IO11 SCLK (SD_CS on expander EXIO3). **Slot is unused → these three are the board's only reusable native GPIOs, and the stepper now owns them.**
54	- I2S audio (ES8311): IO12 MCLK, IO13 SCLK, IO14 ASDOUT, IO15 LRCK, IO16 DSDIN. **PRIVATE BUS — not on any header.** Each net has exactly two nodes: ESP32 + codec. Nothing external can reach them, and nothing external can conflict with them.
55	- Camera (OV5640 DVP): IO17 VSYNC, IO18 HREF, IO21 D7, IO38 XCLK, IO39 D6, IO40 D5, IO41 PCLK, IO42 D4, IO45 D0, IO46 D3, IO47 D1, IO48 D2
56	- USB-C: IO19 (D-), IO20 (D+) — the console (USB-Serial/JTAG) rides here
57	- UART0: IO43 TXD (usable as GPIO), **IO44 RXD — clamped, will NOT drive an output** (the UART mux re-wins over `esp32s3_configgpio`)
58	- IO33–37 dangle (single-node nets); flash + octal PSRAM occupy the IO26–37 region internally
59	- IO0: IMU INT + strapping (avoid)
60	- TCA9554 expander EXIO0–7 (all used): CAM_PWDN, LCD_RST, TP_INT, SD_CS, RTC_INT, AXP_IRQ, SYS_OUT, PA_CTRL.
61	
62	## Header J8 (2×16, 2.54 mm) — the complete map
63	Odd column left, even right:
64	
65	| | | | |
66	|---|---|---|---|
67	| 1 VBAT | 2 VBUS | 17 IO45 | 18 IO18 |
68	| 3 GND | 4 GND | 19 IO46 | 20 IO0 |
69	| 5 IO21 | 6 USB_N | 21 IO47 | 22 EN |
70	| 7 IO38 | 8 USB_P | 23 IO48 | 24 PWRON |
71	| 9 IO39 | 10 **IO11** | 25 IO44 | 26 IO7 SCL |
72	| 11 IO40 | 12 **IO10** | 27 **IO43** | 28 IO8 SDA |
73	| 13 IO41 | 14 **IO9** | 29 GND | 30 GND |
74	| 15 IO42 | 16 IO17 | 31 3V3 | 32 3V3 |
75	
76	**No spare GPIOs remain.** Camera on J2 + stepper on 9/10/11/43 claims everything usable. Any new peripheral goes on the I²C bus (IO7/IO8) or through the TCA9554. An external I²S MEMS mic is **impossible** — there is nowhere to put it.
77	
78	## ACTUATOR WIRING (supersedes the old servo plan)
79	- **Stepper IN1/IN2/IN3/IN4 = GPIO 9/10/11/43** (J8 pins 14/12/10/27). See [[velapaw-stepper-bringup]].
80	- **Free IO43 by keeping the console on USB-Serial/JTAG** (IO19/20), never UART0. Full logging retained.
81	- **IO44 is not a usable output.** **IO12/13/15/16 reach the codec, not the header** — an early revision had IN1..IN3 there and three coils were simply unconnected (the buzz saga).
82	- **Motor power: separate 5 V ≥2 A + common ground** (see BOM). Flash/logs over USB-C.
83	- [Old servo-era note, now moot:] the expander was ruled out for a *servo* because I²C can't do µs-accurate 50 Hz PWM. That objection does not transfer to a stepper, which only needs ~667 coil updates/s (~4 % bus load at 400 kHz) — worth remembering if a pin ever has to be freed.
84	
85	## Onboard audio — free, costs zero GPIOs
86	The -C carries a **microphone** (analog differential into ES8311 `MIC1P`/`MIC1N` via R41/R43) and an **MX1.25 speaker header** driven by an **NS4150B** amp whose enable is `PA_CTRL` = **expander EXIO7**; a **6 Ω 1 W speaker ships in the box**. Codec control (`AU_SCL`/`AU_SDA`) is on the existing IO7/IO8 I²C bus. Because the I²S bus is private (IO12–16), **audio and the stepper cannot physically conflict** — this is the only viable voice-input path, and it needs no new parts and no motor changes. ⚠️ Firmware must not drive 12/13/15/16 as GPIOs once the codec is enabled. NuttX side: `nuttx/drivers/audio/es8311.c` supports `AUDIO_TYPE_INPUT`, and `esp32s3_i2s.c` has `i2s_receive()` with `CONFIG_ESP32S3_I2S0_RX` default y. No ASR engine exists in the tree — keyword spotting would be TFLM, or cloud via `external/bailian_sdk`.

88	## Features this board unlocks (deferred in emulator)
89	- **RTC (PCF85063)** → real **meal-timing** (was skipped for lack of a wall clock).
90	- **microSD** → **persistent feed history / analytics** across reboots (was in-memory only).
91	
92	## Feeder dispensing — grams -> motion (calibration)
93	The app speaks **grams** (portions ~5-50g, daily limits 20-300g; NOT kg). The dispenser does not measure grams; it is CALIBRATED once:
94	- Measure kibble released per unit of motion: run the auger 1 rotation (or motor 1 s), weigh the output on a kitchen scale -> e.g. `grams_per_rotation` ~= 5g (or `grams_per_second` ~= 8g). Store the constant (NVS/SD so it survives reboot).
95	- **Dispense N grams = run actuator for N / grams_per_unit** (e.g. 20g @ 5g/rot = 4 rotations, or 2.5s @ 8g/s).
96	- This is OPEN-LOOP feeding (no sensor): ~±10-20% accurate, standard for consumer feeders. Fine for v1.
97	
98	**Firmware hook:** `velapaw_feeder_dispense(grams)` (currently mock print) becomes on hardware: `runtime = grams / grams_per_second; drive_servo(GPIO43 LEDC PWM, runtime);`. Nothing above it changes (app stays in grams). Planned backend: hal/feeder_servo.c.
99	
100	**Accuracy upgrade (deferred):** add a **load cell + HX711** under the bowl -> CLOSED-LOOP: dispense until measured weight == target (~1g accurate). Same hardware also gives real EATEN-grams / eating-speed (the analytics we deferred). Needs the load cell (not on the board).
101	
102	**Suggested (not yet built):** a UI "Calibrate" mode = dispense a test amount -> user weighs it -> enter value -> stores grams_per_unit.

Read the whole verdict plus the three hardware memories. Two things came out of it, and one of them changes the suspect list.

**Both physical-bisect candidates are dead.** The verdict says "bisect what changed physically since the last good b83 boot," so I checked the two things that were assembled after Aug 7:

- **Camera**: IO17/18/21/38–42/45–48. No overlap with the codec bus.
- **Stepper**: the pre-Aug-2 code did drive GPIO12/13/15/16 — MCLK, BCLK, LRCK, DSDIN. That looked like output-vs-output contention on three clock lines, but it isn't: all four of those are ESP32→codec directions anyway, so the stepper was driving the same direction the I2S peripheral does. And **IO14 (ASDOUT, the one dead line) was never in that set.** No conflict, and the mic worked fine on builds 52–83 *after* that code existed.

More to the point, [velapaw-hardware.md:54](C:\Users\VICTUS\.claude\projects\c--Users-VICTUS-openVela\memory\velapaw-hardware.md#L54) settles it structurally: **IO12–16 is a private two-node bus — ESP32 and codec only, not on J8, not on any connector.** There is nothing to reseat, no cable to flip, nothing external that could ever have been miswired onto it. So "what changed physically" has no candidates at all. If the verdict is right, it means a degraded solder joint or a dead ADC — not an assembly mistake.

**The mic element is exonerated, and that redirects the probe.** The standing signature is owner bit set, `length 0`, no EOF — *zero bytes*. But I2S RX samples on BCLK edges regardless of what DIN is doing: a dead mic element, or DIN stuck flat, still fills buffers with constant zeros and still fires EOF. Your own memory records the distinction — the dead TDM slot reads "0 to the bit" while the live slot carries a noise floor in a silent room, and both arrive. **Silence delivers bytes. Zero bytes means the RX channel isn't clocking.** So "ES8311 ADC/clock, the I²S wiring, or the mic element" is wrong at the mic end, and the analyzer plan's decision rule ("DIN flat while BCLK/WS toggle ⇒ codec/mic side") doesn't discriminate what we need — DIN's level is not the variable.

**The cheap test that has never been run: talk to the codec over I2C.** It's a separate bus (IO7/IO8), it needs no rebuild, no flash and no soldering, and TX working 19/19 through the same chip gives us a built-in control — compare the ADC-side registers against the DAC-side ones on the same codec. First, does the tool exist? Cold power cycle, Enter ×3, then at `nsh>`:

```
?
```

Look for `i2c` in the builtin list. If it's there:

```
i2c bus
i2c dev -b 0 0x03 0x77
i2c get -b 0 -a 0x18 -r 0xfd
i2c get -b 0 -a 0x18 -r 0xfe
```

`0xfd`/`0xfe` should read `0x83`/`0x11` — that alone proves the codec is alive and answering. If the scan shows the codec at `0x19` instead of `0x18`, use that for `-a` throughout.

Then — and this ordering matters, because the registers are only meaningful once the driver has configured the chip — **go straight to the voice dialog on that same boot** (My Pets → Edit, say one word; do *not* run `velapaw kws mic` first), let it fail, and dump the clock and ADC block while b80's held-open session is still up:

```
i2c get -b 0 -a 0x18 -r 0x00
i2c get -b 0 -a 0x18 -r 0x01
i2c get -b 0 -a 0x18 -r 0x02
i2c get -b 0 -a 0x18 -r 0x06
i2c get -b 0 -a 0x18 -r 0x09
i2c get -b 0 -a 0x18 -r 0x0a
i2c get -b 0 -a 0x18 -r 0x0d
i2c get -b 0 -a 0x18 -r 0x0e
i2c get -b 0 -a 0x18 -r 0x14
i2c get -b 0 -a 0x18 -r 0x17
i2c get -b 0 -a 0x18 -r 0x44
```

I'm deliberately not predicting bit meanings ahead of the dump — your memory flags re-deriving register decodes as a trap that has already cost two sessions, and `0x09`/`0x0a` (DAC vs ADC serial port format) and `0x0d`/`0x0e` (system vs analog power) are the ones where the working-TX-versus-dead-RX comparison does the work for us instead of me arguing from a datasheet.

Two honest notes on where this ends. If the codec answers and its ADC block looks correctly configured, then `0x44`'s digital loopback is the one remaining zero-cost probe — poking it live with `i2c set` while a capture runs tests the codec's serial output path without the analog front end, no rebuild needed. And if that also comes back zero bytes, the fault is inside the SoC's I2S RX block, where the only remaining instrument is soldered taps on IO13/14/15 — fine-pitch work on a live board, since none of those pins is on a header. At that point I'd say stop and ship `ask`, which landed on hardware today. But this dump costs one boot and no code, so it's worth doing before that call.

No `i2c` builtin — `CONFIG_SYSTEM_I2CTOOL` is off, so the zero-rebuild path is gone. That's worth knowing rather than guessing at.

Of the two ways to get it back, I'd skip the Kconfig route. `CONFIG_SYSTEM_I2CTOOL` also needs `CONFIG_I2C_DRIVER` and whatever that pulls, `make olddefconfig` is off-limits in this tree so every dependent symbol is hand-set, and this config currently boots a working board with the PSRAM-stack fix and the console intact. That's a lot of exposure for a diagnostic.

The cheaper route uses what's already there. The board already talks to the **PCF85063 over raw I2C** on the same IO7/IO8 bus the codec sits on, and this is a FLAT build — so a `velapaw codec` subcommand can call the existing I2C helper directly, exactly the way `tool_meal.c` reaches `velapaw_meal_set_by_name` through a hand-written `extern`. No Kconfig changes, read *and* write in one build (so the `0x44` loopback poke comes free), and `velapaw <subcommand>` is the form that's safe to run.

I need to see that existing helper before writing anything. One paste, from the VM:

```
cd ~/openvela
grep -rn "es8311\|ES8311\|pcf85063\|PCF85063\|i2cbus_initialize\|I2C_TRANSFER" \
  nuttx/boards/xtensa/esp32s3/esp32s3-devkit/src --include=*.c --include=*.h
```

That should give me three things at once: the ES8311's I2C address and port from its registration, the RTC code as the reusable transfer pattern, and whether there's already a `*_i2c_read_reg`-shaped helper worth calling instead of writing a new one.

Then the shape of it is: add the subcommand, rebuild, flash, cold power cycle, straight to the voice dialog (not `velapaw kws mic`), let the capture fail, `quit` to `nsh>`, and dump the clock/ADC block while b80 is still holding the session open. The ADC-versus-DAC register comparison on a chip whose TX runs 19/19 is the part that does the actual work — it's a control I don't have to argue for.

One caveat I'd rather flag now than after the build: if the board file is where that helper lives, this touches `nuttx/boards/`, which is on your stale-object list — the `.o` there is never invalidated by the rebuild scripts, so the build will need the matching `rm` or it'll silently flash unchanged firmware. I'll spell out the exact deletions once the grep shows me which file I'm editing.

553	## ✅ SOLVED: the `es8311 -22` boot spam is cosmetic — never chase it
554	
555	    es8311_getcoeff: MCLK = 4096000 and samplerate = 48000 not supported
556	    es8311_setsamplerate: Failed to set sample rate: -22
557	
558	The driver does it to itself. `es8311.c:2153` sets
559	`priv->samprate = ES8311_DEFAULT_SAMPRATE` (48000), then `:2191` calls
560	`es8311_setsamplerate()` during init while MCLK is 4096000 (= 256 × 16000).
561	`getcoeff(4096000, 48000)` has no table entry → `-22`. The real rate is
562	programmed later from `caps->ac_controls.hw[0]`, and `:1039` already calls
563	`es8311_reset()` *before* `:1046`'s `setsamplerate()`. **It appears in working
564	boots too**, so its presence in a failing log means nothing. This misled a
565	third-party analysis into proposing an ES8311 power-up clock race; that was
566	rejected on evidence.
567	
568	## Session shape
569	
570	Open, configure, `AUDIOIOC_START` **once**; each capture only enqueues and
571	collects. Between captures the session is running but idle. Free-running RX is
572	not an option: `mq_maxmsg = nbuffers + 8`, so with no reader the driver's
573	`mq_send` would drop buffer pointers. `mic_flush_mq()` before each re-arm.
574	
575	⚠️ **`apb->nbytes` is read by the driver *during* the enqueue ioctl** — the
576	caller sets it: record side `0`, playback side `nmaxbytes`. Zeroing it in a
577	shared helper silently sends a zero-length TX buffer → no clock → hang. TX
578	must stay primed; RX borrows BCLK/WS from TX (see [[velapaw-audio-bringup]]).
579	
580	⚠️ Do not conflate this with the falsified theory above. A **zero-length first**
581	TX buffer means `I2S_TX_START` is never set, so the clock never starts — real.
582	TX **draining after** a good buffer is harmless, because `TX_START` stays set
583	and `#16` cleared `TX_STOP_EN`.

588	8-segment peak profile. Reference at 30 dB, build 52, de-interleaved:

597	Do **not** read a full-scale spike at a fixed index as clipping — that is the
598	start-of-stream transient, see [[velapaw-audio-gain]].

   - **Zero bytes ≠ silence**: I2S RX shifts DIN on BCLK edges regardless of level; silence still produces bytes/EOF. Hence the mic element/DIN level can't cause zero bytes — and **the `velapaw codec set 44 08` loopback I proposed is NON-discriminating** (changes only DIN content); must be corrected to the user before they spend a boot on it.
   - **TX/RX DMA asymmetry in `esp32s3_i2s.c` (the new lead)**: TX copies `apb->samp` into a driver `calloc` bounce buffer (`bfcontainer->buf`) and DMAs from that; RX DMAs **directly into `apb->samp`**, which comes from `apb_alloc()` → `kumm_malloc()` on a common heap including octal PSRAM (`CONFIG_ESP32S3_SPIRAM_COMMON_HEAP=y`, `MM_REGIONS=2`; es8311 has `allocbuffer = NULL`). RX into PSRAM is done with **no `esp32s3_dma_set_ext_memblk`, no 16/64-byte alignment, no cache invalidate, burst disabled** — whereas the team's own camera code does all three (`ESP32S3_DMA_EXT_MEMBLK_64B`, `kmm_memalign(64,…)`, `cache_invalidate_addr`).

568	## Session shape
569	
570	Open, configure, `AUDIOIOC_START` **once**; each capture only enqueues and
571	collects. Between captures the session is running but idle. Free-running RX is
572	not an option: `mq_maxmsg = nbuffers + 8`, so with no reader the driver's
573	`mq_send` would drop buffer pointers. `mic_flush_mq()` before each re-arm.

575	⚠️ **`apb->nbytes` is read by the driver *during* the enqueue ioctl** — the
576	caller sets it: record side `0`, playback side `nmaxbytes`. Zeroing it in a
577	shared helper silently sends a zero-length TX buffer → no clock → hang. TX
578	must stay primed; RX borrows BCLK/WS from TX (see [[velapaw-audio-bringup]]).

581	TX buffer means `I2S_TX_START` is never set, so the clock never starts — real.
582	TX **draining after** a good buffer is harmless, because `TX_START` stays set
583	and `#16` cleared `TX_STOP_EN`.

This session is being continued from a previous conversation that ran out of context. The summary below covers the earlier portion of the conversation.

Summary:
1. Primary Request and Intent:
   - Standing intent: voice-driven meal scheduling for VelaPaw with the **real on-board ES8311 mic** ("I think lets make the real mic work"), not the phone/WebSocket route.
   - Earlier this thread (done): "flash it for me on com 3" → firmware `DBC020BF3C8A4630BD01A17CB61FE620`, 1,563,968 B, hash verified.
   - **Current active request: "Take a look at the velapaw-mic-capture.md and provide a solution since the mic is not working"** — the user wants an actual fix, not more incremental probes. No reply has yet been delivered for it.

2. Key Technical Concepts:
   - **Zero bytes ≠ silence**: I2S RX clocks DIN on BCLK edges regardless of level, so a dead mic/flat DIN can't produce zero bytes; therefore **`velapaw codec set 44 08` loopback is NON-discriminating** (must be corrected to user). `0x44=0x00` poke result: no effect (caps 3, rec 0/54, eof 0, desc 80000ff0, intraw 000000a0, kick 3 ok 0).
   - **The RX descriptor proves the buffer is in PSRAM**: `esp32s3_dma_setup()` uses `dma_size = 0x1000 - alignment` (=4080 with default 16 B ext block) only when `!tx && esp32s3_ptr_extram(pbuf)`; standing stall `desc 80000ff0 80000010` = sizes 4080 + 16 = PSRAM branch. Internal SRAM (no burst) would give one 4092-byte descriptor.
   - **esp32s3_dma_setup rounds RX lengths to 16 but never aligns/checks the ADDRESS**; I2S never calls `esp32s3_dma_set_ext_memblk`; no cache invalidate.
   - **`apb->samp` is only 8-byte aligned**: `apb_alloc()` → `lib_umemalign(MAX(up_get_dcache_linesize(),1), numbytes)`; `up_get_dcache_linesize()` is `#define … 0` without `CONFIG_ARCH_DCACHE` (not set) → alignment 1 → plain malloc → MM_ALIGN 8 (`CONFIG_MM_DEFAULT_ALIGNMENT=0`). So 16-byte alignment is a heap-layout coin flip.
   - **Unifying hypothesis (new, unproven sub-mechanism)**: misaligned PSRAM RX buffers stall GDMA (data reaches infifo → `INFIFO_FULL_WM` re-asserts; descriptor owner=1 length 0; no IN_SUC_EOF; `isr 0`). Explains: per-boot intermittency (b81 "3 of 5 cold boots"), "bad from FIRST capture" (buffers allocated once at preopen and reused), kicks never recover, TX unaffected (TX DMAs from driver `calloc` bounce buffer, no RX alignment rule), b76 "buf1 EOF then buf2 never", and known-good old images (b82, b83) now failing (persistent data — pet DB, history, littlefs, RTC date — shifts pre-session heap allocations deterministically). This undermines the 2026-09-22 "known-good image fails ⇒ hardware" inference. Caveat: good-era buffers were also PSRAM (0x3C5x…) and worked.
   - **Fix direction**: RX DMA into internal SRAM bounce buffers (static .bss ring, e.g. 3 × 4096 B `aligned(16)`), round-robin assigned at enqueue in `i2s_rxdma_setup` (rx.pend FIFO, one active at a time ⇒ start order = enqueue order), stored in `bfcontainer->buf`; `memcpy(apb->samp, buf, apb->nbytes)` in `i2s_rx_worker` after patch #10's sum (CPU write through cache — also kills the PSRAM stale-cache trap / 18-buffer need); never free the static buffer; fallback + one-time syslog if nbytes > slot. Optional gated diagnostic: log `apb->samp` and `((uintptr_t)samp & 15)` per enqueue to confirm alignment hypothesis.
   - Driver facts: RX nbytes per buffer = 4092 (`MIN(nmaxbytes, ESP32S3_DMA_BUFLEN_MAX) & ~3`, patch #9); `I2S_RX_EOF_NUM` = 4092; only one RX container in `rx.act`; ISR `i2s_rx_interrupt` → `i2s_rx_schedule` (moves to rx.done, immediately starts next DMA, queues HPWORK `i2s_rx_worker`); ISR doesn't touch PSRAM; `esp32s3_dma_request(i2s_dma_dev, 1, 1, false)` (no burst).
   - Available internal-heap API: `xtensa_imm_malloc`/`xtensa_imm_memalign` (`esp32s3_imm.c`, declared in `arch/xtensa/include/arch.h`), but IMEM heap (0x30000) also hosts stacks — prefer static .bss.
   - Camera code is the correct PSRAM-DMA recipe (`esp32s3_dma_set_ext_memblk(…64B)`, `kmm_memalign(64,…)`, `cache_invalidate_addr`).
   - Verified bit positions: `I2S_RX_START` BIT2, `RX_SLAVE_MOD` BIT3, `RX_MONO` BIT5, `TX_STOP_EN` BIT13, `SIG_LOOPBACK` BIT27; GDMA IN_DONE BIT0, IN_SUC_EOF BIT1, IN_DSCR_EMPTY BIT4, INFIFO_FULL_WM BIT5, INFIFO_UDF_L1 BIT7.
   - Config: `CONFIG_I2S_DMADESC_NUM=4`, `ESP32S3_DATA_CACHE_LINE_SIZE=32`, I2S0 16-bit @16000, `SPIRAM_MODE_OCT`, `SPIRAM_COMMON_HEAP=y`, `MM_REGIONS=2`, `AUDIO_BUFFER_NUMBYTES=8192`, `AUDIO_NUM_BUFFERS=2`.
   - Image 1,563,968 B vs /data littlefs at 0x180000 → ~8.9 KB headroom.

3. Files and Code Sections:
   - `C:\Users\VICTUS\.claude\projects\c--Users-VICTUS-openVela\memory\velapaw-mic-capture.md` — read fully (599 lines). Previously edited (2026-10-11 codec section). **Needs update**: 0x44=00 no effect; 44 08 non-discriminating; PSRAM-RX/8-byte-alignment lead; verdict-inference flaw; ~8.9 KB headroom.
   - `D:\openVela\velapaw-snapshots\2026-08-10-b82-camerafix\src\nuttx\arch\esp32s3_i2s.c` (3530 lines, Aug 10; identical size copy in b68 snapshot) — the VM's current driver is 3857 lines (md5 720e4818…, patches #26–#36) and is NOT on Windows; author patches against VM via anchors. Key code:
     ```c
     /* i2s_rxdma_setup :954-994 */
     inlink = bfcontainer->dma_link;
     bytes_queued = esp32s3_dma_setup(inlink, I2S_DMADESC_NUM,
                                      bfcontainer->apb->samp,
                                      bfcontainer->nbytes, I2S_RX,
                                      priv->dma_channel);
     ...
     flags = spin_lock_irqsave(&priv->slock);
     sq_addlast((sq_entry_t *)bfcontainer, &priv->rx.pend);
     ret = i2s_rxdma_start(priv);
     spin_unlock_irqrestore(&priv->slock, flags);
     ```
     ```c
     /* i2s_rx_worker :1420-1443 — insert memcpy from bounce after this loop */
     dmadesc = bfcontainer->dma_link;
     bfcontainer->apb->nbytes = 0;
     while (dmadesc != NULL)
       {
         bfcontainer->apb->nbytes +=
             (dmadesc->ctrl >> ESP32S3_DMA_CTRL_DATALEN_S) &
             ESP32S3_DMA_CTRL_DATALEN_V;
         if (dmadesc->ctrl & ESP32S3_DMA_CTRL_EOF) break;
         dmadesc = dmadesc->next;
       }
     /* then #if VELAPAW_I2S_PROBES patch #30 stats; then
        "/* Perform the RX transfer done callback */" ... callback; apb_free; i2s_buf_free */
     ```
     TX worker frees `bfcontainer->buf` (`free(bfcontainer->buf);` under "Release the internal buffer used by the DMA outlink"). `i2s_receive` :3156-3247 (nbytes 4092, `priv->streaming = true` patch #11). `i2s_rx_interrupt` :2658-2684. RXDUMP patch #19/#24 in `i2s_tx_worker` :1253-1365 (gated `VELAPAW_I2S_PROBES`, :88, must be 0 for shipping).
   - `D:\openVela\nuttx\arch\xtensa\src\esp32s3\esp32s3_dma.c` — read fully; `esp32s3_dma_setup` PSRAM branch (lines 237-336), `esp32s3_dma_set_ext_memblk` (528-551), `esp32s3_dma_load` resets IN_RST + sets INLINK (355-388).
   - `D:\openVela\nuttx\include\nuttx\audio\audio.h` :769-785 `struct ap_buffer_s` (samp is a pointer, separate allocation).
   - `D:\openVela\nuttx\libs\libc\audio\lib_buffer.c` :61-105 `apb_alloc` (`lib_umalloc` apb + `lib_umemalign(MAX(up_get_dcache_linesize(),1), numbytes)` samp).
   - `D:\openVela\nuttx\include\nuttx\cache.h` :256-259 `up_get_dcache_linesize()` → 0 without CONFIG_ARCH_DCACHE.
   - `D:\openVela\nuttx\arch\xtensa\src\esp32s3\esp32s3_imm.c` (`xtensa_imm_malloc` :86, `xtensa_imm_memalign` :209); `hardware/esp32s3_soc.h:132` `esp32s3_ptr_extram`.
   - Snapshot configs: `velapaw-snapshots\2026-08-06-b68-voice-working\nuttx\config.golden`, `2026-08-10-b82-camerafix\src\nuttx\config.b82-camerafix` / `config.golden`.
   - `…\b82-camerafix\src\nuttx\boards\esp32s3_st7789.c` :675-731 camera PSRAM DMA recipe (from earlier window).
   - Session transcript: `C:\Users\VICTUS\.claude\projects\c--Users-VICTUS-openVela\3659500b-38f3-47db-bbd0-9b2aab159cd9.jsonl` (401,386,239 B) — only transcript; candidate source of good-era MIC_TRACE addresses.

4. Errors and fixes:
   - PowerShell `Get-ChildItem -LiteralPath … -Include` didn't filter (dumped 16.2 MB to tool-results\b3sjbo1le.txt) → re-ran with `-Filter` per filename.
   - Ripgrep over D:\openVela\nuttx timed out (20 s) → used PowerShell `Select-String` on specific subdirs.
   - Earlier windows: Glob timeout on snapshots; brace-glob Grep returned nothing → per-file greps.
   - Own reasoning error to correct to user: `velapaw codec set 44 08` loopback cannot discriminate.

5. Problem Solving:
   - Established: codec alive and ADC-configured; 0x44=00 no effect; current failing RX buffers are in PSRAM (desc size 4080/16); samp only 8-byte aligned; driver never configures PSRAM RX DMA properly. Strong software lead contradicting the "hardware" verdict.
   - Pending verification: good-era samp addresses mod 16 (transcript search was about to start); VM driver specifics (buf field under ifdef?, any RX path freeing `buf`, patch #36 kick re-running `esp32s3_dma_setup` with `apb->samp`).

6. All user messages:
   - (Pre-window) `?` builtin listing; greps/sed outputs; patch+build+flash-gate results; `python3 -m http.server 8000`; "flash it for me on com 3"; first `velapaw codec` dump; `velapaw codec set 44 00` + re-dump (pasted twice); pasted `velapaw voice` output after 0x44=00 (caps 3, lastret -110, eof 0, start 4, kick 3 ok 0, rec 0/54, play 3/3, cap FAILED at 68110/75840/207170); `/model fable` (local command).
   - **"Take a look at the velapaw-mic-capture.md and provide a solution since the mic is not working"** (current request).
   - **Standing constraints — STILL IN FORCE, verbatim:**
     - **"dont commit"** — no git commits.

     - Never echo a matched secret into the transcript; **do not use GitHub's "allow the secret" unblock URL**; **do not `cat` `/data/ai_agent/config/config.json`** (API key).

so the rule is exactly 16 B — the GDMA `IN_EXT_MEM_BK_SIZE` default.

**Mechanism.** The mic node `/dev/audio/pcm_in0` is an **es8311** lower half
with `allocbuffer = NULL`, so `nuttx/audio/audio.c` `audio_allocbuffer()` calls
libc `apb_alloc()` directly. **A fix in the I2S driver's

`lib_umemalign(MAX(up_get_dcache_linesize(), 1), n)`; without
`CONFIG_ARCH_DCACHE` the linesize is 0 → alignment 1 → plain malloc → 8 B.
`esp32s3_dma_setup()` rounds PSRAM RX *lengths* to 16 (the 4080+16 split in

aligns the *address*. Misaligned PSRAM target → descriptor 0 never completes
(owner 1, length 0, no EOF, raw `000000a0`; the later probe builds showed
`0000000f`).

allocated back-to-back with a stride that is a multiple of 16 (0x20a0), so

that lands on 8 fails every time. Boot-time allocations depend on /data
contents (pets, history, UI objects), so flashing the Aug b82 image did NOT
restore the Aug heap — the 2026-09-22 "known-good image fails ⇒ hardware"
inference below never controlled for heap layout. Fits everything: b81's

text:
I'm confident the mic itself isn't broken. Capture dies when the DMA buffer lands on an address that isn't a multiple of 16, and the August logs show this pattern with no exceptions. The fix is a one-line change. It hasn't been tested on the board yet.

## Root cause

The I2S receive DMA writes straight into the audio buffer (`apb->samp`), which is in PSRAM. On the ESP32-S3, the DMA only finishes a write to PSRAM when the buffer's address is a multiple of 16 bytes. `apb_alloc()` gives plain `malloc` memory, which only guarantees multiples of 8. When the buffer lands at an address that is 8 more than a multiple of 16, the first DMA transfer never completes and every capture that boot returns zero bytes.

The August builds were the only ones that printed the buffer address (`RXDUMP d[0] buf=`). Every dump in the transcript fits the pattern:

| Outcome | Dumps | Buffer address mod 16 |
|---|---|---|
| Stalled (`eofdes=0`, no data) | 18 | **8**, every one (0x3c4bdb48, 0x3c4bdb58, 0x3c510688…) |
| Audio flowed (`mic n=2046 …`) | 13 | **0**, every one (0x3c4bfc40, 0x3c4c1cb0, 0x3c512ed0…) |

Working runs sit at both 0 and 16 mod 32, so the requirement is exactly 16-byte alignment. Today's builds don't print the address, but your current `desc 80000ff0 80000010` is the 4080 + 16 split the DMA code only uses for PSRAM buffers.

## Why it looked like hardware

- **One draw decides the whole boot.** All record buffers are allocated back to back, spaced a multiple of 16 bytes apart, so they all share the first buffer's alignment. That explains "3 of 5 cold boots", "bad from the first capture" and kicks never recovering.
- **The addresses repeat.** For a given build and heap history, the buffers land in the same place every boot. The heap layout also depends on what's stored on `/data` (most likely the pets, history and the UI objects built from them). So flashing the August b82 image didn't bring back the August heap, and the 2026‑09‑22 "known-good image fails, so it's hardware" conclusion doesn't hold. I've marked it retracted in the memory note.
- **Correction:** skip the `velapaw codec set 44 08` loopback test I suggested. A stalled DMA returns zero bytes whatever the codec sends, so it can't tell us anything. The `0x44 = 00` poke having no effect is what this cause predicts.

## Why the fix goes in libc

`/dev/audio/pcm_in0` is an ES8311 device with no buffer allocator of its own (`allocbuffer = NULL`). So `audio.c` calls `apb_alloc()` directly, and a fix in the I2S driver's allocation code would never run. `apb_alloc()` already asks for cache-line alignment, but that size reads as 0 without `CONFIG_ARCH_DCACHE`, so the request falls back to 1 byte. The fix raises the minimum to 64 bytes, which covers every block size the DMA supports.

## VM commands (paste them, then send me the output)

**1. Check, back up and patch**
```bash
cd ~/openvela/nuttx
grep -n 'lib_umemalign' libs/libc/audio/lib_buffer.c
cp -n libs/libc/audio/lib_buffer.c ~/lib_buffer.c.pre-rxalign
python3 - <<'EOF'
import pathlib, sys
p = pathlib.Path('libs/libc/audio/lib_buffer.c')
s = p.read_text()
old = "  samp = lib_umemalign(MAX(up_get_dcache_linesize(), 1), bufdesc->numbytes);\n"
new = ("  /* VELAPAW: the ESP32-S3 I2S RX GDMA writes straight into samp, which\n"
       "   * normally sits in PSRAM.  GDMA only completes a PSRAM write when the\n"
       "   * target is aligned to its external-memory block (16 B by default),\n"
       "   * but up_get_dcache_linesize() is 0 here (no CONFIG_ARCH_DCACHE), so\n"
       "   * this was a plain 8-byte-aligned malloc.  Whenever samp landed at\n"
       "   * 8 mod 16 the first RX descriptor never completed and the mic\n"
       "   * returned zero bytes for the whole boot.  64 covers every block\n"
       "   * size and keeps the buffer on whole 32-byte cache lines.\n"
       "   */\n"
       "\n"
       "  samp = lib_umemalign(MAX(up_get_dcache_linesize(), 64),\n"
       "                       bufdesc->numbytes);\n")
if "VELAPAW: the ESP32-S3 I2S RX GDMA" in s:
    sys.exit("already patched - nothing to do")
if s.count(old) != 1:
    sys.exit("anchor not found exactly once - send me the grep line above")
p.write_text(s.replace(old, new))
print("patched", p)
EOF
grep -n 'dcache_linesize' libs/libc/audio/lib_buffer.c
```
Expected: line 72 with `, 1)` first, then `patched …`, then `MAX(up_get_dcache_linesize(), 64),`.

**2. Remove the stale libc objects** (the same trap as `libarch.a`)
```bash
find libs/libc -name 'lib_buffer.o' -print -delete
rm -fv libs/libc/libc.a staging/libc.a
```

**3. Build**
```bash
cd ~/openvela
./build.sh esp32s3-devkit:waveshare_lcd -j4 2>&1 | tail -n 20
```

**4. Check the build**
```bash
cd ~/openvela/nuttx
find libs/libc -name 'lib_buffer.o' -newer libs/libc/audio/lib_buffer.c -print
xtensa-esp32s3-elf-objdump -d --disassemble=apb_alloc nuttx | grep -B4 '<memalign>'
stat -c '%s' nuttx.bin
md5sum nuttx.bin
```
- **`find`:** must print the rebuilt object.
- **objdump:** must show `a10, 64` a line or two above `call8 … <memalign>`. If it shows `a10, 1`, the old object got linked, so stop there.
- **Size:** must stay under 1572864 (the `/data` partition starts at 0x180000).

Then run `python3 -m http.server 8000` in `~/openvela/nuttx` like last time. I'll download the image, check it against your md5, check the port, and flash COM3.

## Test after flashing

1. Unplug and replug the board (a cold boot, not RESET), then press Enter three times to get `nsh>`.
2. On the screen go to My Pets → Edit, start the voice dialog and say the words.
3. Run `velapaw voice` and paste the output.

It passes if `eof` counts up, `rec` is non-zero, there's no `cap FAILED`, and `intraw` is no longer `000000a0`. Repeat on two or three cold boots, because the old failure was decided per boot. Don't run `velapaw kws mic` first.

## If it doesn't fully work

- **Words heard but scoring low:** the next tweak is the mic gain, still at the old 24 dB: `velapaw codec set 14 1a` (30 dB).
- **Still no `eof` with the 64 confirmed in step 4:** then alignment isn't today's problem. The next step would be having the DMA write into a small internal-RAM buffer in the I2S driver, which takes PSRAM out of the capture path entirely.
- **Rollback:** reflash the current `DBC020BF…` image, or restore `~/lib_buffer.c.pre-rxalign` and repeat steps 2–3.
- **`repo sync`:** this edit lives only on the VM, in an upstream file, so a `repo sync` will undo it. That's recorded in the memory note.

text:
I've updated the memory note. The board is now running the fix (`0a23aa25…`), so it's ready for you to test.

## Test

1. Unplug the USB cable and plug it back in. Open the console in PuTTY and press Enter three times to get `nsh>`.
2. On the screen go to My Pets → Edit, start the voice dialog and say the words.
3. Run `velapaw voice` and paste me the output.
4. Do steps 1–3 once more with a cold boot. Then do a third round, but tap RESET instead of unplugging. RESET used to make the stall happen every time, so a pass there is the strongest evidence.

It passes if:
- `eof` is above 0
- `rec` is no longer `0/54`
- there's no `cap FAILED`
- `lastret` is not `-110`
- `intraw` is not `000000a0`

Don't run `velapaw kws mic` before the dialog, and don't type bare `velapaw`.

## What the results would mean

- **All three boots pass:** the alignment fix is confirmed and I'll mark it solved in memory. The only code change was the 64, so nothing else could explain it.
- **Capture works but the words score low:** run `velapaw codec set 14 1a` to raise the mic gain from 24 to 30 dB, then try the dialog again.
- **Still `eof 0` on any boot:** alignment isn't the whole story. The next step is having the DMA write into a small internal-RAM buffer in the I2S driver.
- **Rollback:** I kept the old `DBC020BF` image in the scratchpad, and putting it back on the board takes about 10 seconds.

The `cp: warning: behavior of -n is non-portable` line from step 1 doesn't matter. The backup `~/lib_buffer.c.pre-rxalign` was still written.

25	exceptions. mod 32 does NOT separate them (working runs sit at both 0 and 16),
26	so the rule is exactly 16 B — the GDMA `IN_EXT_MEM_BK_SIZE` default.
27	
28	**Mechanism.** The mic node `/dev/audio/pcm_in0` is an **es8311** lower half
29	with `allocbuffer = NULL`, so `nuttx/audio/audio.c` `audio_allocbuffer()` calls
30	libc `apb_alloc()` directly. **A fix in the I2S driver's
31	`AUDIOIOC_ALLOCBUFFER` case would never run** — that path is only reached via
32	`audio_i2s.c`, which this board does not register. `apb_alloc` does
33	`lib_umemalign(MAX(up_get_dcache_linesize(), 1), n)`; without
34	`CONFIG_ARCH_DCACHE` the linesize is 0 → alignment 1 → plain malloc → 8 B.
35	`esp32s3_dma_setup()` rounds PSRAM RX *lengths* to 16 (the 4080+16 split in
36	`desc 80000ff0 80000010` is the proof the buffer is in PSRAM) but never
37	aligns the *address*. Misaligned PSRAM target → descriptor 0 never completes
38	(owner 1, length 0, no EOF, raw `000000a0`; the later probe builds showed
39	`0000000f`).
40	
41	**Why it posed as hardware.** `samp = apb + 0x98` and the record buffers are
42	allocated back-to-back with a stride that is a multiple of 16 (0x20a0), so
43	ONE coin flip on the first apb's address decides the WHOLE boot. Identical
44	addresses repeat run after run for a given build + heap history, so a layout
45	that lands on 8 fails every time. Boot-time allocations depend on /data
46	contents (pets, history, UI objects), so flashing the Aug b82 image did NOT

11	The MEAL → HOUR → CONFIRM spoken dialog in the edit-pet modal
12	(`vsched_*` in `app/velapaw/ui/ui_lvgl.c`), on the 14-label tiny_conv KWS
13	model. **WORKING end to end on hardware, build 68 (2026-08-06):**
14	
15	    heard two 0.773    -> step2
16	    heard eight 0.938  -> step3
17	    heard yes 0.957    -> COMMIT meal 2 = 08:00
18	
19	**9.6 s, three steps, two retries, zero false accepts.** See
20	[[velapaw-mic-capture]] for the capture path underneath it.
21	
22	## Constrained decode — threshold the RAW softmax, never renormalised
23	
24	Each step knows its legal answers (MEAL `{one,two,three}`, HOUR `{zero..nine}`,
25	CONFIRM `{yes,no}`) and `velapaw_kws_best_of()` takes the argmax over just
26	those. **The score returned is the raw probability, deliberately not
27	renormalised over the subset** — the mass sitting on `_silence_`/`_unknown_`
28	is exactly the mass meaning "that wasn't one of my words". Renormalising lets
29	86% of silence/OOV clips through the confirm step; the raw score, 4.9%.
30	
31	Confirmed live: the model heard `eight 0.957` at the MEAL step and best-of
32	returned `one 0.000`. That is the design working, not a bug.
33	
34	## Thresholds (hardware-tuned, build 56; still correct at b68)
35	
36	    MEAL 0.40    HOUR 0.55    CONFIRM 0.55    TIMEOUT 15000 ms    TRIES 5
37	
38	They came *down* from 0.45/0.73/0.59 because words through the ES8311 score
39	0.68–0.71 when correctly heard, not the ~0.99 the test split suggested.
40	A wrong hour is cheap (CONFIRM reads it back); a *rejected* hour is expensive
41	(burns a try, ends with nothing set).
42	
43	## The vote rule is load-bearing — it recovers whole dialogs
44	
45	`VSCHED_VOTES 2` + `VSCHED_VOTE_FLOOR 0.25` — a step also accepts a word it
46	heard twice below threshold. Votes, **not** a consecutive run (the b62 log that
47	motivated it had the repeats interrupted by a 0.176 reading). MEAL and HOUR
48	only; CONFIRM keeps the threshold alone since agreeing twice on a two-way
49	choice is as surprising as a coin landing the same way twice.
50	
51	Two hardware runs, two different regimes, and the rule matters in one of them:
52	
53	- **b68** — every accept cleared its threshold outright (0.773 / 0.938 / 0.957);
54	  `v` never got past 0. Looked like dead weight.
55	- **b69** — the HOUR step got `eight 0.395`, then `six 0.215`, then
56	  `eight 0.266`, and **the votes accepted the correct digit** from three
57	  readings that were all far under the 0.55 gate. Note the `six` in between:
58	  a consecutive-run counter would have reset on it and the dialog would have
59	  cancelled. That is exactly the b62 failure this rule was written for.
60	
61	⚠️ Don't conclude from one good run that it isn't needed — that is the mistake
62	made after b68. Scores swing roughly 2× between sessions at what looks like

3	description: "Edits under nuttx/arch/ were silently dropped from every build — staging/libarch.a was never invalidated, so the linker kept using a Sept 3 object. Found 2026-09-22. Any arch-level conclusion from that window is void."

11	**Found 2026-09-22 while swapping the I2S driver.** `./build.sh` reported a
12	successful `LD: nuttx` and regenerated `nuttx.bin`, but **never recompiled the
13	source we had just replaced** — no `CC:` line, and the resulting image was
14	byte-identical in size to the previous one.
15	
16	## The trap
17	
18	Three things line up to hide it:
19	
20	1. **NuttX builds arch objects FLAT.** The source is
21	   `arch/xtensa/src/esp32s3/esp32s3_i2s.c` (reached as `chip/esp32s3_i2s.c` via
22	   a symlink), but the object is `arch/xtensa/src/esp32s3_i2s.o` — one level up,
23	   *not* beside the `.c`. `Make.dep` and `.depend` live up there too. Deleting
24	   `*.o`/`Make.dep` in the `esp32s3/` subdir deletes nothing; the command
25	   succeeds silently.
26	2. **`staging/libarch.a` is treated as satisfied** regardless of arch sources.
27	   With the archive present, the top level relinks from it and never descends.
28	   A `.c` newer than the `.o` is not enough to trigger a rebuild.
29	3. **The link still succeeds**, because the stale member is in the archive. The
30	   only outward sign is a missing `CC:` line in a build log nobody reads
31	   closely, and an image whose size doesn't move.
32	
33	On this tree `arch/xtensa/src/esp32s3_i2s.o` was dated **Sep 3 20:37** and
34	`staging/libarch.a` **Sep 3 20:41** — three weeks of builds linking a Sept 3
35	object. Sept 3 is the *floor* on how long, not necessarily the start.
36	
37	## The fix — mandatory, not insurance
38	
39	After ANY edit under `nuttx/arch/`:
40	
41	```sh
42	cd ~/openvela/nuttx
43	rm -f arch/xtensa/src/<file>.o staging/libarch.a
44	cd ~/openvela && ./build.sh esp32s3-devkit:waveshare_lcd -j4
45	```
46	
47	Other arch objects survive, so removing `libarch.a` forces a re-archive, not a
48	full arch rebuild — cheap. Removing `Make.dep` too costs a slower build while
49	it regenerates; harmless.
50	
51	## How to PROVE a build actually took
52	
53	Size alone is not enough — the Aug 10 swap produced an image of *exactly* the
54	same 1,561,976 B, padding having absorbed the delta. Two real tests:
55	
56	- **Count differing bytes** between old and new images on Windows. A genuine
57	  rebuild differed in **88,921 bytes (5.7 %)**, spanning `0x9ac`–`0x17d4f9`. A
58	  timestamp-only difference is ~4 bytes (see [[velapaw-golden-baseline]]).
59	- **Plant a symbol that only the new code defines.** The link failing without
60	  it, or succeeding with it, is proof the object was recompiled.
61	
62	## What this invalidates
63	
64	**Any conclusion drawn from an `arch/` change between ~Sept 3 and Sept 22 was
65	drawn from an unchanged binary.** That covers I2S driver work in that window.
66	See [[velapaw-mic-capture]] for the stall verdict, which was re-established
67	with this trap accounted for.
68	
69	Related stale-object traps, same family, different subtree:
70	[[velapaw-b82-camerafix-rebuild]] (`nuttx/boards/**/*.o`) and
71	[[velapaw-makefile-recipe]] (`.built`/`.depend`/`Make.dep` under apps).

That's 3 boots out of 3 working, including the RESET tap that used to break the mic every time, so the mic is fixed.

In one sentence, for your report: the mic hardware was fine. The receive DMA silently stops when its PSRAM buffer isn't 16-byte aligned, and since the heap layout settled the alignment once per boot, it looked like a hardware fault until libc was changed to 64-byte align audio buffers.

I've saved where the backup lives in my notes, along with its md5 and how to restore it.

If `lib_buffer.c` ever gets reverted (a `repo sync` will do it), put the fix back with:

```sh
cd ~/openvela/nuttx
patch libs/libc/audio/lib_buffer.c < ~/velapaw-golden/mic-rxalign-working/lib_buffer-rxalign.patch
rm -f libs/libc/bin/lib_buffer.o libs/libc/libc.a staging/libc.a
cd ~/openvela && ./build.sh esp32s3-devkit:waveshare_lcd -j4
xtensa-esp32s3-elf-objdump -d --disassemble=apb_alloc nuttx/nuttx | grep 'a10, 64'
```

- **The file name in the `patch` line is required.** The patch was made against `~/lib_buffer.c.pre-rxalign`, so `patch` can't tell which file to change by itself.
- **The last line checks the build.** It should print the `movi.n a10, 64` line. If it prints nothing, the build used the old code.
- **To restore the board only,** just reflash the backed-up `nuttx.bin`; no rebuild is needed.

Two optional things:
- Your other backup folders are write-protected, but this one isn't yet: `chmod -R a-w ~/velapaw-golden/mic-rxalign-working`
- This backup only exists on the VM. The copy in my session's temporary folder won't last, so tell me if you want one in `D:\openVela\velapaw-snapshots\`.

I also added an untested idea to my notes: the rule "never run `velapaw kws mic` before the dialog" may have been caused by the same bug. Each time the mic is reopened its buffers are allocated again, which gave another chance of a bad alignment. Keep following the rule until someone runs the dialog straight after a `kws mic` on this build.

11	**SHIPPED + HARDWARE-VERIFIED 2026-10-11.** `ask set bob's first meal to 7:30`
12	and `ask set bob's dinner to 19:15` both landed, and `status.md` read back
13	`- scheduled meals: 07:30 12:30 19:15` — two separate agent turns, both

16	(1563648 B) is the complete one; `3ad206ae3c0992c6da8ebacec20d0bf3`
17	(1563536 B) is the earlier build that wrote correctly but reported an error.
18	This is the path that replaces on-device voice for meal scheduling, which is
19	hardware-blocked (see [[velapaw-mic-capture]]).
20	
21	## The three pieces
22	
23	1. **`velapaw_meal_set_by_name(name, slot, minute)`** in
24	   `apps/examples/velapaw/identity/identity.c`. Pet ids are array indices that
25	   renumber on delete (`identity.h:52`), so a **name is the only stable handle**
26	   an agent or dialog can hold. It normalises both sides — lower-case, strip
27	   leading whitespace, trim trailing non-alphanumerics — because the enrolled
28	   pet on this board is literally `bob,` with a comma from the on-screen
29	   keyboard. The model sent `"pet": "bob"` and it matched; the normaliser
30	   earned its place on the first real call. Returns 0 / -1 bad args / -2 no
31	   such pet / -3 ambiguous / -4 rejected, else the save rc. It **copies all
32	   three slots** before writing one, because `velapaw_identity_update()` writes
33	   every slot it is handed; passing 0 for portion/limit means "leave alone".
34	2. **`vp_status_write()` publishes the meal times** as
35	   `- scheduled meals: HH:MM HH:MM HH:MM` (or `off`). This is why there is
36	   **no `get_meal_schedule` tool** — the agent already reaches `status.md`
37	   through `read_file`, so reading costs zero schema budget. That budget was
38	   hard-won (36→16 tools; see
39	   [[velapaw-ai-agent-integration-progress]]), and the write tool took it to 17
40	   builtin / Tools JSON 5245 B, still comfortable.
41	3. **`set_meal_schedule`** in `packages/ai_agent/src/tools/tool_meal.c`.
42	   Declares `velapaw_meal_set_by_name` by hand with `extern` rather than
43	   including `identity.h` — same FLAT image so it links, and the header would
44	   drag in the app's whole include path. Accepts `pet`/`pet_name`/`name`,
45	   `slot`/`meal`, and either `"HH:MM"` or separate `hour`/`minute`. Its success
46	   string **states the Model-B gate explicitly** ("dispenses it only when %s is
47	   recognised at the bowl at or after that time"), or the model promises the
48	   owner food appears on the clock alone, which is false.
49	
50	## THE TRAP: `Local tool shortcut: skip LLM round`
51	
52	`agent_loop.c` ~1230 short-circuits the turn when a round has exactly one
53	"local" tool call: it hands the raw tool output to the user as the final reply
54	and never does another LLM round. **That structurally kills every two-step
55	plan.** First run of the new tool: the model correctly called `read_file` on
56	`status.md` to find the pet name, the shortcut fired, the owner got a raw
57	status dump, and the meal was never set — `iters=1 tools=1`, `status=ok`. It
58	looks like a successful turn.
59	
60	The fix was already half-written in the file: an `is_instruction_read` escape
61	hatch exists for exactly this reason (skill files, `AGENT_HEARTBEAT_FILE`), and
62	`list_dir` had already been pulled out of the local set for the same bug with
63	the same symptom. Added `strstr(path, "/velapaw/")` to that condition —
64	everything in `/data/ai_agent/velapaw/` (`status.md`, `feed_log.md`,
65	`history.bin`) is **data to reason over, never a finished answer**. Correct
66	trace afterwards is `iters=2 tools=2` with a `set_meal_schedule` step, and
67	`[agent] Skill file read — no shortcut` in the log. **Read that trace line
68	before believing a turn worked** — `status=ok iters=1` is the failure mode.
69	
70	Deliberately did NOT "fix" this by rewriting the tool description to make the
71	model skip the read. Read-then-write is the correct behaviour (right name,
72	current times) and must not depend on the model choosing to skip a step.
73	
74	## SOLVED: the HTTP 400 invalid unicode code point was a use-after-free
75	
76	Every successful write used to end with the owner seeing `Sorry, I encountered
77	an error`, because the round *after* `set_meal_schedule` returned was rejected
78	with `[llm] API error 400: … messages[N].content: invalid unicode code point`.
79	The write was already on flash, so a working action reported failure.
80	
81	**Root cause, in `tool_meal.c`:** `cJSON_Delete(root)` ran while `const char
82	*pet` still pointed **into** that tree, and all six `switch` branches format
83	`pet` afterwards. The success string therefore carried raw freed-heap bytes at
84	the `%s`, and DeepSeek rejected the whole request. Fix is three lines — copy
85	the name into a `char petbuf[64]` and repoint `pet` at the copy **before** the
86	delete; reassigning `pet` covers all six branches without renaming anything.
87	Verified 2026-10-11 on firmware `9242daf64d1c9744f9d1ec917bf13d69`
88	(1563648 B): `result: 151 bytes`, no sanitiser warning, `status=ok iters=3
89	tools=2` in 5 s, real owner-facing reply.
90	
91	**The byte arithmetic was the signal all along.** The log said `result: 163
92	bytes`; hand-counting the format string twice gave 151. I trusted the count and
93	hunted an encoder bug instead of asking why the gap existed. `"Meal 2 for "` is
94	11 bytes and the diagnostic reported only 13 valid — corruption began exactly
95	at the `%s`, which names the variable.
96	
97	**Two theories falsified on the way — do not re-derive either.** (1) History
98	truncation: first failure at column 8230 against `hist=8192` looked conclusive;
99	`session_clear_all` reproduced it at column 4536 in a 10286-byte body.
100	(2) A stale over-read of `tool_output`: `cJSON_AddStringToObject` passes bytes
101	through verbatim and takes its own `strlen`, and `agent_tool_exec_streamed`
102	(`static inline` in `src/core/agent_mem.h:278`) is a clean malloc/execute/
103	memcpy with no appending — the message holds exactly our NUL-terminated bytes.
104	Also wrong: re-indexing `messages[N]` onto the assistant message. `msg[0]
105	role=user` proves the **system prompt is not in the messages array**.
106	
107	**Kept as defence:** `utf8_valid_prefix()` + `add_clean_string()` in
108	`agent_loop.c` now sanitise all four content sites (assistant `content` and
109	`reasoning_content`, single- and parallel-tool results), logging `[agent]
110	UTF-8: trimmed N of M byte(s) from "<key>"`. That warning is what localised
111	this bug; a malformed string no longer hard-fails a turn. The companion
112	`msg[N] role=… len=… utf8ok=…` dump fires on every tool round and is pure
113	noise now that it reads clean — remove it, keep the sanitiser.
114	
115	## Verification discipline that worked
116	
117	- `grep -ac "set_meal_schedule" nuttx/nuttx.bin` + `grep -ac "scheduled meals"`
118	  + `nm nuttx/nuttx | grep -E "velapaw_meal_set_by_name|tool_meal_set_execute"`
119	  as flash gates.
120	- `cat /data/ai_agent/velapaw/status.md` **before** any LLM call proves the
121	  VelaPaw half independently of the agent.
122	- The agent's reply text is never the discriminator — only `status.md` is. The
123	  model will happily narrate a write it never performed.
124	- `cat` does not exist at the `vela>` prompt; `quit` back to `nsh>` first.
125	- There is **no direct tool-invoke command** in the agent CLI (`help` lists
126	  none), so tool verification always costs an LLM round trip.
