I couldn't find the finals rules in your repo, so I can't tell you what the judges require. In practice, though, the answer is yes. The terminal is the agent's only interface: you type `ask` there and the reply comes back there. The LCD doesn't show the conversation, so if you hide the terminal the judges never see the agent.

How I'd run it:

- **Use the terminal only for the agent part.** Feeding, recognition, the voice dialog and the touchscreen all work without a terminal or a network. Demo those on the device first, then switch to the terminal. Your own docs make the same point: the agent is an optional extra on top of features that work fully on the device.
- **Make it readable on a projector.** Use PuTTY with a large font (20 pt or more) and clear the screen before you start. Two things will look odd unless you explain them:
  - Every `ask` prints two `[Agent]:` lines: a placeholder first, then the real reply.
  - Each tool step prints debug lines (`msg[N] role=…`). I can remove those before the finals if you want.
- **Show the change, not just the reply.** The model can describe a change it never made, so prove it. After `ask set bob's dinner to 19:15`, type `quit` to get back to `nsh>` and run `cat /data/ai_agent/velapaw/status.md`, or open bob's schedule on the LCD. Check during rehearsal whether the LCD shows the new time without a reboot; I haven't confirmed that.
- **Plan for the venue network.** The agent reaches DeepSeek through your laptop's internet sharing.
  - Rehearse on the network you'll actually have; a phone hotspot is the safest choice.
  - Before your slot, set the board's IP with `ifconfig`, start `ai_agent`, and ping the board from the laptop.
  - Bring a recording of a working run. If the venue has no internet, the agent can't run live and the recording is all you have.
- **Never open `config.json` on screen.** It contains the API key, and the projector would show it.
- **Show the heartbeat from a recording or log.** It only runs every 30 minutes, so you can't wait for it live.
Take a look at anything which can make me lose the competition

186	/* ---- persistence: intentionally RAM-only ----------------------------------
187	 * An earlier version stored a magic-tagged cell at flash 0x818000 (just past
188	 * identity's icon area). That raw spi_flash access WEDGED the SoC: a gray screen
189	 * at boot (the read) and a hard hang the instant you toggled language (the
190	 * write). 0x818000 is outside the range this board's spi_flash path handles
191	 * safely -- identity only ever touches 0x800000 (pets) and 0x810000 (icons).
192	 *
193	 * So language now lives only in RAM: the toggle works within a session and
194	 * resets to English on reboot -- fine for a demo. To persist it later, route it
195	 * through identity's proven flash helper (an in-range, erase-managed slot), not
196	 * a raw offset guessed to be "free". */
197	
198	void velapaw_lang_set(int lang)
199	{
200	  if (lang < 0 || lang >= VP_LANG_N)
201	    {
202	      return;
203	    }
204	  g_lang = lang;
205	}

209	  /* no-op -- RAM-only (see note above) */
210	}

212	/* ---- fonts ----------------------------------------------------------------
213	 * THE seam. Montserrat has no CJK glyphs, so today this always returns the
214	 * Latin fonts (Chinese would render blank). Build CONFIG_VELAPAW_FONT_CJK=y
215	 * with a generated CJK font linked (ui/README_I18N.md) and it returns that
216	 * instead -- every label switches to it automatically. The CJK font carries
217	 * Latin too, so it is used for both languages once present. */
218	const lv_font_t *velapaw_font(int level)
219	{
220	#ifdef CONFIG_VELAPAW_FONT_CJK
221	  extern const lv_font_t velapaw_font_cjk_20;
222	  extern const lv_font_t velapaw_font_cjk_16;
223	  extern const lv_font_t velapaw_font_cjk_14;
224	  /* The CJK subset has ASCII + Chinese but NOT the LV_SYMBOL_* icon glyphs
225	   * (bell/camera/OK/trash/... live in the FontAwesome range that only the
226	   * Montserrat builds carry). Chain each CJK font's fallback to the same-size
227	   * Montserrat, so any glyph the CJK font lacks -- i.e. the icons -- renders
228	   * from there. Copied into mutable statics because the generated fonts are
229	   * const; the .fallback field is the only thing we change. */
230	  static lv_font_t f20, f16, f14;
231	  static int inited;
232	  if (!inited)
233	    {
234	      f20 = velapaw_font_cjk_20; f20.fallback = &lv_font_montserrat_20;
235	      f16 = velapaw_font_cjk_16; f16.fallback = &lv_font_montserrat_16;
236	      f14 = velapaw_font_cjk_14; f14.fallback = &lv_font_montserrat_14;
237	      inited = 1;
238	    }
239	  switch (level)
240	    {
241	      case VP_FONT_TITLE: return &f20;
242	      case VP_FONT_HEAD:  return &f16;
243	      default:            return &f16;   /* BODY/SMALL bumped 14->16 for legibility */
244	    }
245	#else
246	  switch (level)
247	    {
248	      case VP_FONT_TITLE: return &lv_font_montserrat_20;
249	      case VP_FONT_HEAD:  return &lv_font_montserrat_16;
250	      default:            return &lv_font_montserrat_16;  /* BODY/SMALL 14->16 */
251	    }
252	#endif
253	}

1	/****************************************************************************
2	 * VelaPaw - enrollment store + cosine matcher (in-memory)
3	 *
4	 * Persistence is delegated to store/ (stub for now). Embeddings are assumed
5	 * L2-normalized, so cosine similarity == dot product.
6	 ****************************************************************************/
7	
8	#include <string.h>
9	#include <math.h>
10	#include <stdio.h>
11	#include <stdint.h>
12	#include <pthread.h>
13	#include "identity/identity.h"
14	
15	static struct velapaw_pet g_pets[VELAPAW_MAX_PETS];
16	static int                g_npets;
17	
18	/****************************************************************************
19	 * Flash persistence: enrolled pets survive a reset / power-off.
20	 *
21	 * Layout at VELAPAW_PET_FLASH_OFF (well past the models @0x600000 / @0x760000):
22	 *   magic "VPAW" | version | npets | g_pets[npets]      (raw POD copy)
23	 * A blank or garbage sector fails the magic check and reads as "no pets",
24	 * so we never restore nonsense.
25	 *
26	 * IMPORTANT: erase/write SUSPEND THE FLASH CACHE, so they must not run on a
27	 * PSRAM stack (the velapaw task's stack is PSRAM). Same trap the model loader
28	 * hit -- so, like backend_tflm.cc, we run them on a pthread whose stack is an
29	 * internal-RAM .bss buffer.
30	 ****************************************************************************/
31	
32	extern int spi_flash_read(uint32_t src, void *dst, uint32_t size);
33	extern int spi_flash_write(uint32_t dst, const void *src, uint32_t size);
34	extern int spi_flash_erase_range(uint32_t start, uint32_t size);
35	
36	#define VELAPAW_PET_FLASH_OFF  0x800000u          /* 8MB mark, past the models */
37	#define VELAPAW_PET_MAGIC      0x57415056u        /* "VPAW" */
38	#define VELAPAW_PET_VERSION    1u
39	
40	/* Header only (12 B). We deliberately do NOT keep a serialization copy of the
41	 * pets -- we write/read g_pets[] in place, so the RAM cost here is just the
42	 * header + the flash thread stack (~4 KB), not another 4.5 KB of pets. */
43	struct pet_hdr { uint32_t magic; uint32_t version; uint32_t npets; };
44	
45	#define PET_HDR_RESERVED  16u                     /* keeps pets 16-B aligned */
46	#define PET_AREA_BYTES    8192u                   /* 2 x 4 KB flash sectors  */
47	
48	static struct pet_hdr g_hdr;                      /* 12 bytes, .bss          */
49	static uint8_t g_pet_flash_stack[4096];           /* internal-RAM stack      */
50	
51	/* --- per-pet card icons ---------------------------------------------------
52	 * Kept in a SEPARATE flash region from the pet record so old pets still load,
53	 * and written only at enroll/delete (not on every schedule edit). The icon
54	 * buffers live in .bss (internal SRAM), so the flash write reads them
55	 * coherently while the cache is suspended -- no PSRAM bounce needed. */
56	#define VELAPAW_ICON_PX        (VELAPAW_ICON_W * VELAPAW_ICON_H)
57	#define VELAPAW_ICON_FLASH_OFF 0x810000u          /* past the pet record       */
58	#define VELAPAW_ICON_MAGIC     0x4E434956u        /* "VICN"                    */

17	(1563536 B) is the earlier build that wrote correctly but reported an error.
18	This is the path that replaces on-device voice for meal scheduling, which is
19	hardware-blocked (see [[velapaw-mic-capture]]).
20	
21	## The three pieces
22	
23	1. **`velapaw_meal_set_by_name(name, slot, minute)`** in
24	   `apps/examples/velapaw/identity/identity.c`. Pet ids are array indices that
25	   renumber on delete (`identity.h:52`), so a **name is the only stable handle**
26	   an agent or dialog can hold. It normalises both sides — lower-case, strip
27	   leading whitespace, trim trailing non-alphanumerics — because the enrolled
28	   pet on this board is literally `bob,` with a comma from the on-screen
29	   keyboard. The model sent `"pet": "bob"` and it matched; the normaliser
30	   earned its place on the first real call. Returns 0 / -1 bad args / -2 no
31	   such pet / -3 ambiguous / -4 rejected, else the save rc. It **copies all
32	   three slots** before writing one, because `velapaw_identity_update()` writes
33	   every slot it is handed; passing 0 for portion/limit means "leave alone".
34	2. **`vp_status_write()` publishes the meal times** as
35	   `- scheduled meals: HH:MM HH:MM HH:MM` (or `off`). This is why there is
36	   **no `get_meal_schedule` tool** — the agent already reaches `status.md`
37	   through `read_file`, so reading costs zero schema budget. That budget was
38	   hard-won (36→16 tools; see
39	   [[velapaw-ai-agent-integration-progress]]), and the write tool took it to 17
40	   builtin / Tools JSON 5245 B, still comfortable.
41	3. **`set_meal_schedule`** in `packages/ai_agent/src/tools/tool_meal.c`.
42	   Declares `velapaw_meal_set_by_name` by hand with `extern` rather than
43	   including `identity.h` — same FLAT image so it links, and the header would
44	   drag in the app's whole include path. Accepts `pet`/`pet_name`/`name`,
45	   `slot`/`meal`, and either `"HH:MM"` or separate `hour`/`minute`. Its success
46	   string **states the Model-B gate explicitly** ("dispenses it only when %s is
47	   recognised at the bowl at or after that time"), or the model promises the
48	   owner food appears on the clock alone, which is false.
49	
50	## THE TRAP: `Local tool shortcut: skip LLM round`
51	
52	`agent_loop.c` ~1230 short-circuits the turn when a round has exactly one
53	"local" tool call: it hands the raw tool output to the user as the final reply
54	and never does another LLM round. **That structurally kills every two-step
55	plan.** First run of the new tool: the model correctly called `read_file` on
56	`status.md` to find the pet name, the shortcut fired, the owner got a raw
57	status dump, and the meal was never set — `iters=1 tools=1`, `status=ok`. It
58	looks like a successful turn.
59	
60	The fix was already half-written in the file: an `is_instruction_read` escape
61	hatch exists for exactly this reason (skill files, `AGENT_HEARTBEAT_FILE`), and
62	`list_dir` had already been pulled out of the local set for the same bug with
63	the same symptom. Added `strstr(path, "/velapaw/")` to that condition —
64	everything in `/data/ai_agent/velapaw/` (`status.md`, `feed_log.md`,
65	`history.bin`) is **data to reason over, never a finished answer**. Correct
66	trace afterwards is `iters=2 tools=2` with a `set_meal_schedule` step, and
67	`[agent] Skill file read — no shortcut` in the log. **Read that trace line
68	before believing a turn worked** — `status=ok iters=1` is the failure mode.
69	
70	Deliberately did NOT "fix" this by rewriting the tool description to make the
71	model skip the read. Read-then-write is the correct behaviour (right name,
72	current times) and must not depend on the model choosing to skip a step.
73	
74	## SOLVED: the HTTP 400 invalid unicode code point was a use-after-free
75	
76	Every successful write used to end with the owner seeing `Sorry, I encountered
77	an error`, because the round *after* `set_meal_schedule` returned was rejected
78	with `[llm] API error 400: … messages[N].content: invalid unicode code point`.
79	The write was already on flash, so a working action reported failure.
80	
81	**Root cause, in `tool_meal.c`:** `cJSON_Delete(root)` ran while `const char
82	*pet` still pointed **into** that tree, and all six `switch` branches format
83	`pet` afterwards. The success string therefore carried raw freed-heap bytes at
84	the `%s`, and DeepSeek rejected the whole request. Fix is three lines — copy
85	the name into a `char petbuf[64]` and repoint `pet` at the copy **before** the
86	delete; reassigning `pet` covers all six branches without renaming anything.
87	Verified 2026-10-11 on firmware `9242daf64d1c9744f9d1ec917bf13d69`
88	(1563648 B): `result: 151 bytes`, no sanitiser warning, `status=ok iters=3
89	tools=2` in 5 s, real owner-facing reply.
90	
91	**The byte arithmetic was the signal all along.** The log said `result: 163
92	bytes`; hand-counting the format string twice gave 151. I trusted the count and
93	hunted an encoder bug instead of asking why the gap existed. `"Meal 2 for "` is
94	11 bytes and the diagnostic reported only 13 valid — corruption began exactly
95	at the `%s`, which names the variable.
96	
97	**Two theories falsified on the way — do not re-derive either.** (1) History
98	truncation: first failure at column 8230 against `hist=8192` looked conclusive;
99	`session_clear_all` reproduced it at column 4536 in a 10286-byte body.
100	(2) A stale over-read of `tool_output`: `cJSON_AddStringToObject` passes bytes
101	through verbatim and takes its own `strlen`, and `agent_tool_exec_streamed`
102	(`static inline` in `src/core/agent_mem.h:278`) is a clean malloc/execute/
103	memcpy with no appending — the message holds exactly our NUL-terminated bytes.
104	Also wrong: re-indexing `messages[N]` onto the assistant message. `msg[0]
105	role=user` proves the **system prompt is not in the messages array**.
106	
107	**Kept as defence:** `utf8_valid_prefix()` + `add_clean_string()` in
108	`agent_loop.c` now sanitise all four content sites (assistant `content` and
109	`reasoning_content`, single- and parallel-tool results), logging `[agent]
110	UTF-8: trimmed N of M byte(s) from "<key>"`. That warning is what localised
111	this bug; a malformed string no longer hard-fails a turn. The companion
112	`msg[N] role=… len=… utf8ok=…` dump fires on every tool round and is pure
113	noise now that it reads clean — remove it, keep the sanitiser.
114	
115	## Verification discipline that worked
116	
117	- `grep -ac "set_meal_schedule" nuttx/nuttx.bin` + `grep -ac "scheduled meals"`
118	  + `nm nuttx/nuttx | grep -E "velapaw_meal_set_by_name|tool_meal_set_execute"`
119	  as flash gates.
120	- `cat /data/ai_agent/velapaw/status.md` **before** any LLM call proves the
121	  VelaPaw half independently of the agent.
122	- The agent's reply text is never the discriminator — only `status.md` is. The
123	  model will happily narrate a write it never performed.
124	- `cat` does not exist at the `vela>` prompt; `quit` back to `nsh>` first.
125	- There is **no direct tool-invoke command** in the agent CLI (`help` lists
126	  none), so tool verification always costs an LLM round trip.

11	The VM's `apps/examples/velapaw/Makefile` is **untracked by git** — if it's clobbered, git cannot restore it. I destroyed it once (2026-07-13) by copying the contest repo's Makefile over it; they are NOT the same file (the contest one uses `-I$(APPDIR)/packages/demos/contest2026_043_velapaw`, mock camera, and stub inference). Master copy now lives at `D:\openVela\contest2026_043_CircuitForge\app\velapaw\Makefile`.
12	
13	**How to recover it if lost again:** the `.o` files from the last good build are a fingerprint of the real source list — `find . -name '*.o'` in the app dir tells you exactly what was compiled. `CMakeLists.txt` (the mirror build) gives the flags/defines.
14	
15	**⚠️ THE BIG ONE — never put `-DTF_LITE_STATIC_MEMORY` in this Makefile.** The Make-built TFLM library (`apps/mlearning/tflite-micro/Makefile`) does **not** define it, and that macro **changes the layout of `TfLiteTensor`** in `tensorflow/lite/core/c/common.h`. Define it on the app side only and the two disagree on field offsets: `AllocateTensors` still succeeds (all inside the library), then **the first `Invoke()` writes through a garbage pointer and HARD-WEDGES THE SoC** — console dies ("semaphore timeout" on open), no crash dump, on *any* thread, from *any* tab. It looks exactly like a camera/DMA/stack bug and it is none of those. Cost a full evening (2026-07-13): I blamed the servo, then idle camera streaming, then the PSRAM stack, all wrong. **`CMakeLists.txt` DOES define it — correctly, because the CMake `tflite_micro` target compiles the library with it too. So flags from the CMake build are NOT portable into this Makefile.** Symptom to recognize instantly: models load, `AllocateTensors OK`, then the board dies on the first inference.
16	
17	**The other flags that each cost a failed build:**
18	1. `CXXEXT = .cc` — NuttX `Application.mk`'s C++ pattern rule keys off `CXXEXT` (default `.cxx`). Without this, `.cc` sources give *"target doesn't match the target pattern"* and `g++: fatal error: no input files`.
19	2. **Mirror tflite-micro's `-D` set exactly** (from `apps/mlearning/tflite-micro/Makefile`, and note the debug trio is an **if/else — not all three**): ours is the strip branch → `TF_LITE_STRIP_ERROR_STRINGS` (NOT `TF_LITE_SHOW_MEMORY_USE`/`TF_LITE_USE_CTIME`, which are the `CONFIG_TFLITEMICRO_DEBUG=y` branch), plus `TFLITE_EMULATE_FLOAT`, `TF_LITE_DISABLE_X86_NEON`, `TF_LITE_USE_GLOBAL_CMATH_FUNCTIONS`, and the esp-nn block `-DESP_NN=1 -DCONFIG_NN_OPTIMIZED -mlongcalls`. `TF_LITE_STRIP_ERROR_STRINGS` compiles `MicroPrintf()` *out of the library*, so an app built without it → `undefined reference to MicroPrintf` at link (that link error is a useful *confirmation* of which branch the library used).
20	3. `CXXFLAGS += -fno-threadsafe-statics` — see [[velapaw-tflm-onboard]]; without it TFLM deadlocks in `__cxa_guard_acquire` → blue screen.
21	
22	**Rule of thumb:** the app and the prebuilt TFLM library share headers, so ANY header-visible define must match on both sides. When inference misbehaves in a way that makes no sense, diff the app's flags against the library's Makefile before suspecting hardware.
23	
24	TFLM's `Make.defs` does NOT export include dirs globally, so velapaw must carry its own `-I`: TFLM root + `third_party/flatbuffers/include` + `$(APPDIR)/math/{gemmlowp,kissfft,ruy}/*`, plus `-include .../float_shim.h -fpermissive`. Also `STACKSIZE = 32768` (LVGL) and `-DVELAPAW_HAVE_BCS` on **both** CFLAGS and CXXFLAGS.
25	
26	## ⚠️ Two silent stale-build traps — `make` lies about having rebuilt
27	
28	Both look **identical to a successful build of unchanged source**: `make -j8`
29	goes straight from the linker-script `CPP:` steps to `LD: nuttx`, no `CC:` of
30	any app file, `Generated: nuttx.bin`, exit 0. NuttX embeds a build timestamp,
31	so the image even has a *new md5* at the *same size*. Nothing warns you.
32	
33	1. **Missing/incorrect `Make.defs`.** An app joins `CONFIGURED_APPS` via a
34	   `Make.defs` in its own directory. Registering a directory that does not
35	   exist drops the app silently — `make` skips it and links stale objects out
36	   of `libapps.a`. The contest repo's version pointed at
37	   `packages/demos/contest2026_043_velapaw`, which does not exist in the VM;
38	   it now probes for `$(APPDIR)/examples/velapaw/Makefile` first.
39	2. **Stale `Make.dep` / `.built`** (hit 2026-08-05, build 43). After a
40	   `make apps_clean`, the app dir's `Make.dep` no longer describes the current
41	   sources, so make has no rule connecting `mic.o` to a rewritten `mic.c`. It
42	   writes a fresh `.built` and moves on. Tell-tale: `.built`/`.depend`/
43	   `Make.dep` timestamps NEWER than the source you just extracted.
44	
45	**Therefore, after extracting any new tarball into the VM app dir:**
46	
47	```sh
48	cd ~/openvela/apps/examples/velapaw && \
49	rm -f .built .depend Make.dep && find . -name "*.o" -delete
50	```
51	
52	**And always prove the new code is in the image before flashing** — pick a
53	string only the new build contains:
54	`grep -ac "some new printf text" nuttx.bin` must be non-zero. `strings` is not
55	available in this Git Bash; `grep -a` on the binary works.
56	
57	Related: **never `rm -rf` the app dir in a fetch command — extract over the
58	top.** Doing so on 2026-08-04 destroyed `ui/ hal/ infer/ identity/ store/
59	assets/` and `Make.defs`, because the tarball only carried `voice/`.
60	
61	Real sources (not the contest repo's): `hal/camera_ov5640.c` (real camera), `hal/feeder_servo.c` (real servo, was `feeder_mock.c`), `ui/ui_lvgl.c`, `assets/velapaw_assets.c`, `infer/backend_tflm.cc` + `infer/gen/velapaw_model_data.cc` (pre-generated, committed — no Python gen step in the Make path).

10	
11	**Symptom (2026-09-22):** on the board, tapping a not-yet-eaten meal row on My Pets did
12	nothing — no "skipped" label. Everything else in the app worked.
13	
14	**Root cause: the feature was never in the flashed firmware, it was not broken.**
15	It shipped and ran on 2026-08-08 (`D:\openVela\velapaw-snapshots\2026-08-08-skipmeal\`,
16	whose RESTORE.md still claimed "⭐ CURRENTLY ON THE BOARD"), was lost in the
17	2026-08-10 b82-camerafix reconstruction (see [[velapaw-b82-camerafix-rebuild]]), and
18	was never put back. The git branch has had it since `af9791d`; the **VM build tree
19	`~/openvela/apps/examples/velapaw/ui/` did not** (`grep -c g_meal_skipped` → 0).
20	
21	**The forensic test that proved it without touching the board:** read `nuttx.bin` with
22	`[Text.Encoding]::GetEncoding(28591)` (byte-preserving; `Latin1` does not exist in
23	.NET Framework 4.x) and check *all ~70* English i18n strings. Exactly one was missing —
24	`"  %02d:%02d   skipped"`. One missing string out of a whole table pinpoints the one
25	source change absent from the build. Checking a single string proves nothing.
26	
27	**THE TRAP — never straight-copy the branch UI files onto the VM.** The VM
28	`ui_lvgl.c` is *ahead* of `dev-ai-contest-2026`: it heap-allocates `g_img565`,
29	`g_thumb565` and `g_voice_audio` (`malloc`, was `.bss`), which is the DRAM the
30	ai_agent integration needed. A file copy silently reverts that. Diff before copying,
31	always, and patch surgically instead. `ui_i18n.c`/`ui_i18n.h` *are* safe to copy —
32	their only diff from the VM copy is the `S_SKIPPED` row.
33	
34	**Restore recipe (done, hardware-verified):** 9-hunk patch built and round-trip
35	validated on Windows (reverse-apply → forward-apply → `diff -q` identical), pasted to
36	the VM as a heredoc, `patch -l -p0` (the `-l` matters: two hunks contain blank context
37	lines). Then clear the stale-object trap (`ui/*.o`, `ui_lvgl.c.tmp.*`, `.built`,
38	`.depend`, `Make.dep`), `./build.sh esp32s3-devkit:waveshare_lcd -j4`.
39	
40	**Gate before flashing:** `grep -ac "skipped" nuttx/nuttx.bin` must be **2** (1 = only
41	the mbedTLS string, the build didn't take); `grep -ac "%02d:%02d   skipped"` must be 1.
42	Image went 1,561,920 → 1,561,976 B (+56).
43	
44	**Flashing is done from Windows, not the VM.** Board enumerates as `USB Serial Device
45	(COM3)`, USB-Serial/JTAG, MAC 1c:db:d4:79:7e:f8. No `esptool` on PATH — use
46	`python -m esptool` (5.3.1). Transfer the image with the user's own `python3 -m
47	http.server 8000` on the VM (VMnet8: VM = 192.168.160.128, host = .1) and
48	`Invoke-WebRequest`. `write_flash 0x0` touches only 0x0–0x17dfff, so the models at
49	`0x600000`/`0x760000` and `/data` at `0x180000` survive.
50	
51	**Known remaining defect (not urgent, cleared on boot):** `g_meal_skipped` is a
52	dateless `uint8_t`, so a skip does *not* expire at real midnight — only on reboot or
53	the demo Next Day button. Fix would be `long g_meal_skip_day[][]` compared against
54	`wall_day()`, mirroring `g_meal_fed_day`. Related: [[velapaw-feeding-history-daystamp]].

text:
I've written the agent-on-the-LCD change and tested the patch on Windows. It hasn't been compiled yet because there's no C compiler on Windows, so your VM build is the first compile.

**Your question about My Pets:** no, it didn't update before. My Pets only redrew when you switched into that tab. If the screen was already on My Pets when the agent changed a meal, the old time stayed until you left the tab and came back. The patch fixes that.

**What the patch does** (6 files):
- **A toast under the bell, for `ask`.** It shows "You: <your question>", then "Agent working… N s" counting up, then the reply. It stays 30 s, and a tap dismisses it.
- **The same toast, for the heartbeat.**
  - An all-clear shows in green for 10 s.
  - A warning shows in red and stays. It also turns the bell red and is listed in the bell panel until the next all-clear.
  - A heartbeat that fails shows nothing, which keeps a dead network from cluttering the screen at your offline defense.
- **Live My Pets.** When the agent changes a meal, the card redraws immediately on whatever tab is showing. If the Edit dialog is open, it picks up the change too, so pressing Save can't put the old time back.
- **Both languages.** The Chinese strings only use characters the font already has.

## 1. Apply on the VM
Open [item8-vm-apply.sh](../AppData/Local/Temp/claude/c--Users-VICTUS-openVela/3659500b-38f3-47db-bbd0-9b2aab159cd9/scratchpad/item8-tools/item8-vm-apply.sh), copy the whole file, and paste it into the VM terminal. It does five things, and stops without changing anything if a check fails:
1. Checks that the six VM files are the pristine copies.
2. Backs them up, plus the current `nuttx.bin`, to `~/velapaw-golden/pre-item8-agent-lcd/`.
3. Checks that the patch arrived intact.
4. Dry-runs the patch.
5. Applies it and checks the results.

All of steps 1 and 5 must say `OK`. I ran this exact file against a copy of your tree: it applied cleanly, and a second paste refused to run.

## 2. Purge and build
Every velapaw object has to rebuild, because the new strings shift the string IDs that every UI file uses. Expect a longer build than usual.
```bash
cd ~/openvela/apps/examples/velapaw && rm -f .built .depend Make.dep ui/ui_lvgl.c.tmp.* && find . -name '*.o' -delete
find ~/openvela -path '*ai_agent*' \( -name '*.o' -o -name .built -o -name .depend -o -name Make.dep \) -delete
cd ~/openvela && ./build.sh esp32s3-devkit:waveshare_lcd -j4 2>&1 | tee /tmp/item8-build.log | tail -n 20
```

## 3. Checks (paste me the output)
```bash
cd ~/openvela
grep -nE 'warning|error' /tmp/item8-build.log | grep -E 'ui_lvgl|ui_i18n|identity|agent_loop'
s=$(stat -c %s nuttx/nuttx.bin); echo "size $s room $((1572864 - s))"; md5sum nuttx/nuttx.bin
grep -ac "Agent working" nuttx/nuttx.bin
nm nuttx/nuttx | grep -E 'velapaw_agent_event|velapaw_identity_gen'
find . -path '*ai_agent*' -name 'agent_loop*.o' -exec nm {} \; | grep velapaw_agent_event
```
Expected:
- The warnings line prints nothing.
- **`room` is greater than 0.** If it isn't, do not flash, because the image would overwrite `/data`. There was only about 8.9 KB to spare.
- The string count is `1`.
- `nm` shows both symbols with type `T`.
- The last line shows `U velapaw_agent_event`, which proves the agent half was rebuilt too.

## 4. Flash
Once the checks pass, run `cd ~/openvela/nuttx && python3 -m http.server 8000 --bind 0.0.0.0` and tell me. I'll download the image, match its md5, check the COM port, and flash with `write-flash 0x0`.

## 5. Test on the board
Start it with your usual pattern, open **My Pets**, and note bob's dinner time.
1. **Live update:** `ask set bob's dinner to 18:30`. The toast should appear within a second and count up, then show the reply, and bob's card should change to 18:30 with no reboot. Check against `status.md`.
2. **Edit dialog:** tap Edit on bob and leave it open. Run `ask set bob's breakfast to 07:45`. The dialog should change to 07:45. Press Save, and `status.md` should still say 07:45.
3. **Heartbeat:** run `heartbeat_trigger` and look for the green all-clear, or a red warning with a red bell. It only fires if HEARTBEAT.md has an item to act on.
4. **Language:** tap 中 while the toast is up. It should come back in Chinese.

**Limits to know for the demo:**
- While the toast is up, it covers the right end of the tab bar (Trends). Tap it to dismiss.
- If the model replies in Chinese, characters the font doesn't have show as blanks. Ask in English during the demo.
- A heartbeat warning keeps the bell red until the next all-clear or a reboot.

To roll back, run `patch -R -p1 < /tmp/item8.patch` in `~/openvela`, or copy the files back from the backup folder, then purge and rebuild.

16	(1563648 B) is the complete one; `3ad206ae3c0992c6da8ebacec20d0bf3`
17	(1563536 B) is the earlier build that wrote correctly but reported an error.
18	This is the path that replaces on-device voice for meal scheduling, which is
19	hardware-blocked (see [[velapaw-mic-capture]]).
20	
21	## The three pieces
22	
23	1. **`velapaw_meal_set_by_name(name, slot, minute)`** in
24	   `apps/examples/velapaw/identity/identity.c`. Pet ids are array indices that
25	   renumber on delete (`identity.h:52`), so a **name is the only stable handle**
26	   an agent or dialog can hold. It normalises both sides — lower-case, strip
27	   leading whitespace, trim trailing non-alphanumerics — because the enrolled
28	   pet on this board is literally `bob,` with a comma from the on-screen
29	   keyboard. The model sent `"pet": "bob"` and it matched; the normaliser
30	   earned its place on the first real call. Returns 0 / -1 bad args / -2 no
31	   such pet / -3 ambiguous / -4 rejected, else the save rc. It **copies all
32	   three slots** before writing one, because `velapaw_identity_update()` writes
33	   every slot it is handed; passing 0 for portion/limit means "leave alone".
34	2. **`vp_status_write()` publishes the meal times** as
35	   `- scheduled meals: HH:MM HH:MM HH:MM` (or `off`). This is why there is
36	   **no `get_meal_schedule` tool** — the agent already reaches `status.md`
37	   through `read_file`, so reading costs zero schema budget. That budget was
38	   hard-won (36→16 tools; see
39	   [[velapaw-ai-agent-integration-progress]]), and the write tool took it to 17
40	   builtin / Tools JSON 5245 B, still comfortable.
41	3. **`set_meal_schedule`** in `packages/ai_agent/src/tools/tool_meal.c`.
42	   Declares `velapaw_meal_set_by_name` by hand with `extern` rather than
43	   including `identity.h` — same FLAT image so it links, and the header would
44	   drag in the app's whole include path. Accepts `pet`/`pet_name`/`name`,
45	   `slot`/`meal`, and either `"HH:MM"` or separate `hour`/`minute`. Its success
46	   string **states the Model-B gate explicitly** ("dispenses it only when %s is
47	   recognised at the bowl at or after that time"), or the model promises the
48	   owner food appears on the clock alone, which is false.
49	
50	## THE TRAP: `Local tool shortcut: skip LLM round`
51	
52	`agent_loop.c` ~1230 short-circuits the turn when a round has exactly one
53	"local" tool call: it hands the raw tool output to the user as the final reply
54	and never does another LLM round. **That structurally kills every two-step
55	plan.** First run of the new tool: the model correctly called `read_file` on
56	`status.md` to find the pet name, the shortcut fired, the owner got a raw
57	status dump, and the meal was never set — `iters=1 tools=1`, `status=ok`. It
58	looks like a successful turn.
59	
60	The fix was already half-written in the file: an `is_instruction_read` escape
61	hatch exists for exactly this reason (skill files, `AGENT_HEARTBEAT_FILE`), and
62	`list_dir` had already been pulled out of the local set for the same bug with
63	the same symptom. Added `strstr(path, "/velapaw/")` to that condition —
64	everything in `/data/ai_agent/velapaw/` (`status.md`, `feed_log.md`,
65	`history.bin`) is **data to reason over, never a finished answer**. Correct
66	trace afterwards is `iters=2 tools=2` with a `set_meal_schedule` step, and
67	`[agent] Skill file read — no shortcut` in the log. **Read that trace line
68	before believing a turn worked** — `status=ok iters=1` is the failure mode.
69	
70	Deliberately did NOT "fix" this by rewriting the tool description to make the
71	model skip the read. Read-then-write is the correct behaviour (right name,
72	current times) and must not depend on the model choosing to skip a step.
73	
74	## SOLVED: the HTTP 400 invalid unicode code point was a use-after-free
75	
76	Every successful write used to end with the owner seeing `Sorry, I encountered
77	an error`, because the round *after* `set_meal_schedule` returned was rejected
78	with `[llm] API error 400: … messages[N].content: invalid unicode code point`.
79	The write was already on flash, so a working action reported failure.
80	
81	**Root cause, in `tool_meal.c`:** `cJSON_Delete(root)` ran while `const char
82	*pet` still pointed **into** that tree, and all six `switch` branches format
83	`pet` afterwards. The success string therefore carried raw freed-heap bytes at
84	the `%s`, and DeepSeek rejected the whole request. Fix is three lines — copy
85	the name into a `char petbuf[64]` and repoint `pet` at the copy **before** the
86	delete; reassigning `pet` covers all six branches without renaming anything.
87	Verified 2026-10-11 on firmware `9242daf64d1c9744f9d1ec917bf13d69`
88	(1563648 B): `result: 151 bytes`, no sanitiser warning, `status=ok iters=3
89	tools=2` in 5 s, real owner-facing reply.
90	
91	**The byte arithmetic was the signal all along.** The log said `result: 163
92	bytes`; hand-counting the format string twice gave 151. I trusted the count and
93	hunted an encoder bug instead of asking why the gap existed. `"Meal 2 for "` is
94	11 bytes and the diagnostic reported only 13 valid — corruption began exactly
95	at the `%s`, which names the variable.
96	
97	**Two theories falsified on the way — do not re-derive either.** (1) History
98	truncation: first failure at column 8230 against `hist=8192` looked conclusive;
99	`session_clear_all` reproduced it at column 4536 in a 10286-byte body.
100	(2) A stale over-read of `tool_output`: `cJSON_AddStringToObject` passes bytes
101	through verbatim and takes its own `strlen`, and `agent_tool_exec_streamed`
102	(`static inline` in `src/core/agent_mem.h:278`) is a clean malloc/execute/
103	memcpy with no appending — the message holds exactly our NUL-terminated bytes.
104	Also wrong: re-indexing `messages[N]` onto the assistant message. `msg[0]
105	role=user` proves the **system prompt is not in the messages array**.
106	
107	**Kept as defence:** `utf8_valid_prefix()` + `add_clean_string()` in
108	`agent_loop.c` now sanitise all four content sites (assistant `content` and
109	`reasoning_content`, single- and parallel-tool results), logging `[agent]
110	UTF-8: trimmed N of M byte(s) from "<key>"`. That warning is what localised
111	this bug; a malformed string no longer hard-fails a turn. The companion
112	`msg[N] role=… len=… utf8ok=…` dump fires on every tool round and is pure
113	noise now that it reads clean — remove it, keep the sanitiser.
114	
115	## Verification discipline that worked
116	
117	- `grep -ac "set_meal_schedule" nuttx/nuttx.bin` + `grep -ac "scheduled meals"`
118	  + `nm nuttx/nuttx | grep -E "velapaw_meal_set_by_name|tool_meal_set_execute"`
119	  as flash gates.
120	- `cat /data/ai_agent/velapaw/status.md` **before** any LLM call proves the
121	  VelaPaw half independently of the agent.
122	- The agent's reply text is never the discriminator — only `status.md` is. The
123	  model will happily narrate a write it never performed.
124	- `cat` does not exist at the `vela>` prompt; `quit` back to `nsh>` first.
125	- There is **no direct tool-invoke command** in the agent CLI (`help` lists
126	  none), so tool verification always costs an LLM round trip.

text: Reading the log: the screen is probably right, and the agent is the one that's wrong. Checking two things in the source before I explain.

I think the screen is right and the agent is what's wrong. Only one of your three asks changed anything.

| Ask | Did it change the feeder? | Evidence in the log |
|---|---|---|
| dinner → 18:30 | No | It read the status file, saw 18:30 there, and replied "no change needed". |
| breakfast → 07:45 | **Yes** | `set_meal_schedule` ran and printed `saved 1 pet(s) to flash rc=0`. |
| dinner → 18:50 | **No**, but the agent said "Done" | `tools=1`: it only read the file, never set anything, then claimed it had. |

The third ask also didn't reach the agent as you typed it. The board printed `Sent to agent: … 18:30`, and the message was 31 bytes instead of 25, so invisible editing keys (arrows or backspace) went in with it. For the demo, type each `ask` fresh and don't edit the line.

**The root cause is my bug.** The agent learns the current meal times from `status.md`, and that file is only rewritten at boot, after a feed, an enroll, or a body-condition update. Changing a meal time doesn't rewrite it, whether the change comes from the agent or the touchscreen. Your log shows it: a minute after breakfast became 07:45, the agent still listed Bob's meals as "05:00, 07:00, …". So after the first change in a boot, the agent works from an old copy. It can say "already set" when it isn't, and it repeats old times. Those are the "old ones still there", but in its replies, not on the LCD.

**Proposed fix:**
1. Rewrite `status.md` every time a meal time changes, from the agent or from the edit dialog.
2. Add one line to the meal tool's description: "never tell the owner a meal changed unless this tool returned success in this turn."
3. Strip escape bytes and backspaces from `ask` input, so a mistyped line arrives clean.

**Please check these on the board:**

1. **Look at My Pets now.** Does Bob show **07:45 / 07:00 / 18:30**? If yes, the LCD side works.
2. **Optional:** check the status file is stale. Type `quit` to get back to `nsh>`, then run:
   ```
   cat /data/ai_agent/velapaw/status.md
   ```
   I expect it still says `scheduled meals: 05:00 07:00 18:30`.
3. **Serve the source folder so I can write the fix.** The fix touches the store file, which I don't have from the VM. The current server only shares `nuttx/`, so stop it with Ctrl+C and start one from the source root:
   ```
   cd ~/openvela && python3 -m http.server 8000 --bind 0.0.0.0
   ```
   Tell me when it's running, and I'll download the store file, its header, and the `ask` command's source.

# Line-for-line port of the cmd_ask sanitiser in nsh_commands.c.
def clean(b):
    c = bytearray(b) + b"\0"
    w = 0
    r = 0
    while c[r] != 0:
        ch = c[r]
        if ch == 0x1b:
            if c[r + 1] in (ord('['), ord('O')):
                r += 2
                while c[r] != 0 and (c[r] < 0x40 or c[r] > 0x7e):
                    r += 1
                if c[r] == 0:
                    break
            elif c[r + 1] != 0:
                r += 1
            r += 1
            continue
        if ch in (0x08, 0x7f):
            while w > 0 and (c[w - 1] & 0xc0) == 0x80:
                w -= 1
            if w > 0:
                w -= 1
            r += 1
            continue
        if ch < 0x20:
            r += 1
            continue
        c[w] = ch
        w += 1
        r += 1
    return bytes(c[:w])

cases = [
    (b"set bob's dinner to 18:50", b"set bob's dinner to 18:50"),
    (b"set bob's dinner to 18:3\x7f50", b"set bob's dinner to 18:50"),
    (b"set bob's dinner to 18:30\x08\x0850", b"set bob's dinner to 18:50"),
    (b"set bob's dinner to 18:30\x1b[D\x1b[D", b"set bob's dinner to 18:30"),
    (b"set\x1bOD bob", b"set bob"),
    (b"x\x1b[1;5Dy", b"xy"),
    (b"abc\x1b", b"abc"),
    (b"abc\x1b[", b"abc"),
    (b"abc\x1b[12", b"abc"),
    (b"\x7f\x7fhi", b"hi"),
    ("喂食".encode() + b"\x7f", "喂".encode()),
    ("喂食".encode(), "喂食".encode()),
    (b"to \x7f18", b"to18"),
    (b"\x1b[A\x1b[A", b""),
]
ok = True
for src, want in cases:
    got = clean(src)
    flag = "OK " if got == want else "BAD"
    ok &= got == want
    print(flag, repr(src), "->", repr(got))
print("ALL PASS" if ok else "FAILURES")

Show its last reply or heartbeat warning under the bell. Also make My Pets show a meal time the agent just changed without a reboot; I haven't confirmed it does. Then the demo becomes "watch the feeder change", not "read the terminal"."

   - The user does NOT want the contest submission process or rules investigated.

2. Key Technical Concepts:
   - **Platform:**
     - openVela/NuttX FLAT build on ESP32-S3 (Waveshare 3.5" LCD).
     - ai_agent calls velapaw functions through a hand-written `extern` (same image).
     - LVGL 9.1 is UI-thread only. Cross-thread changes are signalled by the `g_ident_gen` counter, polled by `ident_poll()` in the UI loop.
   - **status.md (`/data/ai_agent/velapaw/status.md`):**
     - Written by the static `vp_status_write()` in store_stub.c.
     - Includes "- scheduled meals: HH:MM HH:MM HH:MM".
     - Rewritten only at `velapaw_store_init` (boot), `log_feeding`, `seed`, `roll_day`, `delete` and `set_bcs`.
     - NOT rewritten when a meal time changes (agent tool, Edit dialog, voice dialog via edit_save), so the agent reads stale times.
     - On delete, `velapaw_store_delete` writes status before `velapaw_identity_delete`, so names are misaligned with history.
   - **The agent reads meal times only via read_file of status.md;** there is no get tool. The agent's reply text is never proof of a change: check the trace for a `set_meal_schedule` step and the "saved … rc=0" line.
   - **The model can hallucinate "Done" without calling the tool.** Observed: tools=1, read_file only.
   - **`ask` input:** cli_thread uses `fgets` on stdin, `tokenise` splits on " \t\r\n", and cmd_ask joins argv. Raw terminal editing bytes (ESC sequences, BS/DEL) reach the agent. Evidence: a 31-byte message shown as "…18:30" while the user saw "18:50".
   - **Littlefs writes directly from task stacks are safe:** all stacks are in internal SRAM (`XTENSA_IMEM`). identity.c's worker-thread pattern is obsolete for new code.
   - **The VM source files use CRLF line endings throughout.** Edits must keep CRLF; verified that they do.
   - **Build traps:**
     - Purge: `rm -f .built .depend Make.dep` plus `find . -name '*.o' -delete` in the app dir, and `find ~/openvela -path '*ai_agent*' \( -name '*.o' -o -name .built -o -name .depend -o -name Make.dep \) -delete`.
     - Image must be < 1,572,864 B.
     - Gates: `grep -ac` on the .bin and `nm` on nuttx/nuttx.
   - **Flash from Windows:** `python -m esptool --chip esp32s3 --port COM3 write-flash 0x0 <file>`. The image is fetched from the VM http server (192.168.160.128:8000) with `Invoke-WebRequest -UseBasicParsing -TimeoutSec 10`.

The fix is ready to paste. I ran the apply script against a copy of your files and the output matched my edited versions byte for byte. A second run stops at the first check without changing anything, so pasting it twice is safe.

**What it changes:**
- **The agent sees the new times.** `status.md` is the only place the agent reads meal times from, and until now it was rewritten only at boot or after a feed. It's now also rewritten after an agent change, an Edit dialog or voice-dialog save, and a pet deletion. This is why the agent told you breakfast was 05:00 one turn after it moved it to 07:45.
- **No more fake "Done".** The tool's description now says a meal only changes when the tool succeeds. Your 18:50 request got "Done" back without the tool ever being called.
- **Typing corrections now reach the agent.** Backspace and arrow-key bytes are now applied or dropped before the message is sent, so what you see is what the agent gets.

It's the USB link, not the meal-time patch, and not ICS:
- The board's last request went out to DeepSeek.
- From then on, nothing came back from Windows: not the answer, not the DNS replies (`-11`), not my pings. Windows can't even get an ARP reply from the board, so its neighbour entry stays `Incomplete`.
- Windows' routing table is correct, and ICS is still serving DNS and DHCP.

So the Windows→board direction stopped working, and the board waited about 10 minutes before giving up.

Bob's lunch was still saved as 12:00 (`rc=0`) and is on screen. The 请求超时 only means the agent couldn't send its confirmation; it doesn't mean the change failed.

**One honest suspect.** The link died in the 1.5 seconds between the agent's second answer, which arrived fine, and its third request. In that window `set_meal_schedule` wrote to flash twice: the identity save, plus the new `status.md` refresh from today's patch. Ask 1 did the same two writes and its link survived. Its first ARP also failed before any write, so the link was already flaky. One case can't decide it, so the next run will.

**1. Before you reset, while the board is still in this state,** run at `nsh>` and paste the output:
```
ifconfig
cat /proc/iobinfo
```
`/proc/iobinfo` shows whether the network buffers (IOBs) are all used up. That's the known stall from my notes; if so, it shows as zero free. If the file doesn't exist in this build, just tell me.

**2. Then press RESET**, Enter three times, and run your `ifconfig eth0 …` line. **Don't start `ai_agent` yet.** Tell me, and I'll:
- ping the board over the USB link to confirm it answers;
- leave a timestamped ping running in the background. My notes say a running ping from Windows prevents this stall, and the log will show the exact second the link drops if it happens again.

If it dies right after a `set_meal_schedule` with the ping running, the double flash write is the cause, and I'll fold the `status.md` refresh into a single write.

**For the demo,** if the final request fails after a meal was already saved, the board should say "Bob's lunch is now 12:00" instead of 请求超时. That's a small change, and I can make it next if you want.

11	**SOLVED 2026-09-01, hardware-confirmed.** VelaPaw's composite USB gadget (one physical USB-C port, GPIO19/20) now runs CDCACM (console, interfaces 0-1) + **CDC-NCM** (network, interfaces 2-3) instead of RNDIS, and both work simultaneously — proven via a real NSH shell round-trip on COM8 (`uname -a` → actual kernel banner) **and** a real bidirectional ping (`10.0.0.2` ⇄ `10.0.0.1`, 4/4, TTL=128, non-VPN-spoofed) in the same boot. Golden snapshot: VM `~/velapaw-golden/cdcncm-console-network-working/` (`nuttx.bin` md5 `dc1fbd41f6c580097b08fa696bdcf2ea`, `config.golden`, full `esp32s3-devkit` board tree, chmod a-w'd).
12	
13	**Why RNDIS was abandoned (this is NOT the same failure as [[velapaw-rndis-usb-networking]]'s Kconfig-regression story — that fix worked for a while, then this genuine limitation surfaced):** Windows Code 10 / `CM_PROB_FAILED_START` / `STATUS_UNSUCCESSFUL` when RNDIS sits at composite interface position ≠0. Extensively ruled out as a firmware bug first: `pnputil /remove-device` + fresh re-enumeration still failed (not a driver-cache issue); NuttX's `drivers/usbdev/rndis.c` `ifnobase`-based interface numbering, IAD class codes (`0xef/0x04/0x01`), and MS OS Descriptor/WCID compatible-ID mechanism (`CONFIG_COMPOSITE_MSFT_OS_DESCRIPTORS`) are all correctly implemented and position-independent. Conclusion: Windows' inbox `rndismp6.sys` hard-requires RNDIS to be interface 0 in a composite device — not fixable from the NuttX side. **CDC-NCM does not share this limitation** — it enumerates and works cleanly at interface 2.
14	
15	**The board has only one physical USB-C connector** (GPIO19/20, shared/muxed between USB-Serial/JTAG and USB-OTG — see [[velapaw-hardware]]), so "run console and network on separate USB peripherals" was never an option; they must coexist in one composite gadget.
16	
17	**Board file pattern** (`boards/xtensa/esp32s3/esp32s3-devkit/src/esp32s3_composite.c`): register CDCACM first via `cdcacm_get_composite_devdesc()` (`ifnobase=0`), then CDCNCM via `cdcncm_get_composite_devdesc()` (`ifnobase` continues after CDCACM's interface count) — both helpers internally set `classobject`/`uninitialize`, don't set those manually. `epin`/`epout` are separate counters (IN/OUT are physically distinct endpoint address spaces on this DWC2 OTG controller) — this is the correct, standard NuttX composite pattern, not a bug.
18	
19	**Kconfig recipe to reproduce:**
20	```
21	kconfig-tweak --enable NET_CDCNCM
22	kconfig-tweak --enable CDCNCM_COMPOSITE
23	kconfig-tweak --disable RNDIS_COMPOSITE
24	kconfig-tweak --disable RNDIS   # must fully disable, not just RNDIS_COMPOSITE, or rndis.c fails to compile (leftover CONFIG_RNDIS_EPINTIN etc. undeclared)
25	kconfig-tweak --set-val CDCNCM_EPINTIN_FSSIZE 16
26	kconfig-tweak --set-val CDCNCM_EPBULKOUT_FSSIZE 64
27	kconfig-tweak --set-val CDCNCM_EPBULKIN_FSSIZE 64
28	kconfig-tweak --set-val CDCNCM_QUOTA_TX 8
29	kconfig-tweak --set-val CDCNCM_QUOTA_RX 8
30	```
31	The five `--set-val` lines are required because `make olddefconfig` is permanently broken in this tree (unrelated legacy Kconfig syntax errors in tricore/zblue/quickapp/lvgl etc.) and won't auto-populate CDCNCM's sub-option defaults — pull them from `drivers/usbdev/Kconfig`'s `CDCNCM_*` block if the values ever need rechecking.
32	
33	**`CONFIG_NETINIT_THREAD` HANGS THE ENTIRE BOARD — do not enable it.** Tested directly: enabling it (to auto-apply the static `CONFIG_NETINIT_IPADDR`/`DRIPADDR` at boot instead of a manual `ifconfig`) makes the whole system unresponsive — not just USB/console, `dmesg` and even a bare `\r\n` get zero bytes back, while the USB device itself stays enumerated (`Status: OK`) the whole time. Root cause not chased further (diminishing returns once the core console+network coexistence was already proven); the workaround — one manual command after every boot — is cheap:
34	```
35	ifconfig eth0 10.0.0.2 netmask 255.255.255.0
36	```
37	matching `CONFIG_NETINIT_IPADDR=0x0a000002`/`CONFIG_NETINIT_DRIPADDR=0x0a000001`/`CONFIG_NETINIT_NETMASK=0xffffff00` already baked into `.config`. Windows side needs a matching static IP on the "VelaPaw VelaPaw Composite" adapter (`New-NetIPAddress -IPAddress 10.0.0.1 -PrefixLength 24`, **requires elevated PowerShell**) — does not persist automatically across every reboot, re-set it if pings start failing.
38

This session is being continued from a previous conversation that ran out of context. The summary below covers the earlier portion of the conversation.

Summary:
1. **Primary Request and Intent:**
   - **Current task: item 8 of the improvement list.** The user's words, verbatim: "let us start with this  Show the agent on the LCD. Right now the judges can only see the agent in a terminal. Show its last reply or heartbeat warning under the bell. Also make My Pets show a meal time the agent just changed without a reboot; I haven't confirmed it does. Then the demo becomes "watch the feeder change", not "read the terminal"."
   - **Toast part:** done and confirmed earlier ("the pop up is showing properly").
   - **fix9** (status.md refresh, tool-description rule, `ask` input sanitizer):
     - Applied on the VM, built and flashed.
     - The live LCD update of agent-changed meal times is CONFIRMED on hardware: 12:00, then 12:30, appeared on My Pets without a reboot.
   - **Current problem:** agent turns intermittently stall after "REQ written". The user's latest message: "the first one changed but the second one got stuck".
     - The diagnosis in this window shows the board's CDC-NCM USB-network TX path goes permanently silent.
   - **The user asked, verbatim:** "so it means i cant send ask two in a row". This was answered: asks queue FIFO (16 deep) and are processed one at a time.
   - **Do not redo:**
     - the mic fix (golden copy `~/velapaw-golden/mic-rxalign-working/`, md5 0a23aa25);
     - the VM backup;
     - the defense advice.
   - The other items of the 15-item list are not started; do them only if asked.
   - The user does NOT want the contest submission process or rules investigated.

2. **Key Technical Concepts:**
   - **Platform:**
     - openVela/NuttX FLAT build on ESP32-S3 (Waveshare 3.5" LCD), single-core (no CONFIG_SMP in the contest defconfig).
     - ai_agent calls velapaw via `extern`.
     - LVGL 9.1 runs on the UI thread only; `g_ident_gen` is polled by `ident_poll()`, which triggers `refresh_pets()`.
   - **status.md** (`/data/ai_agent/velapaw/status.md`, 323 B for Bob):
     - Written by the static `vp_status_write()` in store_stub.c.
     - fix9 adds `velapaw_store_status_refresh()`, called after agent meal sets, `edit_save` and `do_delete_pet`.
   - **Agent bus:**
     - FIFO ring with `AGENT_BUS_QUEUE_LEN 16` and a 5000 ms push timeout.
     - `agent_loop.c:1475` pops one message at a time with UINT32_MAX.
     - Each ask prints a placeholder `[Agent]:` followed by the real reply.
     - `quit` exits the vela CLI to nsh.
     - The LLM watchdog is 420 s.
     - `ssl_read ret=0x4c` = MBEDTLS_ERR_NET_RECV_FAILED. It arrives after about 8 min, consistent with NuttX giving up on TCP retransmission.
     - DNS failure shows as -11; `net_connect` fails with 0x52.
   - **Network:**
     - Board 192.168.137.2 (MAC 00:e0:de:ad:be:ef, board MTU 1500), gateway/ICS 192.168.137.1 on Windows "Ethernet 2" (VelaPaw Composite, CDC-NCM, UsbNcm.sys, MTU 1420).
     - The HotspotShield VPN routes 0.0.0.0/1 and 128.0.0.0/1.
     - A plain `ping 192.168.137.2` from Windows goes into the VPN. Use `ping -S 192.168.137.1 192.168.137.2`.
     - ICS is alive (SharedAccess listens on :53/:67/:68).
     - Never change host networking.
   - **CDC-NCM driver** (`nuttx/drivers/usbdev/cdcncm.c`):
     - ETHWORK = LPWORK (1 LP thread by default); CDCNCM_DGRAM_COMBINE_PERIOD 1 ms.
     - NTB_DEFAULT_IN_SIZE = NTB_OUT_SIZE = 16384; TX_MAX_NUM_DPE 32; ndpindivisor 4, remainder 0, alignment 4.
     - Single `wrreq` plus a `wrreq_idle` semaphore (init 1).
   - **ESP32-S3 OTG device driver** (`nuttx/arch/xtensa/src/esp32s3/esp32s3_otg_device.c`):
     - One 64-byte packet per XFRC interrupt.
     - A request is completed when its last packet is LOADED into the FIFO.
     - `privep->active` is cleared only when `epin_request` finds the queue empty.
     - DIEPMSK = XFRCM|EPDM|TOM, so ITTXFE is masked.
   - **Build traps:**
     - Purge velapaw objects plus `.built/.depend/Make.dep`, and all ai_agent objects.
     - Arch objects build FLAT in `arch/xtensa/src/`; you must `rm -f arch/xtensa/src/<file>.o staging/libarch.a`.
     - The image must be < 1,572,864 B.
     - Gates: `grep -ac` on the .bin and `nm` on nuttx/nuttx.
     - VM source files are CRLF.

3. **Files and Code Sections** (scratchpad = `C:\Users\VICTUS\AppData\Local\Temp\claude\c--Users-VICTUS-openVela\3659500b-38f3-47db-bbd0-9b2aab159cd9\scratchpad\`):

     - store.h declares `void velapaw_store_status_refresh(void);`
     - store_stub.c: the function calls `vp_status_write()`.
     - identity.c: `#include "store/store.h"`; the refresh is called after `velapaw_identity_save()` in `velapaw_meal_set_by_name`, before `g_ident_gen++`.
     - ui_lvgl.c: refresh in `edit_save()` and `do_delete_pet()`.
     - tool_registry.c: the `set_meal_schedule` description gains "A meal changes ONLY when this tool returns success: never tell the owner a time changed without calling it."
     - nsh_commands.c: the `cmd_ask` sanitizer handles ESC sequences, treats BS/DEL as a UTF-8 character erase, drops control bytes, and prints usage if the result is empty.

1105	/****************************************************************************
1106	 * Name: esp32s3_epin_transfer
1107	 *
1108	 * Description:
1109	 *   Start the Tx data transfer
1110	 *
1111	 ****************************************************************************/
1112	
1113	static void esp32s3_epin_transfer(struct esp32s3_ep_s *privep,
1114	                                  uint8_t *buf,
1115	                                  int nbytes)
1116	{
1117	  uint32_t pktcnt;
1118	  uint32_t regval;
1119	
1120	  /* Read the DIEPSIZx register */
1121	
1122	  regval = esp32s3_getreg(ESP32S3_OTG_DIEPTSIZ(privep->epphy));
1123	
1124	  /* Clear the XFRSIZ, PKTCNT, and MCNT field of the DIEPSIZx register */
1125	
1126	  regval &= ~(OTG_DIEPTSIZ_XFRSIZ_MASK | OTG_DIEPTSIZ_PKTCNT_MASK |
1127	              OTG_DIEPTSIZ_MCNT_MASK);
1128	
1129	  /* Are we sending a zero length packet (ZLP) */
1130	
1131	  if (nbytes == 0)
1132	    {
1133	      /* Yes.. leave the transfer size at zero and set the packet count to
1134	       * 1
1135	       */
1136	
1137	      pktcnt = 1;
1138	    }
1139	  else
1140	    {
1141	      /* No.. Program the transfer size and packet count .  First calculate:
1142	       * xfrsize = The total number of bytes to be sent. pktcnt = the number
1143	       * of packets (of maxpacket bytes) required to perform the transfer.
1144	       */
1145	
1146	      pktcnt = ((uint32_t)nbytes + (privep->ep.maxpacket - 1)) /
1147	               privep->ep.maxpacket;
1148	    }
1149	
1150	  /* Set the XFRSIZ and PKTCNT */
1151	
1152	  regval |= (pktcnt << OTG_DIEPTSIZ_PKTCNT_SHIFT);
1153	  regval |= ((uint32_t)nbytes << OTG_DIEPTSIZ_XFRSIZ_SHIFT);
1154	
1155	  /* If this is an isochronous endpoint, then set the multi-count field to
1156	   * the PKTCNT as well.
1157	   */
1158	
1159	  if (privep->eptype == USB_EP_ATTR_XFER_ISOC)
1160	    {
1161	      regval |= (pktcnt << OTG_DIEPTSIZ_MCNT_SHIFT);
1162	    }
1163	
1164	  /* Save DIEPSIZx register value */
1165	
1166	  esp32s3_putreg(regval, ESP32S3_OTG_DIEPTSIZ(privep->epphy));
1167	
1168	  /* Read the DIEPCTLx register */
1169	
1170	  regval = esp32s3_getreg(ESP32S3_OTG_DIEPCTL(privep->epphy));
1171	
1172	  /* If this is an isochronous endpoint, then set the even/odd frame bit the
1173	   * DIEPCTLx register.
1174	   */
1175	
1176	  if (privep->eptype == USB_EP_ATTR_XFER_ISOC)
1177	    {
1178	      /* Check bit 0 of the frame number of the received SOF and set the
1179	       * even/odd frame to match.
1180	       */
1181	
1182	      uint32_t status = esp32s3_getreg(ESP32S3_OTG_DSTS);
1183	      if ((status & OTG_DSTS_SOFFN0) == OTG_DSTS_SOFFN_EVEN)
1184	        {
1185	          regval |= OTG_DIEPCTL_SEVNFRM;
1186	        }
1187	      else
1188	        {
1189	          regval |= OTG_DIEPCTL_SODDFRM;
1190	        }
1191	    }
1192	
1193	  /* EP enable, IN data in FIFO */
1194	
1195	  regval &= ~OTG_DIEPCTL_EPDIS;
1196	  regval |= (OTG_DIEPCTL_CNAK | OTG_DIEPCTL_EPENA);
1197	  esp32s3_putreg(regval, ESP32S3_OTG_DIEPCTL(privep->epphy));
1198	
1199	  /* Transfer the data to the TxFIFO.  At this point, the caller has already
1200	   * assured that there is sufficient space in the TxFIFO to hold the
1201	   * transfer we can just blindly continue.
1202	   */
1203	
1204	  esp32s3_txfifo_write(privep, buf, nbytes);
1205	}

1210	 * Description:
1211	 *   Begin or continue write request processing.
1212	 *

1214	
1215	static void esp32s3_epin_request(struct esp32s3_usbdev_s *priv,
1216	                                 struct esp32s3_ep_s *privep)
1217	{
1218	  struct esp32s3_req_s *privreq;
1219	  uint32_t regaddr;
1220	  uint32_t regval;

1225	
1226	  /* We get here in one of four possible ways.  From three interrupting

1229	   * 1. From esp32s3_epin as part of the transfer complete interrupt
1230	   *    processing This interrupt indicates that the last transfer has
1231	   *    completed.
1232	   * 2. As part of the ITTXFE interrupt processing.  That interrupt
1233	   *    indicates that an IN token was received when the associated
1234	   *    TxFIFO was empty.
1235	   * 3. From esp32s3_epin_txfifoempty as part of the TXFE interrupt
1236	   *    processing.  The TXFEinterrupt is only enabled when the TxFIFO
1237	   *    is full and the software must wait for space to become available
1238	   *    in the TxFIFO.
1239	   *
1240	   * And this function may be called immediately when the write request
1241	   * is queued to start up the next transaction.
1242	   *
1243	   * 4. From esp32s3_ep_submit when a new write request is received WHILE

1245	   */

1248	
1249	  privreq = esp32s3_rqpeek(privep);
1250	  if (!privreq)
1251	    {
1252	      usbtrace(TRACE_DEVERROR(ESP32S3_TRACEERR_EPINREQEMPTY), privep->epphy);
1253	
1254	      /* There is no TX transfer in progress and no new pending TX requests
1255	       * to send.  To stop transmitting any data on a particular IN endpoint,
1256	       * the application must set the IN NAK bit. To set this bit, the
1257	       * following field must be programmed.
1258	       */

1260	      regaddr = ESP32S3_OTG_DIEPCTL(privep->epphy);
1261	      regval = esp32s3_getreg(regaddr);
1262	      regval |= OTG_DIEPCTL_SNAK;
1263	      esp32s3_putreg(regval, regaddr);
1264	
1265	      /* The endpoint is no longer active */
1266	
1267	      privep->active = false;
1268	      return;
1269	    }
1270	
1271	  uinfo("EP%d req=%p: len=%zu xfrd=%zu zlp=%d\n",
1272	        privep->epphy, privreq, privreq->req.len,
1273	        privreq->req.xfrd, privep->zlp);
1274	
1275	  /* Check for a special case: If we are just starting a request (xfrd==0)
1276	   * and the class driver is trying to send a zero-length packet (len==0).
1277	   * Then set the ZLP flag so that the packet will be sent.
1278	   */
1279	
1280	  if (privreq->req.len == 0)
1281	    {
1282	      /* The ZLP flag is set TRUE whenever we want to force the driver to
1283	       * send a zero-length-packet on the next pass through the loop (below).
1284	       * The flag is cleared whenever a packet is sent in the loop below.
1285	       */
1286	
1287	      privep->zlp = true;
1288	    }
1289	
1290	  /* Add one more packet to the TxFIFO.  We will wait for the transfer
1291	   * complete event before we add the next packet (or part of a packet to
1292	   * the TxFIFO).
1293	   * The documentation says that we can can multiple packets to the TxFIFO,
1294	   * but it seems that we need to get the transfer complete event before we
1295	   * can add the next (or maybe I have got something wrong?)
1296	   */
1297	
1298	#if 0

1300	#else

1302	#endif

1305	
1306	      bytesleft = privreq->req.len - privreq->req.xfrd;
1307	      nbytes = bytesleft;
1308	
1309	      /* Assume no zero-length-packet on the next pass through this loop */
1310	
1311	      privep->zlp = false;
1312	
1313	      /* Limit the size of the transfer to one full packet and handle
1314	       * zero-length packets (ZLPs).
1315	       */
1316	
1317	      if (nbytes > 0)
1318	        {
1319	          /* Either send the maxpacketsize or all of the remaining data in
1320	           * the request.
1321	           */
1322	
1323	          if (nbytes >= privep->ep.maxpacket)
1324	            {

1326

1328	               * maxpacketsize.  Do we need to send a zero-length packet in
1329	               * this case?
1330	               */
1331	
1332	              if (bytesleft == privep->ep.maxpacket &&
1333	                  (privreq->req.flags & USBDEV_REQFLAGS_NULLPKT) != 0)
1334	                {

1337	                   * through this loop. The flag is cleared (above) whenever
1338	                   * we are committed to sending any packet and set here when
1339	                   * we want to force one more pass through the loop.
1340	                   */

1344	            }
1345	        }

1348	
1349	      nwords = (nbytes + 3) >> 2;
1350	
1351	      /* Get the number of 32-bit words available in the TxFIFO. The DXTFSTS
1352	       * indicates the amount of free space available in the endpoint TxFIFO.
1353	       * Values are in terms of 32-bit words:
1354	       *
1355	       *   0: Endpoint TxFIFO is full
1356	       *   1: 1 word available
1357	       *   2: 2 words available
1358	       *   n: n words available

1361	      regaddr = ESP32S3_OTG_DTXFSTS(privep->epphy);

1363	      /* Check for space in the TxFIFO.  If space in the TxFIFO is not

1365	       * TxFIFO is empty.
1366	       */
1367	
1368	      regval = esp32s3_getreg(regaddr);
1369	      if ((int)(regval & OTG_DTXFSTS_MASK) < nwords)

1371	          usbtrace(TRACE_INTDECODE(ESP32S3_TRACEINTID_EPIN_EMPWAIT),
1372	                   (uint16_t)regval);
1373	
1374	          /* There is insufficient space in the TxFIFO.  Wait for a TxFIFO
1375	           * empty interrupt and try again.
1376	           */
1377	
1378	          uint32_t empmsk = esp32s3_getreg(ESP32S3_OTG_DIEPEMPMSK);
1379	          empmsk |= OTG_DIEPEMPMSK(privep->epphy);
1380	          esp32s3_putreg(empmsk, ESP32S3_OTG_DIEPEMPMSK);
1381	
1382	#ifdef CONFIG_DEBUG_FEATURES
1383	          /* Check if the configured TXFIFO size is sufficient for a given
1384	           * request. If not, raise an assertion here.
1385	           */
1386	
1387	          regval = esp32s3_getreg(ESP32S3_OTG_DIEPTXF(privep->epphy));
1388	          regval &= OTG_DIEPTXF_INEPTXFD_MASK;
1389	          regval >>= OTG_DIEPTXF_INEPTXFD_SHIFT;
1390	          uerr("EP%" PRId8 " TXLEN=%" PRId32 " nwords=%d\n",
1391	               privep->epphy, regval, nwords);

1393	#endif
1394	
1395	          /* Terminate the transfer.  We will try again when the TxFIFO empty
1396	           * interrupt is received.
1397	           */
1398	
1399	          return;
1400	        }
1401	
1402	      /* Transfer data to the TxFIFO */
1403

1406	
1407	      /* If it was not before, the OUT endpoint is now actively transferring
1408	       * data.
1409	       */
1410	
1411	      privep->active = true;
1412	
1413	      /* EP0 is a special case */
1414	
1415	      if (privep->epphy == EP0)
1416	        {
1417	          priv->ep0state = EP0STATE_DATA_IN;
1418	        }
1419	
1420	      /* Update for the next time through the loop */
1421	
1422	      privreq->req.xfrd += nbytes;
1423	    }
1424	
1425	  /* Note that the ZLP, if any, must be sent as a separate transfer.  The
1426	   * need for a ZLP is indicated by privep->zlp.  If all of the bytes were
1427	   * sent (including any final null packet) then we are finished with the

1437	       */
1438	
1439	      esp32s3_req_complete(privep, OK);

This session is being continued from a previous conversation that ran out of context. The summary below covers the earlier portion of the conversation.

Summary:
1. **Primary Request and Intent:**
   - **Current task: item 8 of the improvement list.** The user's words, verbatim: "let us start with this  Show the agent on the LCD. Right now the judges can only see the agent in a terminal. Show its last reply or heartbeat warning under the bell. Also make My Pets show a meal time the agent just changed without a reboot; I haven't confirmed it does. Then the demo becomes "watch the feeder change", not "read the terminal"."
   - **Toast part:** done and confirmed ("the pop up is showing properly").
   - **fix9** (status.md refresh, tool-description rule, `ask` input sanitizer):
     - Applied, built and flashed.
     - The live LCD update of agent-changed meal times is CONFIRMED on hardware: 12:00, then 12:30, appeared on My Pets without a reboot.
   - **Current problem:** agent turns intermittently stall after "REQ written". The user's latest message: "the first one changed but the second one got stuck".
     - The diagnosis shows the board's CDC-NCM USB-network TX path goes permanently silent.
   - **The user asked, verbatim:** "so it means i cant send ask two in a row". This was answered: asks queue FIFO (16 deep) and are processed one at a time.
   - **Do not redo:**
     - the mic fix (golden copy `~/velapaw-golden/mic-rxalign-working/`, md5 0a23aa25);
     - the VM backup;
     - the defense advice.
   - The other items of the 15-item list are not started; do them only if asked.
   - The user does NOT want the contest submission process or rules investigated.

2. **Key Technical Concepts:**
   - **Platform:**
     - openVela/NuttX FLAT build on ESP32-S3 (Waveshare 3.5" LCD), single-core (no CONFIG_SMP).
     - ai_agent calls velapaw via `extern`.
     - LVGL 9.1 runs on the UI thread only; `g_ident_gen` is polled by `ident_poll()`, which triggers `refresh_pets()`.
   - **status.md** (`/data/ai_agent/velapaw/status.md`):
     - Written by the static `vp_status_write()`.
     - fix9 adds `velapaw_store_status_refresh()`, called after agent meal sets, `edit_save` and `do_delete_pet`.
   - **Agent bus:**
     - FIFO with `AGENT_BUS_QUEUE_LEN 16` and a 5000 ms push timeout; one message at a time.
     - Each ask prints a placeholder `[Agent]:` followed by the real reply. The LLM watchdog is 420 s.
     - `ssl_read ret=0x4c` = MBEDTLS_ERR_NET_RECV_FAILED. mbedtls also maps EAGAIN from SO_RCVTIMEO on a blocking socket to 0x4c, so it does not prove a TCP retransmit timeout.
     - DNS failure shows as -11; `net_connect` fails with 0x52 (unknown host).
   - **Network:**
     - Board 192.168.137.2 (MAC 00:e0:de:ad:be:ef, MTU 1500); ICS gateway 192.168.137.1 on Windows "Ethernet 2" (VelaPaw Composite CDC-NCM, UsbNcm.sys, MTU 1420).
     - The HotspotShield VPN captures plain pings to the board, so use `ping -S 192.168.137.1 192.168.137.2`.
     - ICS is alive (SharedAccess listens on :53/:67/:68).
   - **USB composite:**
     - CONFIG_CDCACM_CONSOLE=y and NSH_USBCONSOLE=y, so the nsh console is CDC-ACM on the SAME ESP32-S3 OTG controller as CDC-NCM (VID 0x1209, PID 0x0001, "VelaPaw Composite", IAD, MSFT OS descriptors).
     - The console works during the stall, so the OTG core and interrupts are alive; only the NCM bulk-IN path is dead.
     - A USB soft-disconnect recovery would drop the PuTTY COM port, which is bad for the demo.
   - **Work queues:**
     - `ETHWORK` = LPWORK in cdcncm. TCP timers use `work_queue(LPWORK, &conn->work, tcp_timer_expiry…)` (tcp_timer.c:269); tcp_close and tcp_notifier also use LPWORK.
     - cdcncm never sets `rxtype` or `priority`. Both are 0, which gives `NETDEV_RX_WORK` on queue ID 0.
     - In wqueue.h, `HPWORK=0`, and LPWORK equals HPWORK+1 only if both SCHED_HPWORK and SCHED_LPWORK are set; otherwise LPWORK is also 0.
     - The defconfig shows only CONFIG_SCHED_LPWORK=y (LPNTHREADS default 1). Whether HPWORK is enabled is unknown; check the VM .config.
   - **CDC-NCM driver facts** (`cdcncm.c`):
     - A single `wrreq` plus semaphore `wrreq_idle` (init 1).
     - NTB_DEFAULT_IN_SIZE = NTB_OUT_SIZE = 16384; TX_MAX_NUM_DPE 32; 1 ms combine period.
     - NTB parameters: ndpin divisor 4, remainder 0, alignment 4.
     - `SET_NTB_INPUT_SIZE` is ignored (only uinfo), and `GET_NTB_INPUT_SIZE` returns 0 bytes.
     - NULLPKT/ZLP is never set on bulk IN; the NTH sequence number is always 0.
     - Datagrams are formatted into the in-flight buffer, which corrupts the NTB in flight.
     - `cdcncm_send` can call `transmit_work` directly, which blocks the caller's work queue.
     - `EP_SUBMIT` in `transmit_work` is unchecked.
     - TX quota = CONFIG_CDCNCM_QUOTA_TX; `netpkt_free` is called immediately in send.
   - **ESP32-S3 OTG driver facts:**
     - One 64 B packet per transfer (each XFRC loads the next packet).
     - A request is completed when its last packet is LOADED into the FIFO.
     - `active` is cleared only when `epin_request` finds the queue empty.
     - DIEPMSK = XFRCM|EPDM|TOM (ITTXFE masked).
     - FIFO total 1280 B; 6 endpoints; each IN TX FIFO is 106 B = 27 words, which fits one packet.
     - `ep_submit` sets `xfrd=0` and `result=-EINPROGRESS` before its critical section; -EBUSY if stalled; -EINVAL/-ESHUTDOWN only under DEBUG_FEATURES.
     - `ep_cancel` → `req_cancel(-ESHUTDOWN)` flushes the TX FIFO and completes all queued requests but does NOT clear `active`.
     - `esp32s3_epin` only continues a non-EP0 transfer if `devstate == DEVSTATE_CONFIGURED`.
     - If the FIFO lacks space, `epin_request` enables DIEPEMPMSK and returns without setting `active`.
   - **Debug config** (D: defconfig): CONFIG_DEBUG_FEATURES=y, DEBUG_NET(+ERROR/WARN)=y, DEBUG_USB=y. There is NO DEBUG_USB_ERROR and NO DEBUG_ASSERTIONS, so `uerr()` and `DEBUGASSERT` are compiled out and patch diagnostics must use `nerr()`/`syslog(LOG_ERR,…)`. Rate-limit them, because CDC-ACM console syslog can block on the 193-byte buffer.
   - **nsh `mw`/`mb`:** NSH_DISABLE_MW and NSH_DISABLE_MB default to y, and the defconfig does not override them, so register peeking from nsh is likely unavailable.
   - **OTG register map** (DR_REG_USB_BASE 0x60080000): DIEPCTL(n)=0x900+n·0x20, DIEPINT(n)=0x908+n·0x20, DIEPTSIZ(n)=0x910+n·0x20, DTXFSTS(n)=0x918+n·0x20, DIEPTXF(n)=0x104+(n-1)·4, DIEPEMPMSK=0x834. The NCM bulk-IN endpoint number has not been determined.
   - **Build traps:**
     - Purge velapaw objects plus `.built/.depend/Make.dep`, and all ai_agent objects.
     - Arch objects build FLAT in `arch/xtensa/src/`, so run `rm -f arch/xtensa/src/<file>.o staging/libarch.a`.
     - The cdcncm object location is not yet verified (have the user run `find nuttx -name 'cdcncm.o'` and purge it plus `staging/libdrivers.a`).
     - The image must be < 1,572,864 B. fix9 is 1,564,456 B, so only about 8.4 KB of headroom remains and the patch must be small.
     - Gates: `grep -ac` on the .bin and `nm` on nuttx/nuttx. VM sources are CRLF.
